In source-extended de Broglie-Bohm dynamics the conflict disappears: probability is carried by the particle ensemble, while the wavefunction guides its motion. The difficulty is then different. What does quantum equilibrium mean when the particle distribution remains normalized but the guiding density does not? We show that the departure has two independent components: a structural one, measured by the Kullback--Leibler divergence between the particle distribution and the normalized guiding density, and an amplitude one, measured by the Born weight. The Born rule holds precisely when both are equilibrated. Their evolution is governed by the complex source-to-wavefunction ratio; scale covariance further distinguishes an independently prescribed source, against which the amplitude of the wave matters, from state-dependent generators for which rescaling remains a symmetry. We develop a source-aware analytical--computational method, combining exact or semi-analytical guiding fields with Bohmian trajectory transport, ensemble quadrature and independent numerical checks. Free-space impulses expose the limits of global diagnostics and an exact jump rule; a driven ring has constant Born weight but either periodic or secular structural departure; oscillators show both source-generated structural change and amplitude-only evolution, including a finite-horizon weak-drive plateau far below its frozen-particle value; and a coupled two-body model exhibits nonlocal guidance and evolving particle entanglement. The source-free, initially equilibrated sector recovers standard quantum mechanics.
tldr: The paper develops a source-extended de Broglie-Bohm pilot-wave framework to analyze departures from quantum equilibrium via structural and amplitude nonequilibrium components.
motivation: It addresses an apparent conflict between source terms in the Schrödinger equation and probability conservation, asking what quantum equilibrium means when the guiding density is not normalized.
method: The authors separate equilibrium departure into a Kullback-Leibler structural component and a Born-weight amplitude component, then combine analytical guiding fields with Bohmian trajectory transport and numerical checks.
result: They characterize source-induced dynamics in free-space impulses, a driven ring, oscillators, and a coupled two-body model, showing cases of periodic or secular structural departure and amplitude-only evolution.
conclusion: The source-free initially equilibrated sector recovers standard quantum mechanics, while source fields induce distinct nonequilibrium behaviors in the pilot-wave system.

title: A Proof Of The Weighted B\"ottcher-Wenzel Inequality Conjectured By Mayumi, Kimura, Ohno And Chru\'sci\'nski
authors: Tomoharu Suzuki
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a positive definite matrix [MATH] with two smallest eigenvalues [MATH] and the weighted Frobenius norm [MATH], Mayumi, Kimura, Ohno and Chru\'sci\'nski conjectured that [MATH] for all complex matrices [MATH]. We prove this inequality for real and for complex matrices of every size, by a short computer-free argument, and we determine the cases of equality. In fact [MATH] for all complex matrices of compatible sizes, where [MATH] is the Ky Fan [MATH] norm (the [MATH] norm of the two largest singular values), and the constant is attained unless [MATH] and [MATH] are [MATH] matrices; the conjecture is the case [MATH]. The best constant is the square of a unitarily invariant norm of [MATH], which is convex, so it suffices to treat weights whose [MATH] largest eigenvalues coincide. For these, an inequality for one matrix and a pair of unit vectors, written in bases adapted to the pair of unit vectors, reduces the conjecture to the positive semidefiniteness of an explicit [MATH] Hermitian matrix depending on a [MATH] matrix [MATH] in a convex set defined by two weighted operator-norm bounds, and an explicit determinant identity writes its determinant as a sum of products of factors that are visibly nonnegative; the phases of the entries of [MATH] enter only through [MATH], so the real case is literally a special case. As a second theorem we prove, for every weight, a strengthening of the conjecture that is equivalent to the inequality for one matrix and all pairs of unit vectors; its best constant is again a convex function of [MATH], and the same argument applies. We also read the inequality as a sharp bound for inner derivations on the GNS space of a faithful state.
tldr: A short, computer-free proof of the weighted Böttcher–Wenzel inequality conjectured by Mayumi, Kimura, Ohno and Chruściński, together with its equality cases and a strengthening in terms of the Ky Fan 2-norm.
motivation: The conjectured inequality bounds the commutator of a matrix with a positive definite weight in a weighted Frobenius norm, generalizing the classical Böttcher–Wenzel inequality; a proof and sharp constant were previously unknown.
method: The authors reduce the problem via unitary invariance and convexity to weights with coinciding largest eigenvalues, then reduce further to an inequality for one matrix and a pair of unit vectors; positivity follows from positive semidefiniteness of an explicit 4x4 Hermitian matrix verified through a determinant identity.
result: They prove the conjectured inequality for real and complex matrices of all sizes, determine all equality cases, and obtain a stronger Ky Fan 2-norm bound whose best constant is attained except in the 2x2 case; the conjecture corresponds to the 2x2 instance.
conclusion: The result is a sharp operator-norm inequality that can be read as a bound on inner derivations on the GNS space of a faithful state, but it is a pure matrix-analysis contribution with no direct quantum-information protocol or thermodynamic consequence.

title: On A Class Of Affine Temperley-Lieb Modules
authors: Yacine Ikhlef
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the class of all affine Temperley-Lieb modules, equipped with the recently introduced "diagrammatic" tensor product, forms a quasitensor (i.e. monoidal braided) category. When the Temperley-Lieb parameter [MATH] is not a root of unity, we consider the infinite subcategory generated by the simple quotients of reducible standard modules, and we argue that it is a semi-simple ribbon category. We present some evidence that, under the fusion rules and the associativity maps, each simple module in this subcategory is equivalent to a pair of [MATH] heighest-weight modules.
tldr: The paper proves that affine Temperley-Lieb modules with a diagrammatic tensor product form a quasitensor category and, away from roots of unity, identifies a semisimple ribbon subcategory with fusion rules related to pairs of highest-weight modules.
motivation: Affine Temperley-Lieb algebras and their module categories are mathematically rich structures connected to diagrammatic algebras, fusion categories, and integrable models, motivating a systematic categorical treatment.
method: The author introduces or uses a diagrammatic tensor product on affine Temperley-Lieb modules and verifies quasitensor/monoidal braided structure, then analyzes the subcategory generated by simple quotients of reducible standard modules when the loop parameter is not a root of unity.
result: The class of affine Temperley-Lieb modules is shown to form a quasitensor category, and the relevant infinite subcategory is argued to be a semisimple ribbon category; evidence is presented that its simple modules correspond to pairs of highest-weight modules under the fusion rules and associativity maps.
conclusion: This work provides a categorical framework for affine Temperley-Lieb modules and suggests a ribbon-category structure with fusion rules resembling highest-weight module pairs, but it is primarily a mathematical algebra/category-theory result rather than a quantum information, thermodynamics, network, or hybrid-systems contribution.

title: Quantum Reversal Of Dialectics: Inversion Of Qualities And Occupation Numbers In Statistical Physics
authors: Elmira A. Isayeva
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a conceptual approach to quantum statistics called the inversion of qualities. Inspired by dialectical philosophy and the distinction between quality and quantity, the approach interprets quantum modes as qualitative characteristics and occupation numbers as quantitative measures of their realization. The paper examines the relation between occupation numbers and the statistical behavior of bosons and fermions. It discusses the role of combinatorial reasoning in describing quantum states, the harmonic oscillator, and Planck's black-body radiation formula. The mean occupation number of a bosonic mode is derived using the standard geometric-series method. The approach is compared with the Fock-space formalism and second quantization. Its conceptual scope and limitations are discussed through examples involving electromagnetic modes, phonons, and the hydrogen atom. The proposed inversion is presented as a philosophical interpretation of established quantum-statistical formalism rather than a replacement for standard quantum mechanics.
tldr: The paper offers a philosophical re-interpretation of quantum statistics, treating quantum modes as 'qualities' and occupation numbers as 'quantities', framed as an 'inversion of qualities' inspired by dialectics.
motivation: The author aims to give a conceptual, philosophically motivated reading of the standard bosonic/fermionic occupation-number formalism, motivated by the Hegelian quality/quantity distinction rather than by any open technical problem.
method: Discursive conceptual analysis: modes are identified as qualitative characteristics and occupation numbers as quantitative measures, with standard derivations (geometric series for mean bosonic occupation, combinatorial counting, Planck's law) re-narrated in this vocabulary and compared to Fock-space/second-quantization language.
result: No new technical results are derived; the mean occupation number of a bosonic mode is reproduced via the standard geometric-series method and reinterpreted conceptually, with examples from electromagnetic modes, phonons, and the hydrogen atom used to illustrate scope and limits.
conclusion: The author explicitly presents the inversion of qualities as a philosophical interpretation of established quantum-statistical formalism rather than a replacement for quantum mechanics, and acknowledges its conceptual rather than predictive character.

title: Dynamic Combinatorics Of Quantum Modes In An Inverted Fock Space
authors: E. A. Isayeva
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An inversive approach to the combinatorics of Fock space in quantum field theory is proposed. The traditional description of Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac systems is based on distributing indistinguishable quanta (particles) over energy states (modes). The present model introduces a methodological inversion: identical wave modes of a fixed frequency are declared as invariant elements (balls), while discrete occupancy numbers (Fock numbers) act as bins (spatial axes). It is shown that the time evolution of a quantum system governed by elastic interactions represents a trajectory of geometric hops of modes across occupancy axes. This approach eliminates ultraviolet divergences without introducing artificial regulators, visually differentiates thermodynamic quantum statistics, and rigorously derives Planck's entropy and the spectral characteristics of coherent laser systems.
tldr: The paper proposes an inverted combinatorial representation of Fock space in which fixed-frequency modes are treated as invariant objects and occupancy numbers as bins, claiming simplified derivation of quantum statistics and removal of ultraviolet divergences.
motivation: The author aims to reformulate the combinatorics of Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac systems by inverting the usual particles-over-modes picture, seeking a more geometric and divergence-free description of quantum field modes.
method: The approach reinterprets Fock-space combinatorics as trajectories of identical wave modes hopping across discrete occupancy axes under elastic interactions, and uses this framework to discuss quantum statistics, Planck entropy, and laser spectral properties.
result: The paper claims that this inverted Fock-space model eliminates ultraviolet divergences without artificial regulators, visually distinguishes thermodynamic quantum statistics, and derives Planck entropy and coherent-laser spectral characteristics.
conclusion: The work is a speculative combinatorial/QFT reformulation rather than a contribution to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems, so it is not aligned with the defined research priorities.

title: Machine Learning Electronic Hamiltonian With Long-Range Effects And External Fields
authors: Xueheng Kuang, Ruoyu Wang, Kwangrae Kim, Rongjing Guo, Yiyang Fu, Yuanyue Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional machine-learning electronic Hamiltonian (MLEH) models rely on a local-environment approximation and can miss the effects of long-range (LR) interactions and external fields. Here, we introduce MLEH-LR, a framework that incorporates these effects into Hamiltonian prediction. Benchmarks across materials with different polarizations and dimensionalities demonstrate substantial improvements in the accuracy of the predicted Hamiltonians and resulting electronic structures. MLEH-LR enables accurate, large-scale, high-throughput electronic-structure calculations, as demonstrated for zigzag boron nitride ribbons under transverse electric fields. These calculations allow us to formulate a quantitative relation describing the joint width and field dependence of the band gap and to reveal the electronic mechanisms underlying its field response. Our work provides an efficient method and tool for studying electronic structure in materials where long-range electrostatics and external fields play an important role.
tldr: MLEH-LR is a machine-learning framework that predicts electronic Hamiltonians while including long-range electrostatic effects and external fields, improving electronic-structure accuracy for polarized and low-dimensional materials.
motivation: Conventional machine-learning electronic-Hamiltonian models use a local-environment approximation, so they miss long-range interactions and externally applied fields, which limits accuracy for polarized or low-dimensional systems.
method: The authors extend a machine-learning Hamiltonian model with long-range and field-dependent terms, then benchmark it on materials of varying polarization and dimensionality and apply it to zigzag boron nitride ribbons under transverse electric fields.
result: The framework substantially improves the accuracy of predicted Hamiltonians and the resulting electronic structures, and yields a quantitative relation for how the band gap depends jointly on ribbon width and applied field.
conclusion: MLEH-LR enables large-scale, high-throughput electronic-structure calculations in systems where long-range electrostatics and external fields matter, though the work lies outside the quantum-information-oriented research directions.

title: JAX-Nano: A GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Phonon Boltzmann Transport Solver For Nanoscale Heat Transfer
authors: Amy Zhaomei Zhang Bo Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As semiconductor device dimensions approach phonon mean free paths, heat transport enters ballistic and quasi-ballistic regimes where Fourier's law becomes inadequate. The phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) describes these nonequilibrium effects but presents significant computational challenges. This work introduces JAX-Nano, a GPU-accelerated, end-to-end differentiable phonon BTE solver for nanoscale heat transport. The solver integrates steady-state and transient BTE formulations within a unified finite-volume framework, supporting structured and unstructured meshes, mode-resolved transport, phonon scattering, volumetric heat generation, and multiple boundary conditions. Automatic differentiation enables gradient computation with respect to transport properties, boundary conditions, heat-generation rates, and geometric parameters without separately derived adjoint equations. Numerical predictions are validated against analytical solutions and established BTE solvers across diffusive-to-ballistic regimes. Applications to complex three-dimensional geometries are demonstrated using single-fin, double-fin, and arrayed fin field-effect transistor (FinFET) configurations. Gradient-based inverse learning enables single- and multi-parameter identification, including simultaneous recovery of mode-resolved phonon relaxation times and spatially distributed heat-generation rates in steady-state and transient problems. GPU performance and scalability are evaluated with respect to spatial resolution, angular discretization, and phonon bands, including comparisons with an MPI-based BTE solver. JAX-Nano provides a unified computational framework for three-dimensional phonon transport, automatic differentiation, and inverse parameter identification, enabling sensitivity analysis and optimization of nanoscale thermal systems.
tldr: JAX-Nano is a GPU-accelerated, end-to-end differentiable finite-volume solver for the phonon Boltzmann transport equation in nanoscale heat transport, with automatic-differentiation-based inverse parameter learning.
motivation: As semiconductor devices shrink below phonon mean free paths, Fourier's law fails and the phonon BTE is needed, but solving it in 3D is computationally demanding.
method: The authors build a unified finite-volume BTE framework (steady and transient, structured/unstructured meshes, mode-resolved transport, scattering, multiple boundary conditions) in JAX, using automatic differentiation instead of hand-derived adjoint equations, validated against analytical solutions and established solvers.
result: The solver reproduces known diffusive-to-ballistic benchmarks, handles 3D FinFET geometries, and enables gradient-based recovery of mode-resolved relaxation times and spatially distributed heat-generation rates, with GPU scalability benchmarked against an MPI-based BTE solver.
conclusion: JAX-Nano offers a general differentiable computational platform for phonon transport, sensitivity analysis, and inverse thermal design in nanoscale electronics.

title: Neural Schr\"{o}dinger Bridge Via Yasue Action With Applications To Generative Modeling
authors: Yan-Han Chen, Abhishek Halder, Hailiang Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a novel neural solver for inferring the continuous state evolution of the Schr\"{o}dinger bridge problem. The proposed solver builds on a saddle point formulation involving the Yasue action functional. This allows us to realize the continuous state evolution by learning the optimal velocity for an ordinary differential equation, as opposed to learning the optimal drift for a stochastic differential equation. The proposed solver only uses the source and the target samples, and not the source and target distributions per se, which makes it particularly suitable for high dimensional applications arising in generative modeling. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solver using several numerical experiments in low and high dimensions, using both real and synthetic datasets.
tldr: The paper proposes a neural solver for the Schrödinger bridge problem using a saddle-point formulation of the Yasue action, learning an ODE velocity field for generative modeling.
motivation: Schrödinger bridge problems are challenging in high dimensions, and existing methods often learn stochastic drift terms rather than continuous deterministic evolution.
method: The authors formulate the bridge via the Yasue action functional and train a neural network to learn the optimal velocity for an ODE using only source and target samples.
result: Numerical experiments in low and high dimensions with real and synthetic datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed neural solver.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical sample-based method for continuous state evolution in Schrödinger bridge problems, with applications to generative modeling.

title: Orthosymplectic $K$-matrices In Small Dimensions
authors: Vladimir Stukopin Egor Ryzhkin
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using elementary methods, we describe coideal subalgebras of quantum orthosymplectic algebras of small dimensions, classify the corresponding [MATH]-matrices and find explicitly the centralizers of these subalgebras in the vector representation. The main attention is paid to generators with a Cartan term. For them, at generic values of the parameters, we find the centralizers and all [MATH]-matrices and describe the decomposition of the vector representation over the coideal subalgebra. We find all special values of the parameters of two types and, at a generic point of each set of special values, describe the decomposition of the vector representation and all [MATH]-matrices. At special values of the first type the dimension of the centralizer grows. One hypersurface of such values is related to Cartan terms, and on it one of the generators is given by the same formula as in the quantum electrical algebra. At special values of the second type the dimension of the centralizer is the same, but nonzero nilpotent elements appear in it. The [MATH]-matrices on the sets of special values of the second type are obtained from those already found by substituting the condition, and there are no others. We describe the classical limit, including the limit of special values. We formulate an observation relating the admissibility of a Cartan term to the first homology of the classical subalgebra.
tldr: A purely algebraic study classifying coideal subalgebras and K-matrices of quantum orthosymplectic algebras in small dimensions.
motivation: K-matrices and coideal subalgebras underlie integrable boundary systems and reflection equations, and a systematic low-dimensional classification with explicit centralizers is desired.
method: Elementary algebraic methods are used to construct generators with Cartan terms, compute centralizers in the vector representation, and identify special parameter values of two types, followed by a classical limit analysis.
result: All K-matrices are found at generic parameters and at both types of special values; at type-one values the centralizer dimension grows (one hypersurface linked to quantum electrical algebra generators), while at type-two values nilpotent elements appear without dimension growth.
conclusion: The classification is complete for the small-dimensional orthosymplectic cases, and an observation connects admissibility of a Cartan term with the first homology of the classical subalgebra.

title: Observation Of Collective Flatbands In Hybrid Mie-grating THz Metasurfaces
authors: Jie Ji, Thanh Xuan Hoang, Ayan Nussupbekov, Siyan Zhou, Kehan Wang, Yuri Kivshar, Jaime G\'omez Rivas
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a novel type of functional metasurfaces created by a hybridization of Mie resonators with high-index optical gratings. We demonstrate that such hybrid metasurfaces possess flatbands characterized by zero group velocity and strong energy localization. We experimentally observe the flatbands in free-standing terahertz (THz) metasurfaces, where dielectric interconnections between Mie resonators, forming the grating, mediate multipolar hybridization and provide a geometric control over collective resonances. Our THz near-field measurements with a dipole excitation uncover long-lived coherent oscillations associated with the quasi-flat magnetic-dipolar resonant modes, while a spatial mapping resolves the resonant electromagnetic response across the dielectric interconnections. We vary the grating width continuously to tune the hybrid magnetic-dipolar resonances and substantially enhance the quality factor (Q factor), while preserving the quasi-!atband dispersion. Complementary Bloch-resolved Purcell calculations reveal the substantial Purcell enhancement with increasing Q factor, followed by a trend towards saturation and highlighting the interplay between radiative confinement and local emitter-mode coupling. We believe our findings establish the engineering of dielectric interconnections in periodic lattices as a novel strategy for spectrally tuning high-Q flatbands in these metastructures, tailoring localized electromagnetic interactions in functional optical metasurfaces.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates collective flatbands in hybrid Mie-grating terahertz metasurfaces formed by dielectric interconnections between Mie resonators.
motivation: The authors aim to create functional metasurfaces with high-Q flatband resonances and strong energy localization by hybridizing Mie resonators with high-index gratings.
method: Free-standing THz metasurfaces are fabricated and characterized via near-field measurements with dipole excitation, complemented by Bloch-resolved Purcell calculations and continuous tuning of the grating width.
result: Long-lived coherent oscillations and quasi-flat magnetic-dipolar resonant modes are observed, with enhanced Q factors and substantial Purcell enhancement that saturates at higher Q.
conclusion: Engineering dielectric interconnections in periodic lattices provides a strategy for spectrally tuning high-Q flatbands and tailoring localized electromagnetic interactions in optical metasurfaces.

title: Integrable Orbital Exchange Between Ellipsoidally Deformed $p$, $d$, And $f$ Electron States: Two-Angle Sklyanin Representations And Fused Elliptic $R$-Matrices
authors: Vladimir Mikhalev
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct integrable orbital exchange models from ellipsoidally deformed [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH] multiplets. A two-angle realization of the Sklyanin algebra gives explicit Jacobi difference operators [MATH], complete distortion spectra and eigenfunctions, and a positive inner product transported from Sklyanin's integral. In the [MATH] sector the coordinate functions carry an exact spin-one action, and applying [MATH] componentwise maps the confocal ellipsoid to a sphere. Elliptic fusion gives explicit [MATH]-matrices in the angular generators on both factors. Their Yang--Baxter relations yield commuting charges and exchange Hamiltonians for homogeneous and alternating chains, as well as mixed-pair interactions that can act between angular degrees of freedom on the same center. Exchange changes angular projections and correlations while preserving the two local Casimirs of each constituent, which fix its angular-momentum-squared and distortion-plus-rotation kinetic-energy invariants. The [MATH]--[MATH] model recovers Fateev's elliptic spin-one interaction and reduces to the Takhtajan--Babujian Hamiltonian in the rational isotropic limit.
tldr: The paper constructs integrable orbital exchange models from ellipsoidally deformed p, d, and f electron multiplets using two-angle Sklyanin representations and fused elliptic R-matrices.
motivation: The work aims to generalize integrable spin-exchange models to orbital degrees of freedom with deformed angular multiplets and elliptic fusion structures.
method: It develops a two-angle realization of the Sklyanin algebra with Jacobi difference operators, derives distortion spectra and eigenfunctions, and uses elliptic fusion to obtain R-matrices satisfying Yang-Baxter relations.
result: The construction yields commuting charges and exchange Hamiltonians for homogeneous and alternating chains, recovers Fateev's elliptic spin-one interaction in the p-d sector, and reduces to the Takhtajan-Babujian Hamiltonian in the rational isotropic limit.
conclusion: The paper provides a mathematical framework for integrable orbital exchange with deformed p, d, and f states, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Cryogenic Luminescence Thermometry Of Upconversion Micro- And Nanoparticles Via Deep Learning
authors: Pablo Jos\'e Coria Ledo, Lina W\"olcken, Lucas R. Mendicino, Santiago Gliosca, M. Claudia Marchi, Marcos Illescas, Beatriz Barja, Christian Tom\'as Schmiegelow
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Luminescence thermometry with single or optically trapped particles is hampered by weak signals that fluctuate with alignment, collection efficiency, and excitation conditions and, for [MATH]-based probes, by the loss of sensitivity of the luminescence intensity ratio (LIR) at cryogenic temperatures. Here we use a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) to predict the temperature directly from single emission spectra of [MATH] micro- and nanoparticles between [MATH] and [MATH], and compare it with the standard LIR under adverse conditions deliberately reproduced with particle ensembles. From [MATH] to [MATH], the 1D-CNN reduces the single-spectrum mean absolute error from [MATH] to [MATH] and keeps its temperature uncertainty nearly constant down to the lowest temperatures, where Stark-component features remain temperature dependent while the LIR loses its sensitivity. Under deliberate optical misalignment, its error increases only from [MATH] to [MATH], whereas that of the LIR rises from [MATH] to [MATH]. The same approach reaches sub-degree accuracy ([MATH]) over a narrow temperature window and a single calibration valid across different pump powers and wavelengths. These results establish 1D-CNNs as robust single-shot thermometers and a step toward fast thermometry of single and trapped particles.
tldr: The paper uses a 1D convolutional neural network to improve cryogenic luminescence thermometry of upconversion micro- and nanoparticles from single emission spectra.
motivation: Single-particle luminescence thermometry suffers from weak, fluctuating signals and reduced sensitivity of the standard luminescence intensity ratio at cryogenic temperatures.
method: A one-dimensional CNN is trained to predict temperature directly from single emission spectra of upconversion particles between cryogenic temperatures, and is compared with the conventional LIR method under misalignment and varying excitation conditions.
result: The 1D-CNN reduces mean absolute error and maintains nearly constant temperature uncertainty at low temperatures, while also proving more robust to optical misalignment than the LIR approach.
conclusion: The authors establish 1D-CNNs as robust single-shot thermometers and a step toward fast thermometry of single and trapped particles.

title: Comment On Phase Vortex Lattices In Neutron Interferometry
authors: Wolfgang Treimer, Terrence Jach, Martin Suda, Frank Hau{\ss}er
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a phase-based theoretical description of the four-plate crystal neutron interferometer (LLLL geometry) originally introduced by Heinrich et al. [Z. Phys. B 72, 357 (1988)]. The LLLL interferometer can be interpreted as two coupled LLL interferometric loops that share partial beam paths, leading to characteristic interference phenomena beyond the standard three-plate configuration. Using a coherent beam-splitting model we derive the forward intensity in terms of loop phase sums and recover the cosine-sum structure reported in Refs.[1,2]. Based on these results we analyze the phase dependence of the forward beam in the presence of localized phase objects, such as wedges inserted into individual partial beams. In experiments presented in [2], the LLLL interferometer is used to generate a periodic array of intensity in two dimensions by which the authors claim to demonstrate a phase vortex grating of significant extrinsic orbital angular momentum (OAM). However, the same interference patterns are predicted by simulating a coherent superposition of {beam paths} along different interferometer loops and experiencing phase shifts in each loop due to two wedges that are perpendicular to each other, without assuming any neutron OAM.
tldr: This comment argues that observed interference patterns in a four-plate neutron interferometer can be explained by coherent loop-phase superpositions without invoking neutron orbital angular momentum.
motivation: The authors revisit claims that an LLLL neutron interferometer demonstrates a phase vortex grating with significant extrinsic orbital angular momentum, and they aim to provide a phase-based alternative explanation.
method: They model the four-plate crystal neutron interferometer as two coupled LLL interferometric loops and derive the forward intensity from loop phase sums and localized phase shifts induced by perpendicular wedges.
result: The model reproduces the cosine-sum interference structure and predicts the same periodic two-dimensional intensity patterns without assuming any neutron OAM.
conclusion: The reported phase vortex lattice signatures in neutron interferometry may be fully accounted for by standard coherent beam-path interference, so the OAM interpretation is not required.

title: Effective Hamiltonians And Asymptotic Band Coupling
authors: Guillaume Bal, Paul Cazeaux, Daniel Massatt, Solomon Quinn
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By a multiple-scale asymptotic expansion, we derive effective macroscopic models for a large class of tight-binding Schr\"odinger equations with slow spatial variations. For wave packets that are spectrally localized to some point [MATH] in the unperturbed tight-binding dispersion relation, our effective models produce long-time approximations of the tight-binding dynamics, accurate to any prescribed order in the asymptotic parameter. Our framework allows the point [MATH] to be degenerate, meaning that multiple (but not necessarily all) energy bands of the tight-binding Hamiltonian can attain the value [MATH] at the frequency [MATH]. We construct an effective Hamiltonian on the relevant degenerate subspace, which quantifies the coupling between the degenerate and other bands. Several applications and numerical simulations illustrate the theory.
tldr: The paper develops multiple-scale asymptotic effective Hamiltonians for slowly varying tight-binding Schrödinger equations, including degenerate spectral points and interband coupling.
motivation: It aims to provide long-time macroscopic approximations for tight-binding quantum dynamics with slow spatial variations, extending effective-mass theory to degenerate bands and asymptotic band coupling.
method: The authors use a multiple-scale asymptotic expansion to construct effective Hamiltonians on degenerate subspaces and quantify coupling to non-degenerate bands, with numerical simulations illustrating the theory.
result: The framework yields effective models that approximate tight-binding dynamics to arbitrary prescribed order in the asymptotic parameter, including cases where multiple bands meet at a spectral point.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous asymptotic homogenization method for tight-binding models with band degeneracies, but it is a mathematical condensed-matter/numerical analysis paper rather than a quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems contribution.

title: Feshbach Resonances Of The Second Order In A Friedrichs Model
authors: Alexander K. Motovilov Dmitry S. Grudko
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider an extended version of the matrix Friedrichs model that may produce Feshbach resonances of the second order. In this model, under enlarging of the coupling constant, a pair of eigenvalues of the unperturbed Hamiltonian embedded into the continuous spectrum first transforms in resonances of the first order. At some moment later on, these two resonances merge into a single resonance but of the second order, and we fix conditions for this event. Being based on the operator interpretation of resonances, we found that, in the case under consideration, the operator roots of the transfer function have a very particular structure.
tldr: The paper studies an extended matrix Friedrichs model in which embedded eigenvalues turn into first-order resonances and then merge into a second-order Feshbach resonance as the coupling increases.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize the emergence and merging of higher-order Feshbach resonances in a solvable operator-theoretic model.
method: They use the operator interpretation of resonances and analyze the transfer function's operator roots in the extended Friedrichs model.
result: They identify conditions under which two first-order resonances merge into a single second-order resonance and show that the operator roots of the transfer function have a special structure.
conclusion: The work provides a mathematical description of second-order Feshbach resonances, but it is unrelated to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Large Deviations And Critical Scaling In The Finite-Population Granovetter Threshold Model
authors: Jos\'e F. Fontanari
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a systematic asymptotic analysis of the exact finite-population solution of Granovetter's threshold model, in which a single initial instigator triggers a cascade among agents with independently distributed adoption thresholds. By expressing the propagation probability as an order-statistic boundary-crossing event, we formulate its macroscopic large-deviation rate as a constrained relative-entropy minimization problem. For Beta-distributed thresholds, we obtain explicit solutions for all shape parameters [MATH] and [MATH], identifying four possible optimal empirical threshold profiles: fully free, fully pinned, pinned--free, and free--pinned. These profiles determine both the exponential probability of macroscopic cascades and the threshold configurations responsible for their occurrence. Importance-sampling estimates confirm the analytical rate functions, while sequential Monte Carlo simulations independently reproduce the predicted optimal profiles. We also revisit the critical scaling near [MATH] and confirm the principal finite-size scaling laws: the mean active fraction decays as [MATH] for uniform thresholds and as [MATH] for [MATH] and [MATH]. In the latter regime, we further derive an explicit scaling function for the logarithmic critical window from the microscopic branching-process limit. Our results provide a general framework for determining the probabilities and characteristic configurations of rare collective events in threshold-driven cascade processes.
tldr: The paper analyzes finite-population Granovetter threshold cascades using large-deviation rate functions and critical scaling near the cascade threshold.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize rare macroscopic cascade events and finite-size scaling in a classic threshold model of collective behavior.
method: They express cascade probability as an order-statistic boundary-crossing event and derive a large-deviation rate via constrained relative-entropy minimization, supported by importance sampling and sequential Monte Carlo.
result: For Beta-distributed thresholds they obtain explicit optimal threshold profiles and confirm finite-size scaling laws, including an explicit scaling function for the logarithmic critical window.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework for probabilities and characteristic configurations of rare collective events in threshold-driven cascade processes.

title: Multiscale Wave-coupled Neural Networks For The Inverse-design Of Broadband Diffractive Optics
authors: Peyton Brown, Riccardo Franchi, Roberto Riganti, Jonathan Schuster, Luca Dal Negro
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we introduce an inverse-design model called multiscale wave-coupled neural networks (MSWNets) inspired by physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) that integrate the deep-learning capability of fully-connected neural networks with rigorous Rayleigh-Sommerfeld diffraction theory. MSWNets are trained using spatial input and output functions describing the height profiles of diffractive structures. Importantly, a MSWNet is composed of multiple sub-networks that provide learning across multiple frequency components of the optimal design solution. First, we validate and analyze the inverse design capabilities of the MSWNets' architecture through training on the complete complex field propagated from the analytical design of an axilens, demonstrating accurate reconstruction. Finally, we employ MSWNets, trained to maximize focusing efficiency, for the inverse design of novel diffractive devices. In particular, we design and display the performance of several achromatic lenses and doublets across the mid-wave infrared region ([MATH]) with focal distance [MATH], demonstrating the potential of our inverse-design framework for the next-generation of broadband diffractive optical devices.
tldr: The paper introduces multiscale wave-coupled neural networks for inverse-designing broadband diffractive optical elements such as achromatic lenses and doublets.
motivation: Inverse design of broadband diffractive optics is challenging due to the need to optimize complex height profiles across multiple wavelengths and frequency components.
method: MSWNets combine fully connected neural networks with Rayleigh-Sommerfeld diffraction theory and use multiple sub-networks to learn across frequency components of the optimal design.
result: The authors validate the architecture by reconstructing an analytically designed axilens and then use it to design achromatic lenses and doublets in the mid-wave infrared with improved focusing efficiency.
conclusion: The proposed framework shows potential for inverse-designing next-generation broadband diffractive optical devices, but it is a classical optics and machine-learning contribution rather than a quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems result.

title: Lusin And pseudo-Lusin Theorems For Monotone Measures: Necessary Conditions, Conjugate Duality And A Correction Of A Theorem Of Castaldo And Marinacci
authors: Duc Toan Truong, Kiet Ho, Thanh Ngo Vo Ke, Cuong Le Quoc, Tran Nhat Luan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lusin's theorem for monotone measures has been studied mainly through sufficient conditions. Here we study it from the side of necessary conditions and of conjugate duality. We show that, for an arbitrary monotone measure on a metric space, the Lusin property with closed sets implies regularity, and the Lusin property with compact sets implies order continuity and tightness. Consequently, for finite submeasures the Lusin property is characterized by order continuity on compact spaces, and the compact-set Lusin property is characterized by order continuity on Polish spaces. We then consider a pseudo-Lusin property, in which the Lusin set is required to have almost full measure, and observe that it is exactly the Lusin property of the conjugate measure. For finite monotone measures whose conjugate is subadditive, a class including supermodular capacities, belief functions and coherent lower probabilities, the pseudo-Lusin property is equivalent to continuity from below on compact spaces, and so is its compact-set version on Polish spaces. As an application, we give a corrected form, together with its converse, of a Lusin-type theorem of Castaldo and Marinacci whose original statement was refuted by Wiesel. Several examples, one of them based on meagre sets, show that the hypotheses cannot be omitted.
tldr: The paper characterizes necessary conditions for Lusin-type approximation theorems for monotone measures, introduces a pseudo-Lusin property via conjugate duality, and corrects a theorem of Castaldo and Marinacci.
motivation: Lusin's theorem for monotone measures has been studied mostly through sufficient conditions; the authors aim to establish necessary conditions and a duality-based characterization, and to repair a flawed result in the literature.
method: Pure measure-theoretic analysis on metric and Polish spaces: relating closed-set and compact-set Lusin properties to regularity, order continuity and tightness, and analyzing the pseudo-Lusin property as the Lusin property of the conjugate measure, with counterexamples based on meagre sets.
result: The Lusin property with closed sets implies regularity, the compact-set version implies order continuity and tightness, and for finite submeasures the properties are characterized by order continuity on compact (resp. Polish) spaces; for subadditive conjugates (supermodular capacities, belief functions, coherent lower probabilities) pseudo-Lusin is equivalent to continuity from below.
conclusion: The work gives a corrected, converse-included version of the Castaldo–Marinacci Lusin-type theorem and shows via examples that the hypotheses cannot be dropped.

title: A Matrix-Valued Quotient And A Compatible Bilinear Product On Euclidean Vector Spaces
authors: J. Enrique H. Ramirez
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a matrix-valued quotient and a compatible bilinear product on finite-dimensional Euclidean vector spaces. The quotient is constructed from a bilinear matrix-valued map satisfying a prescribed vector transport identity. We investigate its algebraic structure and establish uniqueness results under orthogonal equivariance and additional structural conditions. We also derive a variational characterization based on the Frobenius norm and examine the spectral properties of the associated matrices, including their determinants and invertibility conditions. The two-dimensional construction is related to complex arithmetic, while the three-dimensional formulation admits a representation using skew-symmetric matrices. The results clarify the relationship between vector transport, matrix algebra, and Euclidean geometry, and extend the framework introduced in our earlier work on vector division and multiplication.
tldr: The paper introduces a matrix-valued quotient and compatible bilinear product on finite-dimensional Euclidean vector spaces, with uniqueness and spectral results.
motivation: The work aims to clarify algebraic relationships between vector transport, matrix algebra, and Euclidean geometry, extending earlier constructions of vector division and multiplication.
method: It constructs a bilinear matrix-valued map satisfying a vector transport identity, analyzes algebraic structure under orthogonal equivariance, and derives variational and spectral characterizations.
result: Uniqueness conditions are established, a Frobenius-norm variational characterization is derived, and determinant/invertibility properties are examined; low-dimensional cases connect to complex arithmetic and skew-symmetric matrices.
conclusion: The framework generalizes vector division/multiplication in Euclidean spaces, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Sub-Riemannian Flow Matching
authors: Scott Zimmerman Wonjun Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study sub-Riemannian conditional flow matching (SRCFM) for generative transport with prescribed velocity constraints. Training uses paths between sampled source and target points whose velocities lie in the allowed horizontal directions at each state. A neural network takes time and the full state as input and predicts the coefficients of these directions, and the horizontal frame then determines the full velocity used for generation. We describe constructions based on Heisenberg geodesics and joint endpoint equations in free step-two Carnot groups. We propose a scalable piecewise algorithm that computes horizontal paths directly from their endpoints. A straight segment sets the horizontal coordinates, and a loop in those coordinates corrects the remaining vertical displacement. We verify the algorithm's endpoint accuracy to numerical precision in high-dimensional tests. Synthetic experiments illustrate approximate distribution transport along horizontal trajectories. On resized MNIST, we use the same construction to generate images from Gaussian inputs with fewer controls than pixels.
tldr: The paper develops sub-Riemannian conditional flow matching, a generative transport method whose trajectories are constrained to horizontal (allowed) directions at every state, with constructions based on Heisenberg geodesics and free step-two Carnot groups.
motivation: Standard flow matching assumes unconstrained velocities in the full tangent space; the authors want generative transport that respects prescribed non-holonomic velocity constraints, a setting naturally formalized in sub-Riemannian geometry.
method: Training pairs sampled source and target points along horizontal paths, and a neural network predicting the coefficients of the horizontal frame from time and full state. They build endpoint-to-path constructions from Heisenberg geodesics and a scalable piecewise algorithm that sets horizontal coordinates by a straight segment and corrects vertical displacement with a loop.
result: The algorithm reaches endpoint accuracy at numerical precision in high-dimensional tests, synthetic experiments show approximate distribution transport along horizontal trajectories, and on resized MNIST it generates images from Gaussian inputs using fewer controls than pixels.
conclusion: Sub-Riemannian flow matching offers a practical, scalable framework for constrained generative transport, suggesting geometric control ideas can be exploited in generative modeling.

title: A $C_2$-cofinite Non-rational Principal $W$-algebra Of Type $d_4$
authors: Ivana Vukorepa Dra\v{z}en Adamovi\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a simple principal [MATH]-algebra can be [MATH]-cofinite and non-rational. For [MATH] of central charge [MATH], D. Xie predicted seventeen irreducible modules and a logarithmic module of lowest conformal weight [MATH]. We determine the Zhu algebra [MATH] and the Poisson algebra [MATH]. Both have dimension [MATH], and [MATH]. We construct all seventeen irreducible [MATH]-modules using the realization of [MATH] as a diagonal coset in [MATH] and our previous classification of irreducible [MATH]-modules in the category [MATH]. We also construct an indecomposable [MATH]-module and use the coset realization to obtain an indecomposable logarithmic [MATH]-module. Its lowest generalized [MATH]-eigenspace is two-dimensional, and [MATH] acts on this space by a nontrivial Jordan block with eigenvalue [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves that a simple principal W-algebra of type d4 at a specific central charge is C2-cofinite but non-rational, and constructs its seventeen irreducible modules plus an indecomposable logarithmic module.
motivation: The work addresses the structure and module theory of principal W-algebras, testing the boundary between C2-cofiniteness and rationality and verifying a prediction by D. Xie.
method: The authors determine the Zhu and Poisson algebras, use a diagonal coset realization of the W-algebra, and apply a previous classification of irreducible modules in a category to construct all irreducible modules.
result: They find seventeen irreducible modules and construct an indecomposable logarithmic module whose lowest generalized eigenspace is two-dimensional with a nontrivial Jordan block action.
conclusion: This establishes a counterexample to the expectation that C2-cofiniteness implies rationality for principal W-algebras of type d4 and provides explicit logarithmic module structure.

title: Quantitative Convergence Of The Spherical Brownian Motion Collisional Particle System For The Maxwellian Landau Equation
authors: Jos\'e Antonio Carrillo, Ruizhi Huang, Lei Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish the quantitative convergence of the spherical Brownian motion (SBM) collisional particle system for the Maxwellian Landau equation via Wasserstein distances. When used as numerical method, it enjoys linear complexity [MATH] in particle number [MATH], and conserves the momentum and energy almost surely. Moreover, only random grouping and sampling are needed for simulations without further numerical discretization. In the first part, we identify the large particle mean field limit of the system, and the Wasserstein convergence to the limit is justified through a coupling similar to the recent work for the Nanbu type Monte Carlo method . The key difference is that the particles in our coupled shadow system are not i.i.d. due to the perfect matching. In the second part, the convergence of the mean field dynamics to the Landau solution is justified by the relative entropy with a bound [MATH], being [MATH] the stepsize. This results in an [MATH] bound for the Wasserstein distance error. A crucial technical tool in the convergence in relative entropy is to provide suitable bounds on the derivatives of the logarithmic density or score function in the mean field dynamics. The combination of these estimates leads to the full convergence of the squared Wasserstein distance with order [MATH] for the numerical scheme in [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves quantitative convergence of a spherical Brownian motion particle system to the Maxwellian Landau equation using Wasserstein and relative-entropy estimates.
motivation: The authors aim to justify a linearly complex stochastic particle method that conserves momentum and energy for numerically solving the Maxwellian Landau equation.
method: They establish a mean-field limit via coupling arguments for non-i.i.d. matched particles, then prove convergence of the mean-field dynamics to the Landau solution using relative entropy and bounds on score-function derivatives.
result: They obtain an explicit Wasserstein error bound for the scheme, combining mean-field and mean-field-to-PDE convergence estimates.
conclusion: The method provides a rigorously justified, discretization-free stochastic simulation approach for the Maxwellian Landau equation with quantitative convergence guarantees.

title: Worst Case Tractability Of Weighted Linear Tensor Product Problems Under The Absolute Error Criterion
authors: Yuheng Xi Heping Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies weighted linear tensor product problems in the worst case setting. We consider algorithms that use finitely many evaluations of arbitrary continuous linear functionals. We investigate algebraic and exponential tractability under the absolute error criterion in the case [MATH], where [MATH] is the square of the univariate maximal singular value. We obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for various notions of algebraic and exponential tractability on weights and univariate singular values. Our approach is to convert algebraic tractability of the problems for the absolute error criterion with [MATH] to exponential tractability of the normalized problems. Specifically, we solve Open Problem 27 as posed by Novak and Wo\'zniakowski (2008).
tldr: The paper settles Open Problem 27 of Novak and Woźniakowski by giving necessary and sufficient conditions on weights and univariate singular values for algebraic and exponential tractability of weighted linear tensor product problems under the absolute error criterion.
motivation: Tractability of multivariate tensor product problems in the worst case setting is a central question in information-based complexity, and the absolute error criterion with the restriction on the squared univariate maximal singular value had remained open.
method: The authors analyse algorithms using finitely many evaluations of arbitrary continuous linear functionals and reduce the algebraic tractability question for the absolute error criterion to exponential tractability of suitably normalized problems.
result: Complete necessary and sufficient conditions on weights and univariate singular values are derived for various notions of algebraic and exponential tractability, resolving Open Problem 27.
conclusion: The reduction technique yields a full characterisation of tractability for this class of weighted tensor product problems and closes a long-standing open question in the classical complexity literature.

title: Understanding Membership Inference Attacks On Eeg Models
authors: Mehrdad Khodapanahandeh, Selin Unal, Berkay Kemal Balioglu, Alireza Khodaie, Beren Semiz, M. Emre Gursoy
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) signals contain sensitive, subject-specific information, making models trained on them potential targets for membership inference attacks (MIAs). Although MIAs have been studied extensively in other domains, their applications to EEG models are relatively scarce, and the factors driving the vulnerability of EEG models to MIAs are not adequately understood. In this paper, we present a systematic empirical analysis of MIAs on EEG models using three datasets, seven model architectures, four attack methods, and two metrics. Results show that poor model generalization (large train-test loss and accuracy gap) is the strongest indicator of MIA vulnerability. Longer training and larger models also increase vulnerability. Moreover, no particular scalp region, frequency band, inter-channel correlation pattern, or temporal versus spectral representation of EEG data consistently explains MIA vulnerability across datasets. Finally, subject identification and leave-one-subject-out experiments indicate that models relying more heavily on subject-specific representations are more vulnerable to MIAs. Overall, our findings identify the key drivers of membership leakage in EEG models and can provide guidance for developing MIA-resilient EEG systems.
tldr: A systematic empirical study of membership inference attacks on EEG-based models, identifying model generalization, training length, model size, and subject-specific representations as key drivers of privacy leakage.
motivation: EEG signals contain sensitive subject-specific information, so models trained on them may leak membership information, yet MIA vulnerability in EEG models is underexplored.
method: The authors evaluate MIAs across three EEG datasets, seven model architectures, four attack methods, and two metrics, including subject identification and leave-one-subject-out analyses.
result: Poor generalization is the strongest indicator of MIA vulnerability; longer training and larger models also increase vulnerability, while no scalp region, frequency band, inter-channel correlation pattern, or temporal/spectral representation consistently explains vulnerability across datasets.
conclusion: The findings identify key drivers of membership leakage in EEG models and provide guidance for developing MIA-resilient EEG systems.

title: Rateless Lattices: Constructions, Coding Theorems, And Capacity
authors: Pegah Sharifi, Hassan Khodaiemehr, Khadijeh Bagheri, Chen Feng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.29169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A rateless code sends a fixed message as an unbounded stream of symbols such that every prefix is a codeword. We introduce rateless lattices, sequences of integral lattices of increasing dimension in which each lattice projects onto the first coordinates of the next while the induced finite codebooks retain constant size. Our first contribution is a family obtained from Construction D' with two nested Raptor codes. We derive generator matrices, volume, and an encoder. For every noise or fading sequence unknown to the transmitter and independent of the code randomness, we prove an ensemble random-coding bound for multistage decoding. These results quantify the loss created by a fixed split of information between two levels, and the bound remains valid for sparse LT stages of logarithmic degree. They concern recovery of the message, or finite-codeword residue; lattice-point recovery with a fixed alphabet incurs an additional coarse-lattice error term. We then show that the split loss is caused by stage-by-stage decoding. For a dense ensemble with ring coefficients, we characterize the rateless capacity region under joint decoding. With equal level sizes, the ensemble achieves the accumulated capacity of uniform pulse-amplitude modulation for two levels and for additional levels. Single-level [MATH]-ary rateless lattices achieve the same performance, satisfy a finite-parameter rateless Poltyrev inequality, and, with geometric shaping, approach within any [MATH] of the Gaussian incremental-redundancy capacity for bounded SNR. Repetition of a fixed-dimension lattice codeword instead incurs a loss that grows unboundedly with retransmissions. We also analyze a joint belief-propagation decoder over [MATH] using density evolution on a tree-like surrogate ensemble. Simulations on AWGN and block-fading channels show that joint decoding removes most of the multistage-decoding loss.
tldr: The paper introduces rateless lattices constructed from nested Raptor codes and analyzes their coding theorems and capacity under multistage and joint decoding.
motivation: Rateless codes provide unbounded symbol streams with every prefix decodable, but lattice-based rateless constructions and their fundamental limits are less developed.
method: The authors construct rateless lattices using Construction D' with nested Raptor codes, derive generator matrices and volume, prove ensemble random-coding bounds for multistage decoding, and analyze joint belief-propagation decoding via density evolution.
result: They characterize the rateless capacity region under joint decoding, show that multistage decoding causes split loss, and demonstrate that single-level M-ary rateless lattices can approach Gaussian incremental-redundancy capacity with geometric shaping.
conclusion: Joint decoding removes most of the multistage-decoding loss, while simple repetition of fixed-dimension lattice codewords suffers unbounded loss with retransmissions.

title: A Simple Counterexample To The Hohenberg-Kohn Theorem For Excited States
authors: Dominic Shillingford
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an even number of non-interacting fermions on the one-dimensional unit torus, a semi-explicit counterexample to the Hohenberg--Kohn theorem for excited states is exhibited. Indeed, for each [MATH], it is shown that there exist constants [MATH] and [MATH] such that an [MATH]-body system with the rescaled Lam\'e potential [MATH] has a simple first excited energy and a first excited-state particle density which is constant on the torus. By translating this potential, we exhibit a non-trivial one-parameter family of potentials, all of which have a constant first excited-state density. As such, the potential-to-density map is not one-to-one in this setting. Under a spectral nonresonance assumption, we obtain the same nonuniqueness at a simple excited energy for odd [MATH]. We also explore connections to the classification problem of elastica in the plane when [MATH], and outline some related questions of interest.
tldr: The paper constructs a semi-explicit counterexample to the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem for excited states using non-interacting fermions on a one-dimensional torus.
motivation: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem underpins density functional theory, but its extension to excited states is less secure; the author tests whether the potential-to-density map remains one-to-one for excited states.
method: For even numbers of non-interacting fermions on the unit torus, the author uses a rescaled Lamé potential to produce a simple first excited energy with constant first excited-state particle density, and translates the potential to obtain a one-parameter family.
result: A non-trivial family of potentials is shown to yield the same constant first excited-state density, proving non-uniqueness of the potential-to-density map in this setting; related results are obtained for odd particle number under a spectral nonresonance assumption.
conclusion: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem for excited states fails in this non-interacting torus setting, with connections to elastica classification and related open questions.

title: The Minimax Value Of Outcome Feedback In Budget-constrained Adaptive Sampling
authors: Shengye Tao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether adaptivity improves estimation is a classical question in sequential design and information-based complexity. In practice, adaptive data collection can use two different kinds of information: process data on whether each contact succeeded, and the observed outcomes themselves. How much each kind is worth in the worst case under a hard budget has not been settled. We study this question for estimating a common Bernoulli mean through channels with unknown response probabilities and known costs, where failed contacts are charged and the budget must hold on every sample path. We compare static designs, designs that adapt to response indicators only, and fully adaptive designs, each with an arbitrary estimator. Our main theorem shows that when the costs are invariant under a group of channel permutations acting transitively on the nuisance parameter, outcome-adaptive allocation has zero minimax value: response-adaptive and fully adaptive designs have the same minimax risk, given by a one-dimensional optimization and attained by an explicit least-favourable prior and equalizer rule. For two contacts we obtain a closed-form criterion for when response feedback strictly improves on every static design. An unequal-cost example with a computer-certified exact saddle shows that the same conclusion can hold without symmetry, even though no product prior is least favourable there. A correlated prior shows that outcome feedback can still reduce Bayes risk, so the equivalence is genuinely minimax. In this idealized setting, the results support responsive survey designs that adapt to paradata but not to outcomes.
tldr: The paper studies whether outcome feedback improves worst-case estimation in budget-constrained adaptive sampling for a Bernoulli mean under unknown channel response probabilities.
motivation: Adaptive data collection can exploit response indicators or observed outcomes, but the minimax value of outcome feedback under hard budget constraints was unsettled.
method: The authors compare static, response-adaptive, and fully outcome-adaptive designs with arbitrary estimators, proving equivalence under transitive channel-permutation symmetries and giving closed-form and computer-certified examples.
result: Under symmetric costs, outcome-adaptive allocation has zero minimax value: response-adaptive and fully adaptive designs achieve the same minimax risk, characterized by a one-dimensional optimization and least-favourable prior.
conclusion: In this idealized setting, adaptivity to response indicators can suffice while outcome feedback provides no minimax benefit, supporting survey designs that adapt to paradata rather than outcomes.

title: Rate--burst Safety Languages: The Farey Structure Of The Burst Boundary And Discrimination Under Erasures
authors: Zhuo Li Lihui Dong
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A leaky-bucket constraint with rate \(\rho\) and burst \(B\) allows at most \(\rho n+B\) costly steps in every window of \(n\) consecutive steps. The infinite 0/1 words that satisfy it form a safety language. For a finite graph with edge costs 0 and 1, we study the least burst at which the cost word of some infinite path lies in this language, as a function of the real rate. This function is the exact tolerance of a monitor that distinguishes two finite-state systems observed through an erasure channel with a leaky-bucket bound. The language is \(\omega\)-regular at every rational rate but not at irrational rates once the burst reaches 1, so ultimately periodic witnesses do not come from automata theory. We prove directly that simple lassos suffice at all real rates and that all breakpoints of the boundary lie in the Farey sequence of order N for a graph with N vertices. One lasso has a tight bound of order N to the power 2/3 on its affine pieces, whereas the choice among paths creates downward jumps and boundaries that are neither convex nor concave. One evaluation at the mediant of each Farey interval recovers the affine piece and an optimal lasso, and a greatest-fixed-point computation over decreasing integer bursts yields the whole function in polynomial time and linear working space. We also compute discrimination horizons and extend the Farey structure to turn-based safety games.
tldr: The paper characterizes the burst boundary of leaky-bucket-constrained (rate, burst) safety languages for cost words of infinite paths in finite graphs, showing its breakpoints lie in Farey sequences and giving polynomial-time algorithms to compute the whole boundary function.
motivation: Leaky-bucket constraints define safety languages that model the exact tolerance of monitors distinguishing two finite-state systems observed through an erasure channel subject to a burst bound, motivating a precise understanding of the minimal burst as a function of the real rate.
method: The authors prove directly that ultimately periodic 'lasso' witnesses suffice at all real rates, including irrational rates where the language is not omega-regular, and exploit Farey-sequence structure plus a greatest-fixed-point computation over decreasing integer bursts.
result: All breakpoints of the burst boundary lie in the Farey sequence of order N for an N-vertex graph; one lasso's affine pieces have a tight bound of order N^(2/3), path choice produces non-convex, non-concave downward jumps, and a single evaluation at each Farey mediant recovers the piece and an optimal lasso; the full function is computed in polynomial time and linear space, with discrimination horizons and extension to turn-based safety games.
conclusion: The work establishes a Farey-based combinatorial structure underlying rate-burst safety boundaries and yields efficient algorithms for computing discrimination horizons, entirely within formal-language and automata theory.

title: An Elasticity Complex For Kirchhoff--Love Shells
authors: Albert Chern Hang Yin
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an elasticity complex for Kirchhoff--Love shell theory, based on the linearized Gauss--Codazzi equations as compatibility conditions for shell strains. The resulting shell complex forms a fine resolution of the sheaf of infinitesimal rigid motions, so its cohomology groups are determined by the corresponding sheaf cohomology. Remarkably, the complex also reveals an Airy potential representation of equilibrium stress fields. The framework further identifies natural boundary conditions for both kinematic and dynamic variables. Finally, we establish a Hodge--Morrey--Friedrichs decomposition for strain and stress fields on shells with boundary.
tldr: The paper constructs an elasticity complex for Kirchhoff--Love shell theory derived from the linearized Gauss--Codazzi compatibility conditions, yielding cohomological, Airy-stress, and Hodge--Morrey--Friedrichs decomposition results.
motivation: Shell theories lack a unified complex-based framework analogous to the elasticity complex in three dimensions, which is needed to characterize compatibility conditions, equilibrium stress representations, and boundary conditions systematically.
method: The authors build a cochain complex using the linearized Gauss--Codazzi equations as strain compatibility conditions, analyze its cohomology as a fine resolution of the sheaf of infinitesimal rigid motions, and establish a Hodge--Morrey--Friedrichs decomposition on shells with boundary.
result: The complex resolves the rigid-motion sheaf, reveals an Airy potential representation of equilibrium stress fields, and identifies natural kinematic and dynamic boundary conditions.
conclusion: The framework provides a rigorous homological and decompositional structure for Kirchhoff--Love shells, useful for shell finite element modeling and continuum mechanics.

title: Pauli-consistent Ensemble Monte Carlo Method For Bipolar Charge Transport In Graphene
authors: Giovanni Nastasi Tigran Zalinyan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a Pauli-consistent ensemble Monte Carlo method for bipolar charge transport in graphene, with an explicit treatment of phonon-assisted interband scattering, including electron-hole generation and recombination. The method employs a valence-vacancy representation to describe coupled electron and hole populations without explicitly simulating the highly populated valence band. It preserves the discrete occupation bounds during both free flight and scattering while conserving net charge. The numerical properties of the method are assessed through sensitivity and refinement studies and comparison with an independent deterministic discontinuous Galerkin solution of the same kinetic model. The two approaches show very good agreement for the time evolution, carrier distributions, and steady-state transport observables across the investigated transport regimes. The results also demonstrate the computational practicality of the method for microscopic simulations of bipolar graphene transport.
tldr: The paper develops a Pauli-consistent ensemble Monte Carlo method for simulating bipolar charge transport in graphene, including phonon-assisted interband scattering and electron-hole generation/recombination.
motivation: Accurate microscopic simulation of coupled electron and hole transport in graphene is challenging due to the highly populated valence band and the need to preserve occupation bounds while conserving charge.
method: The authors introduce a valence-vacancy representation to avoid explicit simulation of the full valence band and implement a Pauli-consistent ensemble Monte Carlo scheme with free-flight and scattering steps that respect discrete occupation constraints. They validate it against an independent deterministic discontinuous Galerkin solver.
result: The Monte Carlo method agrees well with the deterministic solution for time evolution, carrier distributions, and steady-state transport observables across several regimes, and is shown to be computationally practical.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical and physically consistent tool for microscopic simulations of bipolar graphene transport, though it is outside the user's quantum information and thermodynamics research directions.

title: MCP-based Euv Ptychography With Physics-simulation-trained Residual Learning
authors: Qijun You, Nuoxuan Yang, Fangrui Quan, Xu Han, Jie Li, Seunghwoi Han, Wei Cao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Microchannel-plate (MCP) detectors offer high gain for extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) experiments, but spatial blur and nonlinear response hinder quantitative diffraction imaging. Here, we present an MCP-based EUV ptychography system that combines detector hardware with physics-simulation-trained computational restoration. A residual-learning neural network trained on simulated detector degradation restores diffraction patterns without experimentally acquired training pairs. This preprocessing substantially improves image quality compared with reconstructions from uncorrected data under identical reconstruction settings. Single-harmonic imaging at [MATH]~nm yields an effective edge-response width of [MATH]m, approaching the nominal diffraction-limited scale of the imaging geometry. The approach further enables wavelength-multiplexed imaging at [MATH] and [MATH]~nm. By coupling high-gain detection with computational compensation, this system enables high-resolution, multi-harmonic EUV ptychography and offers a cost-effective alternative to scientific-grade EUV CCD detectors.
tldr: The authors build an MCP-based EUV ptychography system whose diffraction patterns are restored by a residual-learning network trained purely on simulated detector degradation, improving reconstruction quality and enabling multi-harmonic imaging.
motivation: Microchannel-plate detectors provide high gain for extreme-ultraviolet experiments but their spatial blur and nonlinear response degrade quantitative diffraction imaging, and scientific-grade EUV CCDs are expensive.
method: A residual-learning neural network trained on physics-based simulations of MCP detector degradation is used to preprocess and restore measured diffraction patterns before ptychographic reconstruction, requiring no experimentally acquired training pairs.
result: Single-harmonic imaging near the diffraction limit yields an effective edge-response width close to the nominal diffraction-limited scale, and wavelength-multiplexed imaging at two harmonics is demonstrated.
conclusion: Coupling high-gain MCP detection with simulation-trained computational compensation offers a cost-effective route to high-resolution, multi-harmonic EUV ptychography as an alternative to scientific-grade EUV CCD detectors.

title: Deterministic Regularisation Of The Nonsymmetric Eigenproblem
authors: Matthew J. Colbrook
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a deterministic algorithm for pseudospectral shattering in exact arithmetic. This resolves an important open problem in the complexity of the nonsymmetric eigenproblem. Given a complex contraction [MATH] of order [MATH] and [MATH], we compute a perturbation [MATH] with [MATH] such that [MATH] has simple spectrum. The ratio of its eigenbasis condition number to its minimum eigenvalue gap is at most [MATH]. The algorithm also computes an exact eigensystem of [MATH]. It uses [MATH] real-field operations and comparisons, where [MATH] and [MATH] are absolute constants. We choose the rank-one perturbations using a lower bound on the circle mean of the logarithm of the discriminant modulus. A quadratic penalty controls how far the accumulated updates move the matrix. By using the same reference eigenbasis for several updates, we can estimate all the current projector norms while recovering only the directions needed for the next perturbation.
tldr: The paper presents a deterministic exact-arithmetic algorithm for pseudospectral shattering of nonsymmetric matrices by computing a small perturbation that yields a simple spectrum with controlled eigenbasis conditioning.
motivation: The nonsymmetric eigenproblem is numerically delicate due to ill-conditioning and pseudospectral effects; resolving pseudospectral shattering deterministically addresses a complexity-theoretic open problem.
method: Using rank-one perturbations chosen via a lower bound on the circle mean of the logarithm of the discriminant modulus, the algorithm controls accumulated updates with a quadratic penalty and reuses a reference eigenbasis to estimate projector norms efficiently.
result: For a complex contraction of order n, the algorithm computes a perturbation with bounded norm such that the perturbed matrix has simple spectrum and the ratio of eigenbasis condition number to minimum eigenvalue gap is bounded, using O(n^3) real-field operations and comparisons.
