conclusion: This provides a deterministic polynomial-time solution to pseudospectral shattering in exact arithmetic, advancing the complexity theory of the nonsymmetric eigenproblem.

title: Pre-d-algebras, Pre-f-algebras And Their Completions
authors: H\"uma G\"urk\"ok Bahri Turan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define pre-d- and pre-f-algebras on Archimedean pre-Riesz spaces by conditions on the order and the multiplication only, and show that a pre-Riesz algebra is a pre-f-algebra if and only if its multiplication extends to an f-algebra multiplication on its Riesz completion. On order dense subspaces of C(K), K a compact Hausdorff space, in which disjoint positive elements separate the points of K, a pre-Riesz algebra is a pre-f-algebra if and only if multiplication by every positive element is band preserving.
tldr: The paper introduces pre-d-algebras and pre-f-algebras on Archimedean pre-Riesz spaces and characterizes when their multiplication extends to an f-algebra multiplication on the Riesz completion.
motivation: The work aims to extend order-algebraic notions such as d- and f-algebras from Riesz spaces to the more general setting of pre-Riesz spaces, motivated by structural questions about multiplication and order compatibility.
method: The authors define pre-d- and pre-f-algebras using only order and multiplication conditions, then prove extension and characterization theorems via Riesz completions and band-preserving multiplication on order-dense subspaces of C(K).
result: A pre-Riesz algebra is a pre-f-algebra exactly when its multiplication extends to an f-algebra multiplication on its Riesz completion; on suitable order-dense subspaces of C(K), this is equivalent to multiplication by every positive element being band preserving.
conclusion: The paper provides an order-theoretic characterization of pre-f-algebras and clarifies how f-algebra structure lifts through Riesz completions, contributing to the theory of pre-Riesz spaces rather than to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Proof Of Blackburn's Conjecture On Non-Overlapping Codes
authors: Yeow Meng Chee
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A code is non-overlapping if no nonempty proper prefix of a codeword is a suffix of a codeword. Let [MATH] be the largest size of a non-overlapping code of length [MATH] over an alphabet of size [MATH]. Levenshtein proved that [MATH], where [MATH]. We prove this conjecture. The proof uses generating functions for the nested partitions that describe maximal non-overlapping codes. We also show that only the codes [MATH] with [MATH] and their reversals meet Levenshtein's bound.
tldr: The paper proves Blackburn's conjecture that for sufficiently large length, maximum non-overlapping codes are attained by certain partition-based constructions.
motivation: Non-overlapping codes are a classical coding-theoretic object, and Blackburn conjectured that the known Levenshtein-bound-attaining partition codes are optimal for all sufficiently large lengths.
method: The proof uses generating functions for nested partitions that describe maximal non-overlapping codes.
result: The conjecture is proved, and it is shown that only the codes arising from certain partitions and their reversals meet Levenshtein's bound.
conclusion: This settles a conjecture in classical coding theory and characterizes the extremal non-overlapping codes.

title: Inner Derivations And Automorphism Groups Of Vertex Operator Algebras
authors: Jianzhi Han
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a simple, rational, [MATH]-cofinite vertex operator algebra of CFT type. We prove that the zero mode map [MATH], [MATH], is an isomorphism of Lie algebras. We prove surjectivity using traces on finite sums of weight spaces and Li's module construction, and injectivity using the vacuum character of Zhu's algebra. It follows that [MATH] is the identity component of [MATH] and has finite index in [MATH]. Moreover, [MATH], so [MATH] is finite if and only if [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves that the zero-mode map is a Lie algebra isomorphism between inner derivations and a certain automorphism Lie algebra for simple rational C2-cofinite vertex operator algebras of CFT type.
motivation: The work aims to clarify the structure of automorphism groups and inner derivations of vertex operator algebras, extending algebraic understanding of conformal field theory-type VOAs.
method: The proof uses traces on finite sums of weight spaces and Li's module construction for surjectivity, and the vacuum character of Zhu's algebra for injectivity.
result: It shows that the inner derivation algebra is the identity component of the automorphism group and has finite index, with finiteness conditions characterized by the vanishing of a certain space.
conclusion: The results establish structural Lie-algebraic properties of automorphism groups of rational VOAs, but are purely mathematical and unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Praxis: Practical Witness Encryption For Np
authors: David Tse (byzantine Research, Stanford University), Nikhil Vanjani (byzantine Research), Psi Vesely
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Witness encryption encrypts a message to an NP statement so that whoever holds a witness can decrypt. Over a decade after its introduction, known constructions for general NP statements are far from practical or rest on heuristic or broken assumptions. We propose Praxis, a practical scheme for NP, and prove it extractable in the bilinear generic group and random oracle models under Module-SIS. Our instantiation encrypts to a Groth16 verifier on BN254, set up honestly, which serves every NP relation at the same cost: at [MATH]-bit security, its ciphertext is [MATH] GiB, encryption takes [MATH] base-field multiplications, and decryption with a Groth16 proof [MATH] on average. We give Lean 4 proofs of correctness and extraction at this instantiation's parameters. Praxis starts from the rank-gap template of the recent feasibility result [Hair and Sahai, arXiv 2026]. Where they raise the gap to keep decryption polynomial, we fix it, so decryption ends with a search that is exponential but concretely fast: [MATH] expected operations for a statement in [MATH] Boolean unknowns at [MATH]-bit security. A quadratic arithmetic program makes our hidden matrix low rank, so where their ciphertext encodes a basis of a matrix space, ours holds factors of width two, which a pairing multiplies. Weights and identities from an extension field tie copies of this matrix, so an adversary telling encryptions apart yields a witness or a Module-SIS solution. For the same Groth16 statement and [MATH]-bit security level, Praxis reduces the ciphertext size and the cost of encryption of either of their constructions by over ten orders of magnitude, and that of decryption by over six.
tldr: Praxis is a practical witness encryption scheme for general NP statements built from a rank-gap template, Groth16 verification on BN254, and Module-SIS assumptions.
motivation: Witness encryption has been theoretically known for over a decade, but existing general-NP constructions are impractical or rely on heuristic or broken assumptions.
method: The authors modify a recent rank-gap feasibility construction by fixing the gap, use a quadratic arithmetic program to make the hidden matrix low rank, and prove extractability in bilinear generic group and random oracle models under Module-SIS, with Lean 4 proofs.
result: For a Groth16 verifier on BN254, Praxis achieves ciphertexts of a few GiB at 128-bit security and reduces ciphertext size and encryption cost by over ten orders of magnitude compared with prior constructions, while keeping decryption concretely fast despite exponential worst-case search.
conclusion: Praxis makes witness encryption for NP significantly more practical, though it remains a classical cryptographic construction rather than a quantum information result.

title: Apuf-sng: A Low-Cost Arbiter-PUF Stochastic Number Generator With Tunable Output Probability
authors: Shelby Williams, Mehran Moghadam, M. Hassan Najafi, Sercan Aygun, Arman Roohi, Gourav Datta
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic computing (SC) encodes numerical values as probabilistic bit-streams and enables arithmetic operations using simple logic gates, offering a promising paradigm for low- cost, fault-tolerant, and highly parallel computation. However, the accuracy and efficiency of SC systems depend on the quality of the stochastic number generator (SNG). Conventional SNGs rely on pseudo-random or quasi-random generators, whose deterministic nature introduces periodicity, correlation, and bias, limiting achievable accuracy and robustness. This paper proposes a low- cost arbiter physical unclonable function (APUF)-based SNG that operates in near-metastable delay conditions to generate true- random stochastic bit-streams with controllable output probabilities. By selecting input challenges that drive the path delay difference toward a target value, the resulting output probability is governed by intrinsic device noise, eliminating the need for conventional random-number generators and comparator-based SNGs. The proposed design inherits the low hardware overhead and statistical independence properties of the APUF structure. A probabilistic model and a challenge selection method are developed to characterize and control the stochastic behavior. An 8-stage APUF-SNG matches the 1% mean absolute error of state- of-the-art true-random SNGs at 1024-bit streams and occupies 116{\mu}m^2 in 45nm, 2.5x and 7x smaller than the TRNG-based and Sobol-based generator designs, respectively.
tldr: The paper proposes a low-cost arbiter-PUF-based stochastic number generator for stochastic computing with tunable output probabilities.
motivation: Conventional stochastic number generators suffer from periodicity, correlation, and bias due to deterministic pseudo-random or quasi-random sources, limiting stochastic computing accuracy and robustness.
method: The authors use an 8-stage arbiter physical unclonable function operating near metastability, select challenges to target path-delay differences, and develop a probabilistic model and challenge-selection method to control output probability.
result: The APUF-SNG matches the 1% mean absolute error of state-of-the-art true-random SNGs at 1024-bit streams while occupying 116 μm² in 45nm, 2.5x and 7x smaller than TRNG-based and Sobol-based designs.
conclusion: The design provides a compact, true-random stochastic bit-stream generator without conventional random-number generators or comparator-based SNGs, suitable for low-cost stochastic computing hardware.

title: Reporting Differential Privacy Guarantees Via Operationally Equivalent $\varepsilon$: What Does $\varepsilon=19.61$ Mean For The 2020 U.s. Census?
authors: Masayuki Terada, Shinsuke Ito, Takumasa Ishioka, Hidetoshi Matsui
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The large value [MATH], reported as an approximate differential privacy (ADP) parameter for the 2020 U.S. Census, has prompted doubts about the adequacy of Census privacy protection. It was obtained by converting component zero-concentrated differential privacy (zCDP) guarantees to ADP at [MATH]. A single ADP pair can substantially loosen the original upper bound on the power (true positive rate) of a distinguishing test. At significance level [MATH], we express the original bound as the smallest pure differential privacy (DP) parameter giving the same power bound. We call this the [MATH]-operationally equivalent [MATH]. The full curve represents the original bound exactly on [MATH], even when the bound is nonconcave. For maximum-power curves and bounds derived from trade-off functions, we characterize the extrema of operationally equivalent [MATH] over an interval of significance levels. When finite, they give the parameters of the pure DP bounds that enclose the original power bound on that interval. The mapping preserves the ordering of power bounds at each significance level. For Laplace and Gaussian mechanisms with equal noise variance, conversion to single ADP pairs or Gaussian DP envelopes can reverse this ordering. For the P.L. 94-171 redistricting data, we reproduce the reported [MATH] as the sum of rounded component ADP values. The published zCDP guarantee yields operationally equivalent [MATH] values of approximately 4.25, 2.94, and 3.18 at significance levels of 1%, 5%, and 10%, respectively. Converting the same guarantee to a single ADP pair at [MATH] gives power bounds near 1 at all three levels. The pure DP scale thus clarifies constraints on distinguishing attacks that are difficult to discern from the reported [MATH].
tldr: The paper interprets the large reported approximate differential privacy parameter for the 2020 U.S. Census by converting zCDP guarantees into operationally equivalent pure-DP parameters that preserve distinguishing-test power bounds.
motivation: The reported ε=19.61 for the 2020 U.S. Census raises concerns about privacy protection, and a single ADP pair can obscure the actual bounds on distinguishing attacks.
method: The authors define an ε that is operationally equivalent at a given significance level by matching the power bound of the original guarantee, extend this to curves over significance levels, and compare conversions for Laplace and Gaussian mechanisms.
result: For the redistricting data, the published zCDP guarantee yields operationally equivalent ε values of about 4.25, 2.94, and 3.18 at 1%, 5%, and 10% significance, whereas conversion to a single ADP pair at ε=19.61 gives power bounds near 1.
conclusion: The pure-DP scale clarifies privacy constraints on distinguishing attacks that are hard to see from the reported ADP value.

title: Intrinsic Value Modules: Trusted-Hardware Support For Locally Final Offline Asset Transfer
authors: Ali Rahimi Amirreza Fathi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consensus lets distributed participants agree on a common state, but it makes monetary validity depend on network connectivity and collective acceptance. We explore making validity intrinsic to a digital coin. We propose an : trusted hardware that gives a coin locally verifiable authenticity and spendability, analogous to verifying a signature. Under stated hardware and cryptographic assumptions, the IVM abstraction and our offline transfer protocol move monetary uniqueness from a replicated ledger into non-clonable protected state. The protocol prevents forgery, replay, double credit, and double spending by genuine, uncompromised IVMs; communication failures may lock value but cannot duplicate it. We distinguish local transfer atomicity and asset uniqueness, which the protocol establishes, from global state consistency across disconnected devices, which it does not. The IVM does not eliminate trust; it relocates trust to certified hardware, issuer roots, and non-rollback state. We present the architecture, protocol, and security analysis, and discuss open challenges.
tldr: The paper proposes trusted-hardware-based Intrinsic Value Modules to enable locally final offline cryptocurrency asset transfer without consensus.
motivation: The authors aim to remove dependence on network connectivity and collective ledger acceptance for monetary validity by making coin authenticity and spendability locally verifiable.
method: They define the IVM abstraction and an offline transfer protocol using non-clonable protected hardware state and cryptographic assumptions, then provide a security analysis against forgery, replay, and double-spending.
result: The protocol prevents duplication and double-spending by genuine uncompromised IVMs while acknowledging that communication failures can lock value and that global consistency across disconnected devices is not achieved.
conclusion: The work relocates trust from consensus to certified hardware, issuer roots, and non-rollback state, and discusses open challenges for practical deployment.

title: From Footprints To Service Regions: Modeling And Analysis Of Dense Leo Satellite Networks Using An Orbit-Aware Cox Point Process
authors: Chang-Sik Choi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.29119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In dense low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks, several accessible satellites cover the same location. A footprint therefore identifies where communication is feasible but does not determine which satellite serves each user. The service region of a satellite, namely the set of locations it serves, governs satellite load, resource sharing, and user throughput. Using an orbit-aware Cox point process on a common orbital shell, we model each service region as the intersection of a satellite's spherical-cap footprint and its spherical Voronoi cell under nearest-satellite association. We then use Palm calculus to derive exact expressions for the mean area and perimeter and a coverage--load identity. After coverage saturates, mean area and load decrease inversely with population. In contrast, adding satellites along existing orbits leaves a positive limiting mean perimeter. We connect this geometry to an approximate noise-limited user rate. Along the tested densification paths, the increase in user rate comes mainly from the decrease in mean satellite load rather than from the improvement of the serving link. We also compare the model with Walker constellations with Starlink-type parameters, using Cox parameters matched to the local orbit and satellite densities at each latitude. The model reproduces the mean area and perimeter of these constellations over broad latitude ranges, with larger differences near component maximum latitudes. These results show that service-region geometry, and hence satellite load and user rate, depend not only on the total satellite population but also on its allocation across orbital planes.
tldr: The paper models service regions of satellites in dense LEO constellations using an orbit-aware Cox point process, deriving exact geometric statistics and connecting them to satellite load and user throughput.
motivation: In dense LEO networks multiple satellites can cover a location, so coverage footprints alone do not determine which satellite serves a user; the service-region geometry governing load and rate needs a tractable stochastic-geometric model.
method: Each service region is modeled as the intersection of a spherical-cap footprint with the satellite's spherical Voronoi cell under nearest-satellite association, analyzed via Palm calculus on a common orbital shell and compared with Walker/Starlink-type constellations.
result: Exact expressions for mean area, perimeter, and a coverage-load identity are derived; mean area and load decrease inversely with population after coverage saturation, while adding satellites along existing orbits leaves a positive limiting perimeter, and rate gains come mainly from reduced load.
conclusion: Service-region geometry—and hence load and user rate—depends on how satellites are allocated across orbital planes, not just total population; the Cox model reproduces Walker constellation statistics over broad latitude ranges.

title: Kam Theory For Contact Hamiltonian Systems
authors: Zhicheng Tong, Yong Li, Xuefeng Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In both finite and infinite dimensions, we establish the first frequency-preserving KAM theorems for full-dimensional Legendrian tori in contact Hamiltonian families with general analytic coupling between the momenta and the contact variable. After adjustment of external parameters, the flow on each torus is analytically conjugate in the original time to the prescribed translation, with estimates uniform as the damping parameter crosses zero. This coupling can generate nonzero mean damping at first order even when the damping parameter vanishes. In finite dimensions, nonzero mean damping yields a time-preserving analytic contact linearization near the torus. In both settings the invariant graphs give global analytic solutions of stationary Hamilton--Jacobi equations whose characteristic flows are conjugate to the prescribed translation. A novel consequence in finite dimensions is that, under global Tonelli assumptions and strict increase in the contact variable, this analytic solution is both the unique forward and the unique backward weak KAM solution, and its associated Legendrian graph is an invariant torus carrying quasi-periodic dynamics.
tldr: The authors prove frequency-preserving KAM theorems for full-dimensional Legendrian tori in contact Hamiltonian systems, in both finite and infinite dimensions, with uniform estimates as the damping parameter goes to zero.
motivation: KAM theory has been developed extensively for symplectic Hamiltonian systems, but contact Hamiltonian systems — which describe dissipative dynamics with a contact structure — lack a frequency-preserving KAM theory for Legendrian tori, particularly with general momentum–contact coupling.
method: Using a Nash–Moser / KAM iterative scheme with external parameter adjustment, the authors construct analytic conjugacies uniform in the damping parameter, and exploit Tonelli-type global assumptions and monotonicity in the contact variable to obtain uniqueness of weak KAM solutions.
result: Invariant Legendrian graphs are constructed whose flows are analytically conjugate to prescribed translations; these give global analytic solutions of stationary Hamilton–Jacobi equations, and in finite dimensions the solution is shown to be both the unique forward and unique backward weak KAM solution.
conclusion: The work establishes a first KAM theory for contact Hamiltonian systems and links contact linearization, stationary Hamilton–Jacobi equations, and weak KAM theory, with implications for quasi-periodic dynamics on Legendrian tori.

title: Particle Separation In A Time-correlated Gaussian Velocity Field: A Numerical Study
authors: Silvia Morlacchi Mario Maurelli
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We numerically investigate the dispersion of passive tracer pairs in a two-dimensional, divergence-free, time-correlated Gaussian velocity field. The field is constructed from a sparse set of Fourier modes evolving as independent Ornstein--Uhlenbeck processes, with spatial regularity and scale-dependent temporal decorrelation comparable to those of a power-law Gaussian velocity ensemble. We show that, for spatial roughness exponent [MATH] and temporal decorrelation exponent [MATH], corresponding to the regime [MATH], the extrapolated mean-square distance is compatible with particle separation (in mean-square) at positive time: two particles reach a mean-square positive distance at a finite time, no matter how close they are initially.
tldr: This numerical study investigates how passive tracer pairs separate in a two-dimensional time-correlated Gaussian velocity field with scale-dependent temporal decorrelation.
motivation: The authors aim to understand particle dispersion in a stochastic velocity field whose spatial and temporal correlation structure resembles power-law Gaussian velocity ensembles.
method: They construct a divergence-free velocity field from sparse Fourier modes evolving as independent Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes and numerically track passive tracer pairs.
result: For a specified roughness exponent and temporal decorrelation exponent, the extrapolated mean-square distance becomes positive at finite time, implying separation even for initially arbitrarily close particles.
conclusion: The findings characterize particle separation regimes in time-correlated Gaussian velocity fields, which is relevant to stochastic fluid dynamics rather than quantum information science.

title: Picojoule-level Self-referencing With Dual Dispersive Waves In Thin-film Lithium Niobate
authors: Kiyoung Ko, Ian Christen, Kamila Kunes, Clayton Cheung, Chun-Ho Lee, Kiwon Kwon, Mihir Chaudhari, Ran Yin, Tushar Sanjay Karnik, Mengjie Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate pulse-energy-efficient f-2f self-referencing of telecom-band pulses in a monolithic thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) waveguide that combines Kerr spectral broadening with quasi-phase-matched (QPM) second-harmonic generation (SHG). Dispersion engineering generates dual dispersive waves (DWs) near 1 and 2 um, placed symmetrically around the pump to reduce the required spectral broadening. With an on-chip pulse energy of only 16.8 pJ, we detect a carrier-envelope-offset frequency (fceo) beatnote with a 32 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and we stabilize the fceo of an Er-fiber laser at 30 pJ, which is, to our knowledge, the lowest pulse energy reported for fceo stabilization at telecom wavelengths. Compared with an identical waveguide without poling, the QPM section enhances the beatnote SNR by 43 dB and reduces the required pulse energy fourfold. We further show that a mode-crossing DW, a chirped poling period, and a poled section aligned with the onset of DW generation to mitigate temporal walk-off are key to this performance.
tldr: The paper demonstrates low-pulse-energy f-2f self-referencing and carrier-envelope-offset stabilization in a thin-film lithium niobate waveguide using dual dispersive waves and quasi-phase-matched SHG.
motivation: Efficient self-referencing at telecom wavelengths is needed for compact, low-power frequency comb sources, but conventional schemes require relatively high pulse energies.
method: The authors engineer a monolithic TFLN waveguide with Kerr spectral broadening, quasi-phase-matched SHG, dual dispersive waves near 1 and 2 µm, mode crossing, and chirped poling to reduce the pulse energy needed for f-2f detection.
result: They observe an fceo beatnote with 32 dB SNR at 16.8 pJ on-chip pulse energy and stabilize the fceo of an Er-fiber laser at 30 pJ, reporting a fourfold pulse-energy reduction and 43 dB SNR enhancement from the QPM section.
conclusion: The work shows that dispersion-engineered TFLN waveguides can enable picojoule-level self-referencing and low-energy fceo stabilization at telecom wavelengths, with potential for compact frequency-comb systems.

title: Inverse Design Of Polarization-analyzing Gratings
authors: Kexin Bian, Alexander R. Fiani, Lisa W. Li, Noah A. Rubin
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metasurface polarization analyzing gratings have attracted increasing interest for polarization management and sensing in optical systems. Traditional strategies for the design of these gratings are based on a formalism combining the Jones calculus with Fourier optics. While this approach has achieved notable success in numerous applications, its validity is restricted to the paraxial regime. Here we introduce a differentiable topology optimization framework for these gratings which is free of this constraint. We show that this framework can yield designs which outperform the traditional approach, especially at high angles. Additionally, we provide preliminary experimental validation to corroborate these results.
tldr: The authors introduce a differentiable topology-optimization framework for inverse-designing metasurface polarization-analyzing gratings that remains valid beyond the paraxial regime.
motivation: Existing Jones-calculus-plus-Fourier-optics design methods for polarization-analyzing gratings are restricted to the paraxial regime and degrade at high angles, limiting performance in demanding optical systems.
method: A differentiable topology optimization approach is used to inversely design grating structures without paraxial assumptions, and preliminary experiments are performed to validate the resulting designs.
result: The optimized gratings outperform traditionally designed ones, particularly at large incidence/steering angles, supported by initial experimental evidence.
conclusion: Differentiable inverse design offers a more general and higher-performance route to polarization-analyzing metasurface gratings than paraxial Jones/Fourier formalisms.

title: Expressive Shallow Networks For Physics-Informed Learning: Why Curvature-Aware Optimization And Fp64 Are Not Enough
authors: Zachary Morrow, Yucheng Fu, Pratanu Roy, Michael Penwarden
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often struggle with high-frequency and high-order partial differential equations (PDEs) due to optimization stiffness and spectral bias, despite possessing sufficient approximation capacity. Existing remedies, including modified feature representations, domain decomposition, higher floating-point precision, and curvature-aware optimizers, can improve convergence but largely act as workarounds for optimization difficulties arising from deep architectures rather than addressing their underlying source. We investigate Physics-Informed Shallow Universal Polynomial Networks (PI-SUPNs), which replace deep nonlinear compositions with learnable polynomial expansions, retaining high approximation capacity within a shallow computational graph. On a high-frequency Helmholtz benchmark, PI-SUPNs are the only architecture to successfully recover the solution, while all competing models fail even under FP64 precision and curvature-aware optimization. However, experiments on higher vibrational modes of a fourth-order Euler-Bernoulli beam reveal that architectural improvements alone are insufficient: accurate solutions require the combination of PI-SUPNs, FP64 precision, and curvature-aware optimization. Additionally, Allen-Cahn experiments show that PI-SUPNs achieve lower solution and derivative errors at reduced computational cost, with more favorable loss landscapes than competing architectures. We also establish quasi-local approximation properties and spline-based convergence bounds for SUPNs. Our results show that shallow network architectures are an important mechanism for improving physics-informed trainability, but accurate solutions to the most challenging PDEs can still require FP64 precision and curvature-aware optimization.
tldr: The paper introduces Physics-Informed Shallow Universal Polynomial Networks (PI-SUPNs), a shallow learnable polynomial architecture that improves trainability for physics-informed learning on stiff, high-frequency PDE benchmarks.
motivation: Physics-informed neural networks struggle with high-frequency and high-order PDEs because of optimization stiffness and spectral bias, and existing fixes (feature reparameterization, domain decomposition, FP64, curvature-aware optimizers) treat symptoms of deep architectures rather than the cause.
method: The authors replace deep nonlinear compositions with learnable polynomial expansions in a shallow computational graph, and benchmark against standard PINN variants on high-frequency Helmholtz, fourth-order Euler-Bernoulli beam, and Allen-Cahn problems, supported by quasi-local approximation and spline-based convergence analysis.
result: PI-SUPNs alone recover the high-frequency Helmholtz solution where all competitors fail even with FP64 and curvature-aware optimization; the hardest beam problems still require PI-SUPNs combined with FP64 and second-order optimization, while Allen-Cahn shows lower error at lower cost with better loss landscapes.
conclusion: Shallow architectures are an important lever for physics-informed trainability, but the most challenging PDEs still demand higher precision and curvature-aware optimization in addition to architectural change.

title: Kinetic Versus Refill-zone Uncertainty In Predicted Pr--burning Of Methane-oxygen Rotating Detonation Rocket Engines
authors: Y. Sungtaek Ju
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rotating detonation rocket engines can lose performance when fresh propellant mixes with hot recirculated combustion products and ignites before the detonation wave arrives. Predicting this pre-burning requires fuel ignition chemistry at high pressure and in product-diluted mixtures, conditions most chemical kinetic mechanisms used in engine simulations were not developed for. With methane as our base fuel, we quantify how strongly predicted pre-burning depends on the choice of mechanism, test the mechanisms against published high-pressure ignition data, and use Bayesian methods to calibrate the most influential uncertain reaction and to assess which measurements would best improve the predictions. As the refill zone is represented by an idealized zero-dimensional model, our results should be viewed as relative comparisons rather than direct engine predictions. Five existing chemical kinetics mechanisms for methane combustion predict refill-zone ignition delays that differ by up to a factor of twenty. Mechanisms without methylperoxy chemistry, including two commonly used in engine simulations, do not reproduce the laboratory data below about 1150 K. Calibrating the CH[MATH] + HO[MATH] reaction against these data, while allowing for systematic differences between datasets, increases the relative importance of its chain-terminating channel, consistent with a direct rate measurement. With the data-consistent mechanisms, the remaining kinetic uncertainty in the predicted pre-burnt fraction is, in most cases, several times smaller than the uncertainty arising from the state of the refill zone: the temperature and composition of the recirculated products and the way fresh and burnt gases mix. Improved pre-burning predictions are therefore expected to depend mainly on accurately characterizing the refill zone.
tldr: A chemical-kinetics uncertainty quantification study of pre-burning (refill-zone autoignition) in methane-oxygen rotating detonation rocket engines, comparing five mechanisms and using Bayesian calibration to attribute predictive uncertainty.
motivation: Rotating detonation rocket engines lose performance when fresh propellant pre-ignites in the refill zone before the detonation wave arrives, and the standard kinetic mechanisms used in engine simulations were not developed for the high-pressure, product-diluted conditions where this occurs.
method: The author compares refill-zone ignition delays predicted by five methane combustion mechanisms against published high-pressure ignition data, then applies Bayesian calibration to the most influential uncertain reaction (CH3 + HO2), allowing for systematic inter-dataset discrepancies, within an idealized zero-dimensional refill-zone model.
result: Predicted ignition delays differ by up to a factor of twenty across mechanisms; those lacking methylperoxy chemistry fail to reproduce data below ~1150 K, and calibration shifts weight toward the chain-terminating channel of CH3 + HO2, consistent with direct rate measurements. With data-consistent mechanisms, refill-zone state uncertainty (temperature, product composition, mixing) dominates over residual kinetic uncertainty.
conclusion: Improving pre-burning predictions for rotating detonation rocket engines mainly requires better characterization of the refill zone rather than further refinement of chemical kinetic mechanisms.

title: Anisoplanatic Blind Deconvolution Using Phase Diversity
authors: Shubhankar Jape, Seungman Choi, Peter Menart, Andrew Schramka, Pratyush Uppuluri, Vaneet Aggarwal, Zubin Jacob
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atmospheric turbulence distorts the wavefront of light from a distant scene and blurs its image. Over a field of view wider than the isoplanatic angle, the distortion varies with direction and evolves in time, so no single wavefront describes the blur. Multiframe blind deconvolution (MFBD) can recover the scene from measurements spread over a long acquisition, but falls short during fast imaging because of limited diversity across measurements. We present coded anisoplanatic blind deconvolution (CA-BD), in which a pupil-plane spatial light modulator (SLM) applies a different known phase code to every measurement, with no wavefront sensor or deformable mirror, so that the measurements carry diversity even within a short acquisition. A per-pixel single-layer estimator recovers the object and spatially varying phases from the coded measurements. In simulation, a Cram\'er-Rao bound analysis shows that under anisoplanatism direct imaging needs about 41 times the photons of coded imaging for equal phase precision in strong turbulence. At the stronger of two turbulence strengths, CA-BD outperforms tuned MFBD on average at every burst length. It reduces the phase mean squared error 3.5x for stationary turbulence and 2-3x for time-varying turbulence. Measurements taken within a few coherence times benefit most from the known coded SLM patterns, making faster SLMs the key to its full advantage in time-varying turbulence.
tldr: The paper introduces coded anisoplanatic blind deconvolution (CA-BD), which uses a pupil-plane SLM to apply known phase codes per measurement so that multiframe blind deconvolution can recover a scene through anisoplanatic atmospheric turbulence without a wavefront sensor or deformable mirror.
motivation: Atmospheric turbulence blurs images from distant scenes, and over fields of view exceeding the isoplanatic angle the distortion varies spatially and temporally, so a single wavefront cannot describe the blur and conventional multiframe blind deconvolution lacks diversity during fast imaging.
method: A spatial light modulator imprints a different known phase code on each measurement, and a per-pixel single-layer estimator jointly recovers the object and spatially varying phases from the coded frames; performance is benchmarked against tuned MFBD and analyzed with a Cramér-Rao bound.
result: Cramér-Rao analysis shows direct imaging needs about 41 times more photons than coded imaging for equal phase precision in strong turbulence, and CA-BD reduces phase MSE by roughly 3.5x for stationary turbulence and 2-3x for time-varying turbulence.
conclusion: Known coded SLM patterns provide measurement diversity within short acquisitions, with the largest gains for measurements taken within a few coherence times, making faster SLMs key to exploiting the method in time-varying turbulence.

title: Approximation By Classical Summability Methods In Variable Lebesgue Spaces
authors: Tengiz Kopaliani, Alina Shalukhina, George Tephnadze
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate approximation by Fej\'er and N\"orlund means with respect to the Walsh system in variable Lebesgue spaces. We prove that the Fej\'er means are uniformly bounded on the weighted space [MATH] if and only if [MATH]. We then apply Rubio de Francia extrapolation to show that both means are uniformly bounded on [MATH] with [MATH] if and only if [MATH]. Finally, we estimate the approximation errors via the modulus of smoothness and deduce convergence rates for variable Lipschitz classes.
tldr: The paper studies approximation by Fejér and Nörlund means with respect to the Walsh system in variable Lebesgue spaces.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize boundedness of classical summability methods and derive approximation rates in variable Lebesgue spaces.
method: They prove uniform boundedness results for Fejér means and apply Rubio de Francia extrapolation to treat Nörlund means, then estimate errors via a modulus of smoothness.
result: They obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform boundedness and deduce convergence rates for variable Lipschitz classes.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical harmonic analysis and approximation theory but has no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fishburn Numbers Count Homogeneous Games
authors: Marnix Joris
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a new combinatorial interpretation for Fishburn numbers, in that they count the number of homogeneous games; specifically homogeneous games without dummy players, which we show extends to homogeneous games via the partial sums of Fishburn numbers. In doing so, we settle two conjectures commented in the OEIS A189359 entry, and finish off by providing some immediate consequences on homogeneous game counts; including an asymptotic formula and congruences.
tldr: The paper gives a new combinatorial interpretation of Fishburn numbers as counting homogeneous games without dummy players, extending to all homogeneous games via partial sums.
motivation: Fishburn numbers (OEIS A189359) lacked a combinatorial interpretation connecting them to homogeneous weighted voting games, and two conjectures in the OEIS entry remained open.
method: Bijective/combinatorial enumeration arguments establishing a correspondence between Fishburn-number structures and homogeneous games, plus derivation of partial-sum identities.
result: Two OEIS conjectures are settled, an asymptotic formula and congruences for homogeneous game counts are obtained.
conclusion: Fishburn numbers provide a clean enumeration of homogeneous games, yielding new arithmetic and asymptotic consequences for cooperative game theory counting problems.

title: Sharp Simultaneous Asymptotic Expansions For Sample-Mean Operators From Natural Exponential Families
authors: Oleksandr Volkov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of positive linear operators constructed from sample means of natural exponential families parametrized by their means. We show that the variance function [MATH] determines the entire hierarchy of cumulants, central moments, and coefficient differential operators [MATH] governing the asymptotic expansions. The cumulants satisfy the recursion [MATH], whereas the central moments are expressed in terms of partial Bell polynomials. Quantitative expansions of arbitrary order, uniform on compact subsets of the mean domain, are obtained. We also establish simultaneous expansions for the derivatives [MATH], with an explicit remainder estimate in terms of the modulus of continuity of the highest derivative. We prove that [MATH]-smoothness is sufficient for the expansion of the derivative of order [MATH] up to and including the term of order [MATH]. The Gauss-Weierstrass operators show that, within the scale of spaces [MATH], this smoothness threshold cannot generally be lowered and that the order of the modulus-of-continuity term is optimal. The general framework is applied to the Bernstein, Sz\'asz-Mirakjan, Baskakov, Post-Widder, and Gauss-Weierstrass operators.
tldr: Pure approximation-theory paper deriving sharp simultaneous asymptotic expansions for positive linear operators built from sample means of natural exponential families, with the variance function generating cumulants and coefficient differential operators.
motivation: Classical approximation operators (Bernstein, Szász–Mirakjan, Baskakov, Post–Widder, Gauss–Weierstrass) are usually analyzed case by case; the authors seek a unified framework based on the mean-parametrized variance function of natural exponential families.
method: Recursions for cumulants and Bell-polynomial expressions for central moments are derived from the variance function, yielding quantitative expansions of arbitrary order uniform on compact mean domains, plus simultaneous expansions of derivatives with explicit modulus-of-continuity remainder estimates.
result: Arbitrary-order uniform expansions are proven, and C^k smoothness is shown sufficient for expanding derivatives up to the corresponding order; Gauss–Weierstrass operators demonstrate the smoothness threshold and modulus-of-continuity order are optimal.
conclusion: The framework unifies and sharpens asymptotic expansions across several families of approximation operators, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Norm-attaining Operators On Renormings Of $c_0$
authors: Manwook Han, Miguel Mart\'in, Daniel L. Rodr\'iguez-Vidanes
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study norm-attaining operators on three renormings of [MATH]: Read's space [MATH], its smooth renorming [MATH], and Mart\'in's space [MATH]. We prove that, for every Banach space [MATH] and every [MATH], norm-attaining finite-rank operators are dense in [MATH]. Consequently, [MATH] is dense in [MATH] whenever [MATH] is reflexive. More generally, we establish that the compact Hilbertian smoothing construction of Debs, Godefroy and Saint-Raymond preserves the density of norm-attaining operators for all finite-dimensional ranges. We also extend a second-order criterion of Kadets, L\'opez-P\'erez, Mart\'in and Werner from rank two to arbitrary ranks [MATH] for operators into [MATH], and prove that the same smoothing preserves the existence and non-existence of such operators. We further investigate the possibilities and limitations of renorming techniques for excluding rank-two norm-attaining operators through analytical and geometrical approaches, including constructions that preserve the set of norm-attaining functionals. For Mart\'in's space [MATH], we prove that, for every Banach space [MATH] and every integer [MATH], there exists a rank [MATH] norm-attaining operator from [MATH] into [MATH], answering a question of Mart\'in . We also show that, for every nonzero Banach space [MATH], [MATH] contains a norm-dense linear subspace whose nonzero elements fail to attain their norms.
tldr: A pure Banach-space-theory paper studying norm-attaining operators on three renormings of c0 (Read's space, its smooth renorming, and Martín's space).
motivation: The authors aim to understand when norm-attaining operators are dense, and to probe the limits of renorming techniques for constructing spaces with few or no norm-attaining operators of given rank.
method: They establish density of norm-attaining finite-rank operators, show the compact Hilbertian smoothing construction of Debs–Godefroy–Saint-Raymond preserves this density for finite-dimensional ranges, and extend a second-order criterion of Kadets–López-Pérez–Martín–Werner to arbitrary ranks.
result: They prove density results for reflexive targets, construct examples excluding rank-two norm-attaining operators, show Martín's space admits rank-n norm-attaining operators into any Banach space, and exhibit dense subspaces of non-norm-attaining elements.
conclusion: The work clarifies the scope and limitations of renorming methods in the geometry of Banach spaces, answering a question of Martín.

title: Louis Bachelier's Theorie De La Speculation: Circulation And Reception
authors: Hector Giacomini
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Louis Bachelier's Theorie de la speculation (1900) introduced a probabilistic model of Brownian motion in a study of financial fluctuations, five years before Einstein's physical theory. By connecting probability distributions with the heat equation and studying speculation and option valuation, Bachelier anticipated central developments in probability, physics, and mathematical finance. How widely did the thesis circulate before its broader significance was recognized? Drawing on library correspondence, surviving copies, accession registers, provenance marks, historical catalogues, and acquisition lists, this article reconstructs its international circulation and reception in two forms: the separate Gauthier-Villars dissertation and its publication in the Annales scientifiques de l'Ecole normale superieure. It identifies thirty-eight foreign academic institutions in the official dissertation exchange network for 1900 and documents its operation. University exchanges, commercial purchases, journal distribution, and personal presentations provided complementary channels. American holdings reveal its geographical reach, including receipt at Cornell in April 1900. Contemporary reviews and subsequent uses establish selective engagement in mathematics, actuarial science, and economics, including transmission without attribution. An examination of probability composition and diffusion clarifies the thesis's place in the history of stochastic processes and its relationship to physical Brownian motion. Columbia's journal volume, accessioned in 1901 and borrowed by Mandelbrot in 1961, connects early dissemination with renewed interest. Distinguishing availability from documented reading and use, the study shows that delayed recognition coexisted with early international circulation and a dispersed readership across scientific traditions.
tldr: A historical-bibliometric reconstruction of the international circulation and reception of Louis Bachelier's 1900 thesis on speculation and Brownian motion.
motivation: The authors ask how widely Bachelier's Theorie de la speculation circulated before its significance was recognized, given its anticipation of Brownian motion, the heat equation analogy, and mathematical finance.
method: Reconstruction from library correspondence, surviving copies, accession registers, provenance marks, historical catalogues, and acquisition lists, tracing both the Gauthier-Villars dissertation and the Annales scientifiques de l'Ecole normale superieure publication across 38 foreign institutions in the 1900 dissertation exchange network.
result: Documents complementary dissemination channels (university exchanges, commercial purchase, journal distribution, personal presentation), early American holdings such as Cornell in April 1900, selective engagement in mathematics, actuarial science, and economics, and Columbia's volume borrowed by Mandelbrot in 1961.
conclusion: Delayed recognition coexisted with early international circulation and a dispersed readership; the study carefully distinguishes availability from documented reading and use.

title: Bennett's Conjecture On Absolutely Summing Inclusions
authors: Eduardo Vasconcelos Oliveira Teixeira Daniel Marinho Pellegrino
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We settle Bennett's conjecture [ (1977), 603--639, Conjecture~7.5] by showing that, for every [MATH], the canonical inclusion [MATH] fails to be absolutely [MATH]-summing at the critical exponents he identified. As a consequence, we obtain a complete characterization of the admissible exponents in anisotropic bilinear Hardy--Littlewood inequalities over the real and complex fields.
tldr: The paper proves Bennett's 1977 conjecture on absolutely summing canonical inclusions at critical exponents, yielding a complete characterization of admissible exponents in anisotropic bilinear Hardy–Littlewood inequalities.
motivation: Bennett conjectured in 1977 that certain canonical inclusions fail to be absolutely p-summing at specific critical exponents; this long-standing open problem in the theory of absolutely summing operators had remained unresolved.
method: The authors construct counterexamples within the Banach space / operator ideal framework, showing failure of absolute p-summability of the canonical inclusion for every relevant exponent, over both real and complex scalar fields.
result: The conjecture is settled affirmatively, and as a corollary the set of admissible exponents for anisotropic bilinear Hardy–Littlewood inequalities is fully characterized.
conclusion: The work closes a decades-old problem in functional analysis and sharpens the exponent ranges for multilinear Hardy–Littlewood-type inequalities, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Unified Bregman Projection Framework For Solving Multi-Split Multiple-Set Implicit Convex Feasibility Problems
authors: Soumitra Dey, Aviv Gibali, Simeon Reich
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the multi-split multiple-set implicit convex feasibility problem (MSMS-ICFP), in which the constraint sets are generated by point-to-set operators and the feasibility conditions are imposed both in the original space and in several image spaces connected by bounded linear operators. We analyze the generalized proximity function, built from weighted Bregman distances and Bregman projections, introduced by Censor and Dey. For translation-type point-to-set operators, we establish the continuity and Lipschitz continuity of the corresponding Bregman projections, the continuous differentiability of the proximity function with an explicit formula for its gradient, and global and local Lipschitz estimates for this gradient. We then propose a generalized simultaneous projection gradient algorithm. In the nonconvex case, the gradient norms of the iterates converge to zero and every accumulation point is stationary. When the proximity function is convex and the solution set is nonempty, the iterates converge in norm to a solution, with an [MATH] rate for the proximity values, an [MATH] rate for the gradient norms, and a linear rate under a quadratic growth condition. Cyclic and block-iterative variants are also analyzed. Numerical experiments, including a cooperative sensor network localization problem, illustrate the theory and show that, in contrast with frozen-set implicit projection methods, the proposed gradient schemes remain convergent when the translation operators are expansive.
tldr: The paper develops a unified Bregman projection and gradient framework for solving multi-split multiple-set implicit convex feasibility problems with point-to-set operators.
motivation: Multi-split feasibility problems generalize split feasibility problems by imposing constraints in several image spaces linked by bounded linear operators, but existing frozen-set implicit projection methods can fail when translation operators are expansive.
method: For translation-type point-to-set operators the authors prove continuity and Lipschitz continuity of Bregman projections, establish continuous differentiability of the weighted-Bregman proximity function with explicit gradient, derive global and local Lipschitz gradient estimates, and propose a generalized simultaneous projection gradient algorithm with cyclic and block-iterative variants.
result: In the nonconvex case gradient norms vanish and accumulation points are stationary; when the proximity function is convex and solutions exist, iterates converge in norm with sublinear rates for proximity values and gradients and a linear rate under quadratic growth, as illustrated by numerical experiments including sensor network localization.
conclusion: The gradient-based Bregman framework extends convergence guarantees beyond frozen-set implicit projection schemes, notably remaining convergent for expansive translation operators.

title: Data-driven Discovery Of Sparse Governing Equations With Parameterized Operators
authors: J. Nathan Kutz Mike Wendels
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study parameterized SINDy (pSINDy), an extension of the Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) framework for the discovery of parsimonious governing equations involving operators with unknown parameters such as fractional-order Caputo derivatives, fractional Laplacians, and parameterized kernel operators. The framework jointly identifies the unknown operator parameters and sparse library coefficients through a sparsity-promoting optimization problem. To solve this problem, we develop and analyze the parameterized sequentially thresholded least-squares (pSTLSQ) algorithm. In each iteration, it removes terms with small coefficients, updates the operator parameters by a fixed number of optimization steps that improve the fit of the remaining library terms, and refits their coefficients by least squares. Under suitable assumptions, we prove that pSTLSQ converges locally to a local minimizer and give sufficient conditions for identifying the terms present in the governing equation. Numerical experiments demonstrate recovery of governing equations from noisy synthetic data for fractional ODEs, fractional PDEs, and nonlocal diffusion equations. We also examine the influence of the hyperparameters, discretization scheme, and noise, and compare pSTLSQ with two benchmark methods. All three methods identify the correct terms at low noise levels, but differ in parameter accuracy, cost, and sensitivity to initialization and the candidate library.
tldr: The paper introduces parameterized SINDy (pSINDy) with a pSTLSQ algorithm to jointly learn unknown operator parameters (fractional derivatives, fractional Laplacians, kernel operators) and sparse governing equations from data.
motivation: Standard SINDy assumes the library operators are fully specified, so it cannot handle governing equations containing operators with unknown parameters such as fractional orders or kernel widths.
method: The authors formulate a sparsity-promoting optimization that jointly fits library coefficients and operator parameters, solved by a sequentially thresholded least-squares scheme (pSTLSQ) that alternates term pruning, a fixed number of parameter-update steps, and least-squares refitting, with local convergence and support-recovery guarantees.
result: Numerical experiments on fractional ODEs, fractional PDEs, and nonlocal diffusion equations show recovery of governing equations from noisy synthetic data, with studies of hyperparameter, discretization, and noise sensitivity plus comparisons to two benchmark methods.
conclusion: pSINDy extends sparse equation discovery to parameterized operator families, with theoretical convergence and support-identification conditions supported by empirical validation.

title: Tuning The False Discovery Rate In The Closed eBH Procedure
authors: Vladimir Vovk
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The closed eBH procedure controls the false discovery rate under arbitrary dependence between the input e-values. It takes the target false discovery rate [MATH] as its input and outputs a rejection set [MATH], the usual goal being to maximize its size [MATH]. This note discusses a modification of the closed eBH procedure that allows choosing the target false discovery rate post hoc: the rejection set and its level [MATH] can be chosen after seeing the data, and the expected ratio of the false discovery proportion to [MATH] is at most 1. We adapt Vovk and Wang's (2023) algorithm for computing discovery e-matrices to computing, in quadratic time, the frontier of achievable combinations [MATH] of the size of a rejection set [MATH] and its level [MATH]. The frontier allows us to compute an optimal rejection set in view of a given utility function [MATH], [MATH], striking a balance between the goals of reducing [MATH] and increasing [MATH].
tldr: This note modifies the closed eBH procedure so that the target false discovery rate can be chosen post hoc, computing the frontier of achievable (size, level) pairs in quadratic time.
motivation: Standard FDR-controlling procedures such as the closed eBH method take the target FDR as a fixed input, which prevents adapting the rejection set and its level after observing the data.
method: The author adapts Vovk and Wang's (2023) algorithm for computing discovery e-matrices to compute, in quadratic time, the frontier of achievable combinations of rejection set size and level, then selects an optimal rejection set via a utility function.
result: The modified procedure guarantees that the expected ratio of the false discovery proportion to the chosen level is at most 1, while allowing the level and rejection set to be selected after seeing the data.
conclusion: Post-hoc choice of the target FDR is possible within the e-value framework, enabling a principled trade-off between reducing the FDR level and increasing the number of discoveries.

title: R2wm: Recursive Reasoning Wireless Model For Long-Horizon mmWave Beam Prediction
authors: Yunxiao Tian, Li Qiao, Ziwei Wan, Andrey Ivanov, Zhen Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon beam prediction aims to extend beam-training intervals while supporting beam alignment in mobile millimeter-wave systems. Although pretrained large models can improve prediction over compact recurrent baselines, their large backbones impose substantial storage and computing requirements. To address this limitation, we propose a recursive reasoning wireless model (R2WM). Given a fixed history of beam indices and angles of departure (AoDs), R2WM repeatedly updates coupled latent and prediction states using a shared causal-attention backbone before jointly decoding the future beam indices. Backbone reuse increases computational depth at fixed parameter count. In the standard 10-step DeepMIMO setting, R2WM achieves an average normalized beamforming gain of 0.9597, compared with 0.8629 for the prompt-as-prefix large language model, with 99.1% fewer parameters and 59.1% fewer counted floating-point operations. Transfer experiments show that R2WM retains normalized gain under the tested carrier-frequency and antenna-count changes, while its beam-index-only variant retains gain under the tested base-station change. Component ablations show higher gains with historical AoD conditioning and causal attention. Recursion analysis reveals a gain-computation trade-off across separately trained configurations with the same parameter count. An additional comparison with a nonrecursive Transformer of similar parameter count shows higher gain for R2WM at greater computational cost. These results support accurate long-horizon beam prediction without a large pretrained backbone.
tldr: The paper proposes R2WM, a compact recursive reasoning model with a shared causal-attention backbone for long-horizon mmWave beam prediction in mobile wireless systems.
motivation: Pretrained large models improve beam prediction over compact recurrent baselines but impose prohibitive storage and compute costs, motivating a parameter-efficient alternative for extending beam-training intervals.
method: Given a fixed history of beam indices and AoDs, R2WM repeatedly reuses a shared causal-attention backbone to iteratively update coupled latent and prediction states before jointly decoding future beam indices, gaining computational depth at fixed parameter count.
result: In the 10-step DeepMIMO setting, R2WM reaches an average normalized beamforming gain of 0.9597 versus 0.8629 for a prompt-as-prefix LLM baseline, with 99.1% fewer parameters and 59.1% fewer FLOPs; ablations confirm benefits of AoD conditioning and causal attention.
conclusion: Accurate long-horizon mmWave beam prediction is achievable without a large pretrained backbone, with recursion offering a tunable gain-computation trade-off.

title: Cross-Boundary Vulnerability Management For SDVs: A Traceability Architecture At The Iso/sae 21434 And Eu Cyber Resilience Act Interface
authors: Krishna Teja Medam
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A software-defined vehicle depends on products that sit under different EU regimes. The type-approved vehicle and the systems, components and separate technical units made for it fall under Regulation (EU) 2019/2144, which makes UN R155 mandatory; Regulation (EU) 2018/858 does so for R156; and ISO/SAE 21434 supports the management system R155 requires. Chargers, companion apps, aftermarket devices and many backends may fall under the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) instead, whose reporting duty in Article 14 has applied since 11 September 2026. Neither side defines how a vulnerability found on one reaches the other's risk process. We contribute a four-question classification procedure, a five-regime traceability matrix, a reference architecture with four handoff paths and three boundary findings. On 75 classified products from a frozen public-source corpus, the procedure yields 47 Periphery, 11 Core, 1 Other and 16 Boundary products, three of them outside both the CRA and compulsory R155. Because UN R10 lets an electronic sub-assembly be approved as a component, the texts leave a second reading open, and we report both counts. Under it, 22 aftermarket devices become components, Periphery falls to 25 and 25 products sit outside both regimes. Seven retrospective walkthroughs suggest that, for third-party products, vulnerability information stops in the vehicle manufacturer's own inventory, triggers or exploitation assessment, and that no provision obliges a product maker to tell a vehicle manufacturer: the only defined two-way route is a contract. No reviewed source establishes a case that reached an Article 14 clock.
tldr: The paper proposes a traceability architecture and classification procedure for cross-boundary vulnerability management between ISO/SAE 21434 automotive cybersecurity and the EU Cyber Resilience Act for software-defined vehicles.
motivation: Software-defined vehicles involve products governed by different EU regulatory regimes, and no clear mechanism exists for vulnerability information to flow between automotive and CRA-covered products.
method: The authors develop a four-question classification procedure, a five-regime traceability matrix, and a reference architecture with four handoff paths, applying them to 75 products from a frozen public-source corpus and seven retrospective walkthroughs.
result: The procedure classifies products into Periphery, Core, Other, and Boundary categories, revealing that vulnerability information often stops within vehicle manufacturers' processes and that no provision obliges product makers to notify vehicle manufacturers except via contract.
conclusion: The work highlights regulatory and procedural gaps at the ISO/SAE 21434 and EU CRA interface and suggests a traceability architecture, but it is unrelated to quantum information science or technology.

title: A Characterized Softmax For Distributing Standing Across Multiple Affiliations
authors: Md Mahedi Hasan Riday, Md Shajalal, Gunnar Stevens
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cooperative game theory answers canonical questions on payoff allocation (Shapley, Owen), interaction attribution (Grabisch-Roubens, Faith-Shap), and coalition formation and stability. None answers a fourth question that arises whenever players carry known, overlapping group tags fixed independently of the game: how should a player's standing be distributed across the groups it already belongs to? We call this membership attribution, formalize it, and give a complete characterization of its solution. The direct, ratio-based answer is provably invalid whenever a player's group-level signals have mixed sign --- a common, structurally unavoidable case. We propose a restricted-domain softmax construction instead, and prove that, for any player satisfying a precisely defined richness condition on the group structure, it is the unique such map, up to a temperature parameter, satisfying five requirements. A sixth requirement fixes the sign of this temperature; a seventh, shown independent of the rest via an explicit counterexample, forces one shared temperature across all eligible players. A worked example on an exact cooperative game confirms the applicable requirements numerically and shows the construction degrades gracefully, valid but uninformative, when a player's evidence fails to distinguish between its groups.
tldr: The paper introduces and axiomatically characterizes 'membership attribution', a new cooperative-game-theoretic problem of distributing a player's standing across overlapping pre-assigned group tags, solved via a restricted-domain softmax construction.
motivation: Existing cooperative game theory frameworks (Shapley, Owen, Grabisch-Roubens, Faith-Shap) address payoff allocation, interaction attribution, and coalition stability, but none answers how a player's standing should be split across groups it already belongs to, especially when group-level signals have mixed sign and naive ratio-based allocation provably fails.
method: The authors formalize membership attribution, show ratio-based solutions are invalid under mixed-sign signals, and propose a restricted-domain softmax map, proving uniqueness up to a temperature parameter under five requirements, with a sixth fixing the temperature sign and a seventh forcing a shared temperature across eligible players.
result: The softmax construction is proven to be the unique admissible solution for players satisfying a richness condition, and a worked example on an exact cooperative game numerically confirms the requirements and shows graceful degradation to a valid but uninformative output when evidence cannot distinguish groups.
conclusion: Membership attribution is a well-posed and fully characterized problem with a unique softmax-based solution, offering a principled tool for distributing credit across overlapping affiliations in cooperative settings.

title: Targeted In-Context Poisoning Of Tabular Foundation Models: An Empirical Study
authors: Adem Alparslan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) predict the label of a query row conditioned on a context of labelled rows, without training on them. Drawn from operational data, the context becomes an attack surface. We study targeted in-context poisoning in its simplest form: an attacker with write access to the context's source places exact copies of a target row there with the wrong label. On 30 OpenML datasets for binary classification, one such poison row flips on average 53% (TabICL) and 65% (TabPFN) of the predictions correct without attack, and three poison rows flip almost all. The same copy with the true label flips almost none, and performance on the remaining rows hardly changes. Predictions flip by two routes: in TabICL, the target row's embedding rotates towards the mean of the wrong class; in TabPFN, the poison row pulls genuine rows of the wrong class along. The TFMs thus infer soundly, but from forged evidence. Predictions of trained models flip as well: almost always for a random forest, for CatBoost as often as for the TFMs, hardly for a logistic regression. New with TFMs is not the kind of vulnerability but the timing: the data take effect at the moment of prediction, not through training, and a poison row in a live context can be deleted afterwards. Three established requirements must therefore cover the context: access control for its source, traceability per prediction, which can also deter, and validation at prediction time. A detection mechanism shows how such validation can work.
tldr: An empirical study showing that injecting a few mislabelled copies of a target row into the in-context data of tabular foundation models (TabICL, TabPFN) flips a large fraction of their predictions.
motivation: Tabular foundation models make predictions conditioned on a labelled context drawn from operational data, which turns that context into an attack surface that classical training-time threat models do not cover.
method: Across 30 OpenML binary-classification datasets, the authors insert exact duplicates of a target row with the wrong label into the context and measure the resulting prediction flips for TabICL and TabPFN, compare against true-label copies, analyse embedding-level mechanisms, and benchmark trained baselines (random forest, CatBoost, logistic regression); a validation-based detection mechanism is also proposed.
result: A single poison row flips on average 53% (TabICL) and 65% (TabPFN) of otherwise-correct predictions, with three rows flipping nearly all; the mechanisms differ (embedding rotation toward the wrong class mean versus pulling genuine wrong-class rows), and a random forest is even more fragile while logistic regression is largely robust.
conclusion: The vulnerability class is familiar but the timing is new, since poisoning acts at prediction time and can be reverted; the authors argue for access control, per-prediction traceability, and prediction-time validation of the context.

title: A Model Obfuscation And Controllable Authorization Scheme For Deep Learning As A Service
authors: Nianyun Song, Haodi Wang, Yu Guo, Xiaohua Jia
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Developing deep learning models requires substantial computational and data resources, making them core intellectual assets for enterprises. As Deep Learning as a Service (DLaaS) increasingly extends to edge computing environments, models deployed on third-party devices face growing threats from reverse engineering. Existing model protection methods often depend on specialized hardware or incur substantial computational overhead, while lacking effective mechanisms for controlling model usage. There is therefore a need for lightweight solutions that combine model protection with controllable authorization. To address this challenge, we propose KeyObf, a model obfuscation and controllable authorization scheme for DLaaS. KeyObf efficiently protects model parameters and architecture through model obfuscation while binding parameter recovery to user keys, ensuring that only authorized users can perform inference correctly. By integrating a key-based mechanism into the obfuscation framework, KeyObf unifies model protection and controllable authorization. Experimental results demonstrate that KeyObf preserves the inference accuracy of authorized users, rejects inference requests when credential authentication fails, and increases the difficulty of recovering model information under the evaluated reverse-engineering conditions. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a lightweight approach to model protection and controllable authorization in third-party deployment scenarios.
tldr: KeyObf is a lightweight key-based model obfuscation and authorization scheme that protects deployed deep learning models from reverse engineering while restricting inference to credentialed users.
motivation: As Deep Learning as a Service moves to edge and third-party devices, model parameters and architectures become exposed to reverse engineering, and existing protections require special hardware or heavy computation while offering no usage control.
method: The scheme obfuscates model parameters and architecture and binds parameter recovery to user keys, unifying protection with credential-based authorization in a single key-driven framework.
result: Experiments show authorized users retain inference accuracy, unauthorized requests are rejected on authentication failure, and model recovery under evaluated reverse-engineering attacks becomes substantially harder.
conclusion: A lightweight, practical approach to model protection and controllable authorization appears feasible for third-party DLaaS deployments without specialized hardware.

title: NP-Completeness Of The Three-Dimensional Polyhedral Separation Problem
authors: Guannan Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bone tumor resection planning motivates the following geometric problem. Given tumor points and healthy-bone points in three-dimensional space, find cutting planes that separate the tumor from the surrounding bone. To avoid tumor seeding, the cutting planes must not pass through the tumor. Given a positive integer k, select at most k closed halfspaces whose intersection contains all tumor points, while minimizing the total weight of healthy-bone points strictly inside this intersection. We formalize this problem and prove that its threshold decision version is NP-complete. Consequently, the corresponding optimization problem is NP-hard.
tldr: The paper proves NP-completeness of a 3D polyhedral separation problem motivated by bone tumor resection planning.
motivation: The authors formalize a geometric cutting-plane separation problem arising in surgical planning, where cutting planes must avoid tumor points while minimizing healthy-bone inclusion.
method: They define a threshold decision version of the problem involving at most k closed halfspaces and prove NP-completeness, implying NP-hardness of the corresponding optimization problem.
result: The threshold decision problem is shown to be NP-complete, and therefore the associated optimization problem is NP-hard.
conclusion: The work establishes computational hardness for a geometrically motivated surgical planning problem, with no apparent connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: InstantCoFFEA: Fast And Accurate Tor Flow Correlation At Realistic Scale
authors: Saeyeon Hong, Hyewon Kim, Mohammad Saidur Rahman, Se Eun Oh
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tor end-to-end correlation attacks can link a client to its destination by matching traffic observed at both ends of a Tor circuit. However, their practical threat remains unclear for two reasons: existing correlation methods rely on O(N^2) pairwise processing, and prior works do not reflect the flow counts and base rates seen by realistic adversaries. We present InstantCoFFEA, which replaces exhaustive pairwise search with approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) retrieval using CAGRA and introduces ranked voting. At N = 200k, InstantCoFFEA is 14.56x faster than DeepCoFFEA and improves PR-AUC from 0.94 to 0.96. We also use TorPS to estimate the flow counts and matching-pair base rates observed by relay-level and network-level adversaries. Our simulations show that realistic attacks involve substantially more candidate flows and much lower base rates than those used in prior evaluations. Under a low-base-rate setting, PR-AUC drops for all methods, but InstantCoFFEA achieves 0.53 compared with 0.42 for DeepCoFFEA. These results show that evaluating correlation attacks requires considering both computational scale and the sparsity of true matching pairs.
tldr: InstantCoFFEA speeds up Tor flow correlation attacks using approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval and ranked voting, while evaluating realistic adversary scales and low base rates.
motivation: Tor end-to-end correlation attacks are important to understand, but existing methods are computationally expensive and prior evaluations use unrealistic flow counts and matching-pair base rates.
method: The paper replaces O(N^2) pairwise search with CAGRA-based approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval and introduces ranked voting, then uses TorPS simulations to estimate realistic candidate flow counts and base rates.
result: At N=200k, InstantCoFFEA is 14.56x faster than DeepCoFFEA and improves PR-AUC from 0.94 to 0.96; under low-base-rate conditions it achieves PR-AUC 0.53 versus 0.42 for DeepCoFFEA.
conclusion: Realistic evaluation of Tor correlation attacks must account for both computational scale and sparsity of true matching pairs, and InstantCoFFEA provides a faster, more accurate method in that setting.

title: Last-Iterate Convergence Of Payoff-Gradient Learning In M\"obius Pricing Games
authors: Martin Bichler, Philip Hierhager, Jan-Sebastian H\"ohener
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove global last-iterate convergence of payoff-gradient learning in every typewise Riemannian metric, which for scalar actions is the same as typewise mirror descent, with explicit rates, in a class of Bayesian bidding and pricing games that includes first-price auctions, unit-demand pay-as-bid auctions, rank-based generalized first-price auctions, and homogeneous-good price competition with inelastic demand. The result holds for symmetric self-play: all players use a common strategy and apply the same payoff-gradient update at each type.
