Convergence is from every continuous weakly increasing feasible initial strategy, including pooling, and does not rely on the monotonicity or Minty conditions that underlie existing guarantees in other games. Instead, the class is characterized by two structural properties: a direct payoff effect that is independent of the action, and a payoff difference at the allocation threshold that is affine in the action. These properties reduce the learning dynamics to a singular transport-damping equation for the common strategy, which, under the stated coefficient and metric assumptions, admits a unique viscosity solution. Comparison barriers make the uniform distance to the unique rest point a strict Lyapunov functional and yield convergence rates with optimal algebraic exponents. In allocation games, the rest point is the unique weakly increasing symmetric equilibrium under the stated tie-breaking conditions, and a positive lower slope bound converts strategy-error bounds into explicit approximate-equilibrium guarantees. A projected grid scheme with a slope floor makes the approximation constructive, with error bounds under deterministic perturbations and almost-sure convergence on a fixed grid under martingale gradient noise.
tldr: The paper proves global last-iterate convergence of payoff-gradient learning (typewise mirror descent) in a class of Bayesian bidding and pricing games, including first-price and pay-as-bid auctions, via a singular transport-damping equation and Lyapunov comparison barriers.
motivation: Existing convergence guarantees for gradient-based learning in games rely on monotonicity or Minty conditions that fail in many economically relevant auction and pricing games, so new structural arguments are needed for these settings.
method: The authors identify two structural properties (action-independent direct payoff effect and affine payoff difference at the allocation threshold) that reduce the learning dynamics to a singular transport-damping PDE, analyzed through viscosity solutions and comparison barriers.
result: Uniform distance to the unique rest point is shown to be a strict Lyapunov functional, yielding explicit convergence rates with optimal algebraic exponents, and a projected grid scheme provides constructive approximate-equilibrium guarantees with almost-sure convergence under martingale noise.
conclusion: Payoff-gradient learning converges globally from weakly increasing initial strategies in these games, and the rest point is the unique weakly increasing symmetric equilibrium under stated tie-breaking conditions.

title: Semantic Communication Via Federated Learning With Knowledge-Enhanced Networks And Privacy
authors: Rodrigo C. de Lamare Hassan Touati
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a novel privacy-preserving semantic communication framework that combines Federated Learning (FL) with Knowledge-Enhanced Networks (KE-NET) for distributed wireless systems. Unlike centralized semantic communication approaches that require data aggregation, our method enables multiple clients to collaboratively train a knowledge-enhanced model while keeping their data and knowledge graphs private. We develop a multi-objective federated optimization strategy that balances semantic fidelity, knowledge integration, channel robustness, and reconstruction accuracy. Theoretical analysis reveals that federated aggregation improves effective SNR for [MATH] clients through noise averaging. Numerical results with AWGN and Rayleigh fading channels demonstrate that multi-client federated learning consistently outperforms both single-client and centralized baselines across all SNR conditions, with particularly significant gains in low-SNR scenarios.
tldr: The paper proposes a privacy-preserving semantic communication framework that couples federated learning with knowledge-enhanced networks for distributed wireless systems.
motivation: Centralized semantic communication requires aggregating client data and knowledge graphs, which raises privacy concerns; the authors aim to train a shared semantic model collaboratively without moving raw data.
method: A multi-objective federated optimization strategy balances semantic fidelity, knowledge integration, channel robustness, and reconstruction accuracy, with analysis showing federated aggregation yields noise averaging and hence an improved effective SNR over AWGN and Rayleigh fading channels.
result: Numerical experiments indicate multi-client federated training consistently beats single-client and centralized baselines across all SNR regimes, with the largest gains at low SNR.
conclusion: Federated, knowledge-enhanced semantic communication is presented as a viable privacy-preserving alternative to centralized designs for wireless networks.

title: Finding Integral Stable Matchings Is PPAD-Complete: Unimodular Hypergraphs, Network $b$-Matchings, And Kernels In Perfect Graphs
authors: Gergely Cs\'aji
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Polyhedral integrality guarantees integral stable solutions in several classical stability problems: stable matchings in normal hypergraphs, stable [MATH]-matchings in unimodular hypergraphs, and kernels in clique-acyclic orientations of perfect graphs. Whether they can be computed efficiently has been a long-standing open question; for kernels in perfect graphs it has been open since the existence theorem of Boros and Gurvich in 1996. We show that, unless [MATH], they cannot. Finding a stable matching is [MATH]-complete already in linear unimodular hypergraphs with hyperedges of size at most three and vertex degrees at most three. Consequently, finding a kernel in a clique-acyclic orientation of a perfect graph is [MATH]-hard even if all cliques have at most three vertices, answering an open question of Pass-Lanneau, Igarashi and Meunier, and stable matchings are [MATH]-hard to find in balanced and in normal hypergraphs. This contrasts with the polynomial algorithm of Chandrasekaran and Kalathur for network hypergraphs. With capacities, even network hypergraphs are hard: University Dual Admission is [MATH]-complete with capacities at most nine, so stable [MATH]-matching is [MATH]-complete on network hypergraphs with hyperedges of size three. This yields [MATH]-completeness for a natural class of hospitals/residents markets with couples where stable matchings always exist, and [MATH]-hardness of computing the near-feasible stable matchings, where capacities are flexible. Both reductions are from PURE CIRCUIT with constant-size gadgets. For unit capacities we use a dual-rail encoding, a symmetry-breaking gadget made of two coupled [MATH] stable marriage markets, and a parity criterion on the bipartite incidence graph that certifies total unimodularity. We expect these tools to be useful for further hardness results about problems with guaranteed integral solutions.
tldr: The paper proves that finding integral stable matchings (in unimodular/normal hypergraphs, network b-matchings, and kernels of perfect graphs) is PPAD-complete, resolving long-standing open questions.
motivation: Polyhedral integrality guarantees existence of integral stable solutions in several classical stability problems, but whether these can be computed efficiently has remained open—for kernels in perfect graphs since 1996.
method: PPAD-hardness reductions from PURE CIRCUIT with constant-size gadgets, using a dual-rail encoding, a symmetry-breaking gadget of two coupled stable marriage markets, and a parity criterion certifying total unimodularity.
result: Finding stable matchings is PPAD-complete even in linear unimodular hypergraphs with degree ≤3, and stable b-matchings are PPAD-complete on network hypergraphs with capacities up to nine; kernels in clique-acyclic perfect graphs are PPAD-hard.
conclusion: These complexity-theoretic tools settle open questions on stable matchings and kernels and are expected to aid further hardness results for problems with guaranteed integral solutions.

title: Achievable Rate And Reconstruction Fidelity Of FeFET-Based Compute-in-Pixel Arrays
authors: Mohamed Akrout, Md Rahatul Islam Udoy, Ahmedullah Aziz, Nuria Gonzalez-Prelcic, Robert W. Heath
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compute-in-pixel (CiP) image sensors such as MACPix weight each photodiode voltage by a conductance stored in a ferroelectric FET and sum the currents on a column bus, so that [MATH] pixels are read as [MATH] weighted sums before digitization. We model the column bus as a Gaussian multiple-access channel and derive its achievable rate under thermal and shot noise, device variation, and ADC distortion. Conductance variation acts as noise proportional to the scene energy, which limits the rate to [MATH] bits per readout and makes a 6-bit ADC sufficient. End-to-end simulations recover natural images at [MATH] dB from 2 bits per pixel and, for sparse scenes, reduce the edge-node energy by up to [MATH] against raw 8-bit readout.
tldr: The paper models FeFET-based compute-in-pixel image sensor arrays as Gaussian multiple-access channels and derives achievable readout rates and reconstruction fidelity under noise and device variation.
motivation: Compute-in-pixel sensors perform analog weighted sums before digitization, but their information-theoretic limits and reconstruction performance under realistic noise are unclear.
method: The column bus is modeled as a Gaussian multiple-access channel with thermal noise, shot noise, conductance variation, and ADC distortion; end-to-end simulations evaluate image reconstruction and energy use.
result: The achievable rate is limited by conductance variation acting as scene-dependent noise, making a 6-bit ADC sufficient; natural images are recovered at a reported distortion level from 2 bits per pixel, with energy savings for sparse scenes.
conclusion: The work provides a communication-theoretic characterization of FeFET CiP arrays and shows that low-bit readout can suffice for image reconstruction, but it is classical sensor hardware and not aligned with quantum information research.

title: Watermark Claims Under Test: Lessons From Auditing A Production Llm
authors: Felix Desyatirikov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.29018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can we tell whether an LLM is watermarked without knowing its secret key? Published black-box tests suggest that carefully designed prompts can reveal the statistical footprint of a watermark. This paper examines what happens when those tests move from controlled reference implementations to a deployed model whose watermarking parameters are undisclosed. We present an audit of the Red-Green watermark presence test on Claude. Across ten initial configurations, the published test never rejects on a model the provider states is watermarked, despite detecting a local reference at comparable sample sizes. Controlled experiments expose a failure mode: including the prompt in the watermark's repeated-context history suppresses marking exactly where the test measures it. The watermark remains active, but the probe becomes blind. Attempts to repair the probe reveal further confounds. Constructed contexts can trigger native digit-to-word preferences, while comparisons within a single response can measure how the model plans its answer. Tokenization changes which contexts the probe actually controls. These findings show why validation on a surrogate model does not establish validity on the model under investigation. A redesigned probe finds a substantial context-dependent shift on Claude Fable that is absent on two sibling controls. However, the pre-registered decision remains inconclusive because selective refusals violate the protocol, and the effect's watermark origin is unresolved. We show how to design controls, distinguish statistical rejection from evidence of watermarking and interpret a null without treating it as proof of absence. We provide researchers and practitioners working on LLM evaluation, watermarking, and provenance with an audit checklist grounded in concrete successes and failures. Code, prompts, and parsed responses are available for reproducing the analyses.
tldr: This paper audits a black-box LLM watermark presence test on a production model and identifies failure modes and confounds that make validation on a surrogate model insufficient.
motivation: The authors investigate whether published statistical watermark-detection tests remain valid when applied to a deployed LLM with undisclosed watermarking parameters, rather than to controlled reference implementations.
method: They run the Red-Green watermark presence test on Claude across ten initial configurations, compare against a local reference, perform controlled experiments to diagnose a repeated-context suppression failure mode, and attempt probe repairs with additional controls.
result: The published test never rejects on the provider-stated watermarked model despite detecting a local reference, and repairs reveal confounds from digit-to-word preferences, answer planning, and tokenization; a redesigned probe finds a context-dependent shift on Claude Fable absent in sibling controls but remains pre-registered inconclusive due to selective refusals and unresolved watermark origin.
conclusion: The authors argue that surrogate-model validation does not establish validity on the target model and provide an audit checklist for distinguishing statistical rejection from evidence of watermarking and for interpreting null results without claiming absence.

title: Who Gets To Do Computing Research? Rethinking Access, Funding, And The Cost Of Research -- How Do We Ensure That Everyone With The Ideas, Ability, And Desire To Contribute To Computing Research Can Do So?
authors: Michela Taufer Gabrielle Allen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.29030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The future of computing research will be shaped not just by the questions we ask, but also by who has the opportunity to pursue them. Major investments in advanced computing, including artificial/super intelligence (AI) and quantum computing (QC), are expanding opportunities for discovery and innovation. Pursuing these opportunities requires more than a promising idea: researchers also need time, infrastructure, technical expertise, and support to compete for and administer funding. Access to these resources varies across institutions and may shape who can participate and which research directions they can pursue. A healthy computing research ecosystem depends on research taking place at institutions with different missions and resources, not only at the best-resourced ones. Computing research spans a broad spectrum of resource requirements, from theoretical work and software developed by small teams to experiments requiring specialized hardware, large datasets, and substantial technical support. Preserving opportunities across this range requires understanding not only the resources needed to conduct research, but also the costs of securing them. What does it cost an institution -- and an individual researcher -- to participate in computing research? This article invites computing researchers, university leaders, funding agencies, and industry partners to examine how funding structures, access to infrastructure, administrative responsibilities, and institutional expectations affect research opportunities, and how meaningful pathways can be preserved across institutions with different missions and resources.
tldr: This article discusses structural barriers and resource costs affecting who can participate in computing research, including funding, infrastructure, and institutional support.
motivation: The authors argue that the future of computing research depends not only on research questions but also on equitable access to time, infrastructure, expertise, and funding across institutions.
method: It is a perspective/position article that invites researchers, university leaders, funders, and industry partners to examine how funding structures, infrastructure access, administrative burdens, and institutional expectations shape research opportunities.
result: The paper frames access to computing research as a systemic issue and highlights the need to understand the costs of securing resources and preserving pathways across institutions with different missions and resource levels.
conclusion: A healthy computing research ecosystem requires broad participation and deliberate attention to resource inequities, but the article does not present quantum information science results or technical contributions.

title: FAS-Assisted Self-Interference Mitigation For In-Band Full-Duplex Communications
authors: Hanjiang Hong, Kai-Kit Wong, Jian Sang, Yiyan Wu, Hyundong Shin
abstract: ArXiv:2611.29095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In-band full-duplex (IBFD) communication relies on effective self-interference cancellation (SIC) to overcome the strong loopback self-interference (SI). While fluid antenna system (FAS)-assisted SIC offers superior SI suppression by dynamically selecting the FAS port to minimize the residual SI power, it incurs high pilot overhead to acquire channel state information (CSI) for both forward and loopback channels. This raises the question of whether forward channel CSI is necessary for effective SI mitigation. To address this challenge, we propose a pilot-efficient FAS-assisted SI mitigation (FAS-SIM) approach that selects the FAS port solely based on the loopback SI channel. Theoretical performance analysis of the forward signal is provided. Numerical results then reveal that FAS-SIM achieves SI suppression and a forward-link rate comparable to the conventional method, while reducing port-selection training overhead by 50%, offering a low-overhead solution for IBFD communications.
tldr: The paper proposes a pilot-efficient fluid antenna system approach for self-interference mitigation in in-band full-duplex wireless communications by selecting antenna ports using only loopback channel state information.
motivation: In-band full-duplex communication requires strong self-interference cancellation, and FAS-assisted mitigation can reduce residual self-interference but typically incurs high pilot overhead for acquiring both forward and loopback channel state information.
method: The authors propose FAS-SIM, which selects the FAS port solely from the loopback self-interference channel, avoiding forward-channel CSI acquisition, and provide theoretical performance analysis of the forward signal.
result: Numerical results show that FAS-SIM achieves self-interference suppression and forward-link rate comparable to the conventional method while reducing port-selection training overhead by 50%.
conclusion: FAS-SIM offers a low-overhead solution for self-interference mitigation in in-band full-duplex communications, indicating that forward-channel CSI may not be necessary for effective port selection.

title: Revisiting The Fermi Paradox: Does The Math Hold Up?
authors: Elmar Teufl Philipp N. Spahn
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a stochastic model to address the famous Fermi Paradox, i.e. the supposed contradiction between the abundance of intelligent life in the universe and the absence of any evidence of it. The model assumes that life can arise and evolve on habitable planets with a certain chance, and that we can detect life on other planets within a certain distance. The parameters of the model include the rates, at which life arises, evolves, vanishes, or advances to "Space Age", i.e. a stage where it gains the capability of interstellar communication. Given any numerical choice of these parameters, the model estimates a Contact Probability, i.e. the probability of having received a signal from an extraterrestrial civilization during the ongoing Space Age on Earth. Based on a critical probability threshold, the model can identify regions in the parameter space where Contact Probability is low, i.e. where the absence of contact is the expected outcome rather than a paradox. Monte-Carlo exploration of the parameter space shows that, even when assuming a high frequency of habitable planets, the median Contact Probability across a wide range of parameter choices is under 0.42, and under 0.06 if we assume that habitable planets generally follow an "Earth-like" trajectory, with life requiring roughly 4.5 billion years to advance to Space Age. Thus, if Earth was a typical planet with regard to its evolutionary timeline, the Fermi Paradox would likely not be a paradox.
tldr: A stochastic model of life emergence, evolution, and detection is used to argue that the Fermi Paradox may not be paradoxical under plausible parameter choices.
motivation: The authors aim to test whether the apparent contradiction between expected extraterrestrial life and the absence of contact signals is statistically robust rather than assumed.
method: They construct a stochastic model with rates for life arising, evolving, vanishing, and reaching a Space Age, then estimate a Contact Probability and explore parameter space via Monte Carlo.
result: They find median Contact Probabilities below 0.42 across wide parameter ranges and below 0.06 for Earth-like evolutionary timelines, suggesting non-contact is expected.
conclusion: If Earth's evolutionary timeline is typical, the Fermi Paradox is likely not a paradox; absence of contact is statistically consistent with the model.

title: Adaptive Precision Incomplete Matrix Factorization
authors: Andrew Lister, Theo Mary, Jennifer Scott
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Incomplete factorizations are widely used to precondition Krylov subspace methods for solving large sparse linear systems. Recent work has explored computing approximate factorizations in low precision, but using only one uniformly low precision limits the achievable accuracy and can degrade the quality of the preconditioner. We propose adaptive precision incomplete factorization algorithms in which we store each entry of the factors in a precision chosen according to its magnitude and a target accuracy. We present a rounding error analysis showing that the adaptive precision threshold-based incomplete LU and incomplete Cholesky factorizations achieve a backward error of the order of the target accuracy. We also discuss how to incorporate pivoting and scaling and how to perform the triangular solves with the adaptive precision factors. Finally, we explain how the approach applies to memory-limited incomplete Cholesky factorizations by using the magnitude of the largest dropped entry as the target accuracy. Numerical experiments on a wide range of matrices from the SuiteSparse collection show that adaptive precision can substantially reduce the storage required by the factors without degrading the quality of the preconditioner and improve the storage-weighted iteration count and overall storage required compared with uniform 64-, 32-, and 16-bit factorizations.
tldr: The paper introduces adaptive-precision incomplete LU and Cholesky factorizations for preconditioning sparse linear systems.
motivation: Uniform low-precision incomplete factorizations limit attainable accuracy and preconditioner quality, motivating per-entry precision choices.
method: Each factor entry is stored in a precision selected by its magnitude and a target accuracy, with rounding error analysis, pivoting/scaling, triangular solves, and memory-limited extensions.
result: Numerical experiments on SuiteSparse matrices show reduced storage without degrading preconditioner quality and improved storage-weighted iteration counts versus uniform 64-, 32-, and 16-bit factorizations.
conclusion: Adaptive precision offers an effective way to reduce memory for incomplete factorization preconditioners while maintaining backward error near the target accuracy.

title: Coupled Dynamical System For Sparsemax Attention
authors: Michael Huang Lianlong Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a family of coupled dynamical systems that compute sparsemax attention. Each system fuses query-key similarity and normalization into a single physical relaxation. Specifically, we cast sparsemax attention as a constrained energy minimization problem and derive a pair of coupled differential equations: one drives the energy minimization and the other enforces the constraint. At equilibrium, the system state gives exactly the sparsemax attention probabilities. We realize this formulation with continuous Ising spins and with Kuramoto oscillators. These relaxations run natively on emerging non-von Neumann platforms such as Ising machines, which have demonstrated orders-of-magnitude higher energy efficiency than digital processors, yet have so far been used mostly for unconstrained quadratic combinatorial optimization. Because analog hardware has limited precision and is noisy, we simulate both systems under these non-idealities, and inference quality degrades gracefully. Our formulation extends these emerging computing substrates from combinatorial optimization to attention, opening a path toward a new class of physical accelerators for transformer inference.
tldr: The paper proposes coupled dynamical systems using Ising spins and Kuramoto oscillators to compute sparsemax attention for transformer inference on non-von Neumann hardware.
motivation: Emerging analog hardware like Ising machines offers high energy efficiency but is mainly used for combinatorial optimization; the authors aim to extend such platforms to attention mechanisms in neural networks.
method: Sparsemax attention is cast as a constrained energy minimization problem, leading to coupled differential equations that are realized with continuous Ising spins and Kuramoto oscillators, with simulations under hardware noise and precision limits.
result: The dynamical systems converge to sparsemax attention probabilities at equilibrium, and simulations show graceful degradation under non-ideal analog conditions.
conclusion: This work opens a path toward physical accelerators for transformer inference but is unrelated to quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Scalability And Performance Trade-offs Between Q-Learning And Parallel Intensified Simulated Annealing In Flexible Job Shop Scheduling
authors: Paul Corry Robert L Burdett
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article presents a controlled comparison of tabular Q-learning (QL) and Parallelized Simulated Annealing with Intensification (PISA) for the Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem (FJSP).
tldr: A controlled benchmark comparison of tabular Q-learning against a parallelized intensified simulated annealing algorithm for the Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem.
motivation: Scheduling problems such as FJSP are combinatorially hard, and practitioners need guidance on which heuristic or learning-based solvers scale best under practical time budgets.
method: The authors run a controlled head-to-head comparison of tabular Q-learning and Parallelized Simulated Annealing with Intensification (PISA) across FJSP instances, examining scalability and solution quality trade-offs.
result: The study characterizes how the two approaches differ in scaling behavior and performance as instance size and computational budget vary.
conclusion: The work offers empirical guidance for selecting between reinforcement learning and parallel metaheuristics for job shop scheduling, but remains entirely within classical operations research.

title: Hierarchical Sub-Array Beam Training For Flexible Intelligent Metasurface-Enabled Hybrid Near-Far-Field Multiuser Communications
authors: Qian Zhang, Yufei Zhao, Jiancheng An, Zheng Dong, Yong Liang Guan, Ju Liu, Chau Yuen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-resolution discrete phase shifters (PSs) are attractive for extremely large-scale arrays, but phase quantization distorts near-field (NF) beam patterns and degrades beam training and multiuser transmission. Moreover, the distinct codebook structures required by NF and far-field (FF) users complicate hybrid NF-FF beam training and codeword switching. To address these challenges, we introduce flexible intelligent metasurface (FIM) surface shaping as an additional geometric beamforming degree of freedom. We establish the hybrid NF-FF channel and beam pattern models, characterize the grating lobes induced by discrete PSs, and develop a phase-quantization compensation method. A deformation-range analysis shows that wavelength-scale shaping can achieve beam patterns comparable to those obtained with continuous PSs. We further propose a hierarchical sub-array beam training (HSABT) scheme that progressively doubles the activated central aperture according to the beam-width and beam-depth characteristics. A beam-intersection-based sampling strategy improves the angle-distance resolution, while a measurement-driven adaptive NF-FF beam-switching mechanism selects the final codeword without relying on the Rayleigh distance or prior user-location information. HSABT is also extended to multi-path channels through adaptive peak detection and inter-level energy-consistency-based candidate tracking. For high-gain multiuser transmission, we develop an alternating-optimization-based design and a complementary non-iterative key observation method, and analyze their convergence, computational complexity, and steady-point properties.Simulation results demonstrate continuous-phase-comparable beam patterns, reduced training overhead, more accurate main-path acquisition than exhaustive polar-codebook training, and higher multiuser sum rates than conventional rigid-array benchmarks.
tldr: The paper proposes hierarchical sub-array beam training for flexible intelligent metasurface-enabled hybrid near-field/far-field multiuser communications.
motivation: Low-resolution phase shifters distort near-field beam patterns and complicate hybrid near-field/far-field beam training, motivating additional geometric beamforming via flexible surface shaping.
method: The authors model hybrid near-far-field channels, characterize grating lobes from discrete phase shifters, develop phase-quantization compensation, and propose hierarchical sub-array beam training with adaptive near-far-field switching and multiuser alternating optimization.
result: Simulations show beam patterns comparable to continuous phase shifters, reduced training overhead, more accurate main-path acquisition than exhaustive polar-codebook training, and higher multiuser sum rates than rigid-array benchmarks.
conclusion: Flexible intelligent metasurface shaping and hierarchical beam training can mitigate phase quantization and improve near-far-field multiuser communication performance.

title: A Hybrid High-order Discretization Of A Volume Integral Formulation For Eddy Currents On Unstructured Polyhedral Meshes
authors: Raman Kumar, Aurelio Spadotto, Silvano Pitassi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Volume integral formulations are attractive for eddy-current simulation because they require a mesh only of the conducting region. However, their dense interaction matrices make it important to control the number of unknowns needed for a prescribed accuracy. We propose an arbitrary-order Hybrid High-Order discretization of a current-based volume integral formulation on general unstructured polyhedral meshes. The method combines high-order polynomial approximation with local mesh refinement around defects and material interfaces. For bounded positive spatially varying resistivity and magnetic permeability uniform throughout space, we establish well-posedness and a priori error estimates using a constructive right inverse of the discrete divergence. Numerical experiments demonstrate convergence for smooth solutions and compare mesh refinement with increasing the polynomial degree. Selected comparisons show that higher degree on coarser meshes can reduce the number of current unknowns coupled by the Green operator and the associated storage for a prescribed accuracy. Finally, a three-dimensional eddy-current testing benchmark assesses the predicted impedance against experimental measurements, using local refinement around a narrow slot and reusing the system matrix and its factorization throughout the probe scan.
tldr: The paper develops an arbitrary-order Hybrid High-Order discretization of a current-based volume integral formulation for eddy-current simulation on unstructured polyhedral meshes.
motivation: Volume integral methods for eddy currents only need to mesh the conducting region, but their dense interaction matrices make it essential to minimize the number of unknowns for a given accuracy.
method: The authors construct an arbitrary-order Hybrid High-Order scheme combining high-order polynomial approximation with local mesh refinement near defects and material interfaces, and prove well-posedness and a priori error estimates via a constructive right inverse of the discrete divergence.
result: Numerical experiments show convergence for smooth solutions, and comparisons indicate that higher polynomial degree on coarser meshes can reduce the number of current unknowns and associated Green-operator storage for prescribed accuracy; a 3D eddy-current testing benchmark matches measured impedance.
conclusion: The proposed HHO volume integral formulation offers a flexible, accurate and computationally economical approach to eddy-current simulation on general polyhedral meshes.

title: Stegoguard-lm: Evaluating End-to-End Protection Against Llm Covert Channels
authors: George Williams Martha Dimgba
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A defense that disrupts hidden messages may still provide little protection if its detector rarely triggers an intervention. We present StegoGuard-LM, a controlled framework for evaluating defenses against covert messages in large language model outputs. We examine token-rank and synonym channels, with Unicode concealment as a structural control, and track messages through detection, intervention, and recovery. Deterministic rewriting prevented full recovery of 103 of 104 synonym-encoded messages when applied unconditionally, but only one when intervention depended on a detector set to limit false alarms. In a four-round replay on a 48-response subset, an attacker selecting from a fixed catalog recovered more bits by switching channels, although paired gains were not statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Randomized rewriting showed no sustained advantage in this pilot. A more sensitive detector improved protection but modified about one-third of clean responses. These findings show how uneven detection can undermine effective rewriting and why protection must be evaluated alongside attacker adaptation and intervention on legitimate text.
tldr: StegoGuard-LM is a controlled evaluation framework for defenses against covert steganographic messages hidden in large language model outputs, tracking messages through detection, intervention, and recovery.
motivation: A defense that disrupts hidden messages provides little real protection if its detector rarely triggers, so end-to-end protection must be assessed jointly with detection reliability and attacker adaptation.
method: The authors compare token-rank and synonym covert channels (with Unicode concealment as a structural control), applying deterministic and randomized rewriting either unconditionally or gated by a detector, and measure message recovery across multiple rounds with a fixed attacker catalog.
result: Unconditional rewriting blocked full recovery of 103 of 104 synonym-encoded messages, but detector-gated intervention blocked only one; an adaptive attacker switching channels recovered more bits, though gains were not statistically significant after multiple-comparison correction, and a more sensitive detector protected better at the cost of altering about a third of clean responses.
conclusion: Uneven detection undermines rewriting-based protection, so covert-channel defenses must be evaluated alongside attacker adaptation and false-positive impact on legitimate text.

title: An LLM-Assisted Multi-Objective AutoML Framework For Efficient Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Ailin Barzegar, Khalil El-Khatib, Li Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional Machine Learning (ML)-based Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) require manual design, optimize only detection performance, and neglect inference latency and model size, which are critical for resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) and Electric Vehicle Charging System (EVCS) deployments. Automated ML (AutoML) reduces manual effort but explores broad search spaces inefficiently. Meanwhile, Multi-Objective Optimization (MOO) methods lack guided search initialization, leading to long search times. This paper proposes a Large Language Model-Assisted Multi-Objective Automated ML (LLM-MOO-AutoML) framework for efficient intrusion detection. A local Llama 3.1 8B model analyzes a compact dataset profile and generates a bounded, validated policy for automated data balancing (AutoDP) and feature engineering (AutoFE). This policy narrows the search space for Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III), which jointly optimizes the LightGBM feature-selection threshold and key hyperparameters across three objectives: maximizing weighted F1-score, minimizing 99th-percentile (P99) inference latency ratio, and minimizing model size ratio. Experiments on CICIDS2017, IoTID20, and CICEVSE2024 demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves the highest weighted F1-scores on CICIDS2017 (99.788%), IoTID20 (99.778%), and CICEVSE2024 (99.989%), with feature sets reduced to as few as 10 features, P99 latency as low as 0.00038 ms, and model size as small as 0.1073 MB. The LLM-guided configuration reduced NSGA-III search time relative to unconstrained multi-objective search on all datasets at the largest trial budget and in most comparisons at smaller budgets, indicating that dataset-aware search-space reduction supports efficient, deployment-aware intrusion detection.
tldr: An LLM-assisted multi-objective AutoML framework is proposed to build efficient, deployment-aware network intrusion detection models for IoT and EV charging systems.
motivation: Conventional ML-based IDSs require manual design, optimize only detection accuracy, and ignore inference latency and model size, which matter for resource-constrained IoT and EVCS deployments; existing AutoML and multi-objective methods search inefficiently without guided initialization.
method: A local Llama 3.1 8B model analyzes a compact dataset profile to generate a bounded, validated policy for automated data balancing (AutoDP) and feature engineering (AutoFE), narrowing the search space for NSGA-III, which jointly optimizes a LightGBM feature-selection threshold and hyperparameters across weighted F1, P99 inference-latency ratio, and model-size ratio.
result: Experiments on CICIDS2017, IoTID20, and CICEVSE2024 achieve weighted F1-scores of 99.788%, 99.778%, and 99.989% respectively, with feature sets as small as 10 features, P99 latency as low as 0.00038 ms, and model sizes as small as 0.1073 MB, while reducing NSGA-III search time.
conclusion: Dataset-aware search-space reduction via LLM-generated policies supports efficient, deployment-aware intrusion detection, though the work lies entirely in classical applied machine learning and cybersecurity.

title: When Being Wrong Is Right: Reverse-Capability Audio CAPTCHAs Through Psychoacoustic Design
authors: Mingjie Bao, Yu Dai, Guangke Chen, Guozhu Meng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) have recently been shown to bypass audio CAPTCHAs designed around limitations of automatic speech recognition. To address this threat, we introduce reverse-capability verification, a general CAPTCHA framework that reverses the conventional human-easy, machine-hard relationship with respect to the physical ground truth. It selects challenges in which stable human perceptual limitations cause the human-reference answer to differ from the physical ground truth, while machine analysis tends toward that truth. Because the verifier accepts the human-reference answer, advanced solver capabilities and resulting improved recovery of the physical ground truth may instead strengthen the human-machine separation. We instantiate the framework through psychoacoustics and design two audio CAPTCHAs: HIPI, a classification task, and YINGCHEN, a counting task, together with their conjunctive composition. Across seven LALMs and eight attack strategies, the maximum observed machine acceptance rates are 19%, 17%, and 3% for HIPI, YINGCHEN, and their composition, respectively, compared with 45-100% for nine prior schemes. A multidimensional human usability study yields corresponding human acceptance rates of 78%, 90%, and 76%, while maintaining competitive efficiency and satisfaction. Further analysis demonstrates that advanced LALMs tend toward physical ground truth. These results show that reverse-capability verification substantially reduces machine acceptance while retaining high human acceptance through an approach different from conventional CAPTCHAs.
tldr: The paper introduces 'reverse-capability verification,' a CAPTCHA framework exploiting stable human perceptual limitations so that correct human answers deliberately diverge from the physical ground truth, instantiated as two psychoacoustic audio CAPTCHAs (HIPI classification, YINGCHEN counting) that resist large audio-language models.
motivation: Large audio-language models can now bypass audio CAPTCHAs built on automatic-speech-recognition limitations, so a new verification paradigm is needed that keeps the task easy for humans but hard for machines even as machine perception improves.
method: The authors design challenges where psychoacoustic effects cause the human-perceived answer to differ from the physical signal ground truth, and the verifier accepts the human-reference answer; they evaluate HIPI, YINGCHEN, and their conjunction against seven LALMs under eight attack strategies plus a multidimensional human usability study.
result: Maximum machine acceptance rates were 19% (HIPI), 17% (YINGCHEN), and 3% (composition), versus 45–100% for nine prior schemes, while human acceptance reached 78%, 90%, and 76% with competitive efficiency and satisfaction; advanced LALMs were shown to trend toward the physical ground truth.
conclusion: Reverse-capability verification substantially lowers machine acceptance while retaining high human acceptance, offering a CAPTCHA design principle distinct from conventional human-easy/machine-hard approaches.

title: More Is Never Less: Affordable Robustness To Additive Attacks Via Monotone Multiple-Instance Learning
authors: Alexander Herzog, Shae Mcfadden, Lorenzo Cavallaro
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Static malware detectors that represent each sample as a bag of extracted features, such as permissions, API calls, or imported functions, are cheap to deploy and remain state-of-the-art under temporal drift and in selective classification. Yet, attackers can evade them by adding benign-looking content that outweighs malicious evidence. Canonically, detectors encode the presence of a few thousand features, selected during training, as sparse multi-hot vectors over a fixed vocabulary. Features that emerge after training remain invisible. We show that linear models and multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) over this input are sum-pooled set models in disguise. Sum-pooling lets added benign features cancel malicious evidence. Instead, we cast malware detection with set-shaped static features as a multiple-instance learning (MIL) problem. To this end, we propose MalSets, which uses max-pooled Deep Sets models with a monotone head to ensure that any malicious evidence remains undiluted; thus, more is never less. Under MIL, a general text encoder maps any feature string to an embedding, thus eliminating the long-standing out-of-vocabulary problem at test time. Max-pooling retains the malicious evidence regardless of how many benign features an attacker adds. Since max-pooling can only grow when features are added, constraining the head alone makes the malware score monotone under additions, even against a white-box attacker adapted to this architecture. While monotone detectors are never evaded by state-of-the-art black-box or white-box attacks, they often significantly pay for this robustness in clean performance since benign features cannot count as evidence. However, by combining a non-monotone set encoder with max-pooling and a monotone head, MalSets maintains the robustness of prior monotone classifiers while achieving state-of-the-art performance.
tldr: MalSets reframes static malware detection with set-valued features as monotone multiple-instance learning using max-pooled Deep Sets to make detectors provably robust to additive evasion attacks.
motivation: Sparse multi-hot detectors act as sum-pooled set models, so attackers can dilute malicious evidence by adding benign features; the authors seek architectures whose anomaly score cannot decrease under feature additions.
method: They cast malware detection as multiple-instance learning, using max-pooled Deep Sets with a monotone classification head and a general text encoder that maps arbitrary feature strings to embeddings, removing out-of-vocabulary limits; robustness is analyzed against white-box attackers.
result: Monotone max-pooled models resist state-of-the-art black-box and white-box additive attacks, and combining a non-monotone set encoder with max-pooling and a monotone head recovers state-of-the-art clean performance while retaining robustness.
conclusion: Monotonicity under feature addition provides an affordable, principled robustness guarantee for set-based malware classifiers without the usual clean-accuracy penalty.

title: It Pays To Brag? On Counterfactual Fair Credit
authors: Elchanan Mossel Ilan Doron-Arad
abstract: ArXiv:2611.29083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intellectual work, such as software, legal documents, and scientific results, typically builds on the work of others, and the same end product can often be obtained in several different ways. When assigning credit for such work, it is not clear whether credit should go according to the way the work was actually produced or also consider counterfactual ways of obtaining it. We study this question by generalizing Shapley values to account for counterfactual ways of obtaining the same result. We show that the fairness axioms of efficiency, nullity, and submodularity (in particular, additivity) are incompatible with incentivizing creators to maximize social welfare. In fact, fair credit can uniquely incentivize arbitrarily small welfare relative to the optimum. We also show that without submodularity, incentive compatibility is achievable, and that the four classical fairness axioms uniquely determine the Shapley value and prohibit dependence on counterfactual outcomes.
tldr: The paper generalizes Shapley values to counterfactual credit assignment and shows that classical fairness axioms conflict with incentivizing welfare-maximizing contributions.
motivation: Intellectual work builds on prior contributions and can often be produced in multiple ways, raising the question of whether credit should reflect the actual production path or also counterfactual alternatives.
method: The authors extend Shapley value theory with counterfactual outcomes and analyze compatibility of fairness axioms (efficiency, nullity, submodularity/additivity) with incentive compatibility via axiomatic and game-theoretic arguments.
result: Fair credit under the four classical axioms can uniquely incentivize arbitrarily small welfare relative to the optimum, while dropping submodularity restores incentive compatibility and the classical axioms uniquely pin down the Shapley value.
conclusion: Fairness and incentive compatibility are fundamentally in tension in credit allocation, and counterfactual dependence is ruled out by the standard axioms.

title: Spatial Ensemble Logic For Biomedical Imaging: Geometric Element Ensembles In Euclidean Space
authors: Guo-Qiang Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.29105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ensemble Logic (EL) is a family of modal logics over metric monoids whose modal parameters are terms with quantified variables. We study its member over the Euclidian space, called Spatial Ensemble Logic (SEL), for biomedical images. Geometric element ensembles (GELs) represent atomic propositions by finite lists of effectively presented semi-algebraic sets, principally closed balls. Translation, dilation and erosion preserve individual balls up to emptiness in any dimension. Translation and dilation act element-wise, but element-wise erosion gives only an inner bound. For [MATH], finite unions of balls are closed under neither intersection nor erosion. We therefore separate record representation from the evaluation domain. Our main result is a satisfaction-preserving translation over GELs into the first-order theory of real closed fields. It yields computable semi-algebraic satisfaction sets, decidable model checking and finite real algebraic evidence. For a fixed formula and dimension, model checking has polynomial data complexity under stated rationality and bounded-degree assumptions. Combined complexity is PSPACE-hard and in EXPSPACE. On the line, rational interval data admit linear-arithmetic evaluation with rational evidence, under rationality assumptions on the norm, query and evaluation point. For [MATH], rational balls can force irrational witnesses. Lower and upper annotation bounds propagate through formulas. Synthesis of a ball ensemble is decidable within a prescribed budget of balls and undecidable without one. In a vascular use case, medial ball ensembles decide calibre and stenosis queries at stored centers by comparing stored numbers. We also examine how far evaluation can proceed element-wise when the union forming a support is deferred to the point of evaluation.
tldr: The paper introduces Spatial Ensemble Logic (SEL), a modal logic over metric monoids whose atomic propositions are finite ensembles of semi-algebraic sets (mainly closed balls), applied to biomedical image queries.
motivation: Biomedical imaging queries about geometric structures (e.g., vessel calibre, stenosis) require a formal, decidable logical framework for reasoning over geometric element ensembles in Euclidean space.
method: The authors separate record representation from the evaluation domain and give a satisfaction-preserving translation of GEL formulas into the first-order theory of real closed fields, yielding computable semi-algebraic satisfaction sets, then analyze model-checking complexity.
result: Model checking is decidable with polynomial data complexity for fixed formulas and dimension (with rationality/bounded-degree assumptions), combined complexity is PSPACE-hard and in EXPSPACE, ball-ensemble synthesis is decidable only with a prescribed budget, and a vascular use case demonstrates calibre/stenosis decisions from stored medial-ball data.
conclusion: SEL provides a rigorous, computable logical foundation for geometric reasoning in biomedical imaging, with tight complexity characterizations and practical query evaluation for vascular analysis.

title: Covering Hypercubic Grids By Polygonal Trails: Capacity Bounds And The Optimum For $p(4,3)$
authors: Marco Rip\`a Aldo Roberto Pessolano
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical nine-dot puzzle asks for a polygonal trail through a square grid using as few segments as possible. We study its higher-dimensional analogue on [MATH] for integers [MATH], allowing arbitrary real vertices and unrestricted segment directions, and denote the minimum number of segments by [MATH]. For [MATH] and [MATH], we give a geometric proof of the previously stated capacity bound: a trail of [MATH] segments meets at most [MATH] grid points. Refinements of this bound, combined with exhaustive finite checks, establish [MATH] and [MATH]. We also exhibit a [MATH]-segment trail through [MATH] points of [MATH], the maximum possible, and a [MATH]-segment covering trail contained in [MATH], which settles the corresponding box-constrained problem. The general capacity theorem, a large-grid lower bound refuting a previously proposed formula for [MATH], and the boxed construction are verified by the Lean 4 kernel, whereas the finite exclusions use native reflection and additionally trust the native compiler and runtime. A companion technical note provides the computational specification and reproducible proof artifacts.
tldr: A pure combinatorics/geometry paper on the higher-dimensional generalization of the nine-dot puzzle, determining the minimum number of straight segments needed to cover all points of a hypercubic grid, with proofs formalized in Lean 4.
motivation: The classical nine-dot puzzle asks for the fewest segments in a polygonal trail covering a square grid; the authors extend this to integer hypercubes in arbitrary dimension with unrestricted real-valued vertices and directions.
method: Geometric proof of a capacity bound (a trail of k segments hits at most a bounded number of grid points), refined bounds supplemented by exhaustive finite computer checks, explicit constructions, and machine verification of the main theorems in the Lean 4 proof assistant.
result: The authors establish p(4,3) and related values, exhibit a 2n-2 segment trail covering the maximum number of points of the 3x...x3 grid, give a box-constrained covering trail, prove a large-grid lower bound refuting a previously proposed formula, and verify the capacity theorem via Lean 4.
conclusion: The work settles several discrete-geometry covering problems and demonstrates formal verification of combinatorial geometry results, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Density Regularity From Derivative Growth Of Cauchy-Type Integrals
authors: Oleksandr Volkov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the relationship between the behavior of the derivative of a Cauchy-type integral near the curve of integration and the regularity of its density. We consider Jordan curves and Jordan arcs composed of finitely many regular [MATH] arcs meeting at nondegenerate angles. For a Cauchy-type integral with continuous density, we establish an inverse estimate: if the growth of its derivative off the curve is controlled by a continuous integrable function of the distance to the curve that is nonincreasing near zero, then the modulus of continuity of the density at scale [MATH] is bounded by the integral of this majorant over [MATH]. As a consequence, we prove that power-law decay of the derivative as the curve is approached forces the density to be constant. For Jordan curves, combining the inverse and direct estimates yields a criterion for H\"older continuity of the density in terms of the growth of the derivative of the integral. We then apply this criterion to characterize the H\"older regularity of analytic functions in bounded Jordan domains whose boundaries satisfy the same geometric assumptions. The proof relies on uniformly transverse shifts of local subarcs and a symmetric jump formula.
tldr: The paper studies how derivative growth of Cauchy-type integrals near Jordan curves controls the regularity of their densities.
motivation: It aims to characterize density regularity, including Hölder continuity and constancy, from the boundary behavior of Cauchy-type integral derivatives.
method: The proof uses uniformly transverse shifts of local subarcs and a symmetric jump formula for Cauchy-type integrals on piecewise regular Jordan curves and arcs.
result: The authors derive inverse estimates bounding the modulus of continuity of the density by an integral of the derivative majorant, show power-law derivative decay forces constant density, and obtain a Hölder continuity criterion.
conclusion: The criterion is applied to characterize Hölder regularity of analytic functions in bounded Jordan domains under geometric assumptions on the boundary.

title: Sharp $s$-nice Recurrence Without The Van Der Corput Property
authors: Sohail Farhangi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every real [MATH], we construct a set [MATH] which is a set of [MATH]-nice measurable recurrence exactly for [MATH] and is not a van der Corput set. The new ingredient of this construction is the Density Frankl--R\"odl theorem. Furthermore, the probability measure [MATH] which witnesses failure of the van der Corput property has an atom at zero with mass [MATH]. A Gaussian tail argument proves both sharpness of the recurrence exponent and the fact that this atom is the largest possible for any [MATH]-nice recurrent set. The result sharpens the recurrence separations of Bourgain and Mountakis, answers a question of Mountakis about the maximal mass of an atom at zero, and answers a question of Forrest about separating the various degrees of nice recurrence. In the appendix we give a self-contained proof of the Density Frankl-R\"odl theorem.
tldr: The paper constructs s-nice recurrent sets that fail the van der Corput property and establishes sharp bounds on the recurrence exponent and the maximal atom at zero.
motivation: It aims to sharpen known separations of recurrence notions and answer questions by Mountakis and Forrest concerning s-nice recurrence and van der Corput sets.
method: The construction uses the Density Frankl-Rödl theorem, together with a Gaussian tail argument to prove sharpness and optimality of the atom at zero.
result: For every real s, the authors obtain a set that is s-nice measurable recurrence exactly for that s, is not a van der Corput set, and has an optimal atom at zero in the witnessing measure.
conclusion: The work advances ergodic theory and additive combinatorics by providing sharp recurrence/van der Corput separations and a self-contained appendix proof of the Density Frankl-Rödl theorem.

title: Multi-location Newsvendor: An Interpretable Inventory Policy
authors: Vineet Goyal Soufiane Fafe
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a multilocation newsvendor problem in which inventory is chosen before demand is observed and surplus stock can subsequently be transshipped to locations with shortages. The objective is to minimize expected holding, backlog, and transportation costs over a metric network. Under uniform transportation costs, the optimality conditions balance local and aggregate demand coverage and reduce to a scalar search under mild regularity conditions. We use this structure to develop an interpretable iterative heuristic for general metrics. The heuristic calibrates effective transportation costs from lateral shipments under independent stocking and uses them to construct location-dependent pooling weights. These weights have a direct operational interpretation through the cost of serving demand at other locations. Under the stated assumptions, the heuristic recovers the exact uniform-metric solution. Numerical experiments on structured and random networks show costs close to the sampled optimum on average and substantial savings relative to independent stocking.
tldr: The paper develops an interpretable heuristic inventory policy for a multi-location newsvendor problem with lateral transshipment under a metric network.
motivation: Multi-location inventory management must balance local and aggregate demand coverage while accounting for holding, backlog, and transportation costs, and practical policies need to be interpretable and near-optimal.
method: The authors derive optimality conditions for uniform transportation costs that reduce to a scalar search, then use this structure to build an iterative heuristic that calibrates effective transportation costs and location-dependent pooling weights for general metrics.
result: The heuristic recovers the exact uniform-metric solution under stated assumptions and achieves costs close to the sampled optimum on average in numerical experiments, with substantial savings relative to independent stocking.
conclusion: The proposed policy provides an interpretable and effective approach to multi-location inventory transshipment, bridging exact structural insights and practical heuristic performance.

title: Numerical Approximation Of The Hilfer Fractional Derivative Using Orthogonal Quasi-Polynomials
authors: Swaminathan Anbhu Rabab Beirkdar
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A numerical approach based on a composite Gaussian quadrature for the Hilfer fractional derivative is presented. This approach employs quasi-polynomials that are orthogonal with respect to the weight function on the interval [MATH]. As special cases, the Riemann--Liouville and Caputo fractional derivatives are obtained. Error bounds for the approximation are derived. To confirm the convergence rates as well as the high efficiency of the new approach, numerical examples are provided.
tldr: This paper develops a composite Gaussian quadrature scheme based on orthogonal quasi-polynomials to numerically approximate the Hilfer fractional derivative, with derived error bounds and numerical validation.
motivation: Fractional derivatives such as the Hilfer derivative generalize Riemann-Liouville and Caputo operators but lack efficient, accurate numerical schemes with rigorous convergence guarantees.
method: The authors construct orthogonal quasi-polynomials with respect to a weight function on an interval and use them within a composite Gaussian quadrature rule to discretize the Hilfer fractional derivative, deriving error bounds for the approximation.
result: Riemann-Liouville and Caputo derivatives emerge as special cases, and numerical examples confirm the predicted convergence rates and high computational efficiency of the scheme.
conclusion: The proposed orthogonal quasi-polynomial quadrature offers an accurate and efficient numerical tool for Hilfer-type fractional derivatives, though it lies entirely outside quantum information science.

title: Well-balanced Nodal Finite Volume Weno Scheme With Flux Localization For Hyperbolic Balance Laws
authors: Jiahui Zhang, Yinhua Xia, Yan Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a general framework for constructing arbitrarily high-order well-balanced ``nodal" finite volume weighted essentially non-oscillatory (WENO) schemes, specifically tailored for hyperbolic balance laws. To handle complex systems involving nonconservative products and steady-state solutions with global integral quantities, we introduce a flux localization technique. This technique defines the numerical fluxes, incorporating the entire source term and nonconservative products, locally within each computational cell. By exactly preserving the nodal equilibrium state and conservatively updating the cell averages within a finite volume framework, the method avoids both reference-state reconstruction and the use of ODE solvers. The well-balanced property is achieved by performing high-order WENO reconstruction and employing a linear segment path in terms of equilibrium variables, rather than conservative ones. A rigorous theoretical analysis confirms that the scheme exactly preserves all the targeted stationary solutions. The effectiveness and versatility of the proposed method are demonstrated through a series of numerical experiments on various systems of hyperbolic balance laws.
tldr: The authors construct arbitrarily high-order well-balanced nodal finite volume WENO schemes for hyperbolic balance laws using a flux localization technique that embeds source terms and nonconservative products directly into cell-local numerical fluxes.
motivation: Standard well-balanced schemes for hyperbolic balance laws with nonconservative products typically require reference-state reconstruction, ODE solvers, or careful source-term balancing, which complicates high-order accuracy and exact preservation of general steady states with global integral quantities.
method: A flux localization technique defines numerical fluxes locally within each cell including the full source term and nonconservative products, enabling exact preservation of nodal equilibrium states and conservative cell-average updates; high-order WENO reconstruction is performed on equilibrium variables along a linear segment path to guarantee the well-balanced property analytically.
result: A rigorous theoretical analysis shows the scheme exactly preserves all targeted stationary solutions, and numerical experiments on several systems of hyperbolic balance laws demonstrate accuracy, well-balancing, and versatility.
conclusion: The framework yields arbitrarily high-order, well-balanced nodal finite volume WENO schemes without reference-state reconstruction or ODE solvers, applicable to a broad class of hyperbolic balance laws with nonconservative products.

title: Coordinate Ordering And Non-collinear Central Configurations
authors: Lei Zhao Jiexin Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a mass-independent criterion for N-body central configurations based on a special coordinate ordering of the bodies. Moreover, we identify a region in the plane that contains no non-collinear central configurations. This provides a way to exclude non-collinear central configurations that are nearly collinear.
tldr: The paper gives a mass-independent criterion for N-body central configurations using coordinate ordering and identifies a region containing no non-collinear central configurations.
motivation: Central configurations are a classical topic in celestial mechanics, and excluding nearly collinear non-collinear configurations is useful for classifying N-body equilibria.
method: The authors introduce a special coordinate ordering of the bodies and derive a mass-independent criterion, then use it to identify a forbidden region in the plane.
result: They establish a criterion for central configurations and find a region in which no non-collinear central configurations can exist, helping rule out nearly collinear cases.
conclusion: The work provides a geometric/ordering-based tool for excluding certain non-collinear central configurations in classical N-body problems.

title: Weight-Space Backdoors In Open-Weight LLMs: Cross-Architecture Attacks And Blind Model Forensics
authors: Mohammed Tanveer
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-weight language models are vulnerable to trigger-conditioned behaviors introduced through sparse post-training weight modifications, creating supply-chain risks beyond conventional provenance checks. We present Neural Sentinel, a cross-architecture study of gradient-guided backdoor insertion and model forensics spanning 18 checkpoints across 14 architecture families (124M-31.3B parameters), including state-space and recurrent models. On Phi-2, modifying approximately 0.0002% of parameters induced an exact short-marker output after 300 steps (332 seconds), with mean next-token KL divergence of [MATH] and 100% top-1 agreement over evaluated positions of eight fixed reference prompts. Separate experiments produced structured tool-call-formatted outputs without establishing downstream execution. We identify three procedure-dependent response regimes -- Gradient-Permeable, Scale-Threshold, and Gradient-Fragmented -- and evaluate PPO-based weight-space exploration, which showed no statistically significant advantage over random search. For defense, Neural Sentinel combines weight-difference analysis, trigger discovery, activation probing, and contextual output inspection. In a 22-artifact development cohort, its reference-optional scanner classified 4/5 backdoored artifacts as BACKDOORED; the remaining positive and all 17 clean artifacts were SUSPICIOUS. These findings establish the feasibility of sparse conditional-output insertion and evidence-producing forensic triage, while identifying limitations in behavioral-drift assessment and clean-model admission.
tldr: Neural Sentinel is a cross-architecture study of gradient-guided backdoor insertion into open-weight LLMs and a corresponding forensic triage pipeline to detect such weight-space tampering.
motivation: Open-weight model distribution creates supply-chain risks because sparse post-training weight modifications can implant trigger-conditioned behaviors that provenance checks cannot catch.
method: The authors insert backdoors via gradient-guided sparse weight edits across 18 checkpoints spanning 14 architecture families (124M-31.3B), compare PPO-based weight-space exploration against random search, and build a defense combining weight-difference analysis, trigger discovery, activation probing, and output inspection.
result: Modifying ~0.0002% of Phi-2 parameters produced exact marker outputs in 300 steps, three procedure-dependent response regimes were identified, PPO gave no significant advantage over random search, and the scanner flagged 4/5 backdoored artifacts correctly while mislabeling all clean artifacts as SUSPICIOUS.
conclusion: Sparse conditional-output insertion in LLM weights is feasible and forensic triage can produce evidence, but behavioral-drift assessment and clean-model admission remain open limitations.

title: Anti Os Fingerprinting, Revisited: A Loadable Kernel Module For FreeBSD And What Twenty-Five Years Changed
authors: Daisuke Miyamoto
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2001 we published a paper on an Anti OS Detection (AoD) system: a modified FreeBSD 4.3 kernel that makes a host answer the probes of an OS fingerprinting tool as if it ran another operating system. This report revisits that work on FreeBSD 15.1. We do not claim a new method. We report three things. First, the same goal is now reachable from a loadable module of about 800 lines that uses the packet filter hook interface and sets one kernel variable, without changing the kernel source. Second, the module covers both active and passive fingerprinting: Nmap 7.98 reports an exact match for Linux and for Windows 10/11, and p0f 3 reports the same systems from the connections the host opens. Third, an exact match in Nmap was not enough: a passive tool, plain FIN scans and a comparison with real hosts each exposed a mismatch that the previous step could not see. A real Windows 11 host and the final Windows personality get the same verdict from Nmap and the same signatures from p0f and JA4T; a real Linux 7.0 host is not an exact match in Nmap at all, while the personality built from Nmap's database is. We describe those mismatches, how we removed them, what the module costs, and what it still cannot hide.
tldr: The paper revisits an anti-OS-fingerprinting system by implementing it as a loadable FreeBSD kernel module and evaluating active and passive fingerprint evasion.
motivation: The original 2001 anti-OS-detection work required kernel modifications; the author aims to modernize the approach using FreeBSD 15.1's packet filter hooks without changing kernel source.
method: A roughly 800-line loadable kernel module uses the packet filter hook interface and sets a kernel variable to alter host responses to fingerprinting probes, covering active and passive fingerprinting.
result: Nmap 7.98 reports exact matches for Linux and Windows 10/11 personalities, and p0f 3 reports the same systems passively, though further passive checks, FIN scans, and real-host comparisons reveal remaining mismatches.
conclusion: The module achieves the original anti-OS-detection goal with less invasive implementation, but exact active fingerprint matches do not guarantee full evasion across passive and scan-based detection methods.

title: Layered Soft-output Mlse Architecture For Pam4 Short-reach Optical Interconnects
authors: Mengqi Guo, Ji Zhou, Zhengxiang Cheng, Changyuan Yu, Xiangjun Xin, Liangchuan Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of data traffic driven by artificial intelligence demands high-speed data-center optical interconnects, where soft-output maximum-likelihood sequence estimation (SMLSE) provides reliability information for soft-decision forward error correction. However, conventional SMLSE suffers from a latency bottleneck because sequential state-metric recursions cause latency to increase linearly with the number of symbols. Here, we propose a layered SMLSE architecture that reduces latency from linear to logarithmic order. Downward branch-metric accumulation combines adjacent interval metrics in parallel, while upward state-metric propagation reconstructs forward and backward state metrics at successive interval midpoints. Experiments with 112-Gbit/s PAM4 transmission over 2-km standard single-mode fiber demonstrate identical soft-output performance for layered and conventional SMLSE, while the total latency decreases from 26 to 10 processing cycles. The proposed layered SMLSE provides a low-latency architecture while preserving soft-output performance for high-speed optical interconnects.
tldr: The paper proposes a layered soft-output MLSE architecture that reduces processing latency for PAM4 short-reach optical interconnects from linear to logarithmic order.
motivation: High-speed data-center optical interconnects require soft-decision forward error correction, but conventional SMLSE has a latency bottleneck due to sequential state-metric recursion.
method: A layered SMLSE architecture accumulates branch metrics downward in parallel and propagates state metrics upward to reconstruct forward and backward metrics at interval midpoints.
result: In 112-Gbit/s PAM4 transmission over 2 km standard single-mode fiber, the layered SMLSE matches conventional soft-output performance while reducing total latency from 26 to 10 processing cycles.
conclusion: The layered architecture provides low-latency soft-output equalization for high-speed optical interconnects without sacrificing performance.

title: Accelerating Wave-scattering Simulations With Learned Search Directions
authors: Haoran Sun, Tao Shan, Hongyu Zhou, Rui Guo, Shenheng Xu, Fan Yang, Maokun Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wave-scattering simulation requires solving a dense boundary-element system for every frequency, incidence and design. Krylov solvers build each search space from scratch, and it grows with problem size. Here we present BEMFormer, a solver that learns to generate search directions across systems of one integral equation and supplies geometry-specific directions through a coarse-grid correction. BEMFormer generalizes to unseen geometries, meshes and excitations, and to acoustic scattering after fine-tuning on eight geometries. It reproduces the measured radar cross-sections of benchmark targets. On a quadcopter with 1.04 million unknowns, 38 times the largest training problem, BEMFormer solves each system 30 times faster than a preconditioned Krylov solver. Both reach a radar cross-section deviation of about 1 dB, comparable to the difference between independent measurements and acceptable for engineering applications. These results show that solving million-unknown scattering problems in minutes is possible when the search space is learned rather than built from scratch.
tldr: BEMFormer learns to generate Krylov search directions for boundary-element wave-scattering simulations, solving million-unknown systems roughly 30x faster than preconditioned Krylov solvers.
motivation: Classical iterative solvers rebuild their Krylov search space from scratch for every frequency, incidence angle, and design, and the cost grows with problem size, making large-scale scattering simulation expensive.
method: The authors train a model that learns geometry-specific search directions across systems sharing one integral equation, and supply these directions through a coarse-grid correction that generalizes to unseen geometries, meshes, excitations, and (after fine-tuning) acoustic scattering.
result: On a quadcopter with 1.04 million unknowns (38x the largest training problem), BEMFormer solves each system 30 times faster than a preconditioned Krylov solver while both reach about 1 dB radar-cross-section deviation, matching benchmark measurements.
conclusion: Learning the search space rather than constructing it from scratch enables million-unknown scattering problems to be solved in minutes, with accuracy adequate for engineering applications.

title: Every Friend Of 10 Has At Least Eleven Distinct Prime Factors
authors: Filip Fifka
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A friend of [MATH] is a positive integer [MATH] such that [MATH]. Whether one exists is an open problem. Thackeray proved that a friend of [MATH] has at least [MATH] distinct prime factors. We describe a computer-assisted proof that it has at least [MATH]. The proof is an exhaustive search over sets of primes, carried out by a recursive certifier written in PARI/GP, which extends the open-source project caioross/solitary10. The new ingredients are a split of ``almost tight'' nodes that avoids enumerating the smallest unknown prime, a treatment of nodes with three or more unknown primes by a saturation dichotomy, a counting rule for unfactored cofactors of cyclotomic values, and the correction of a soundness gap in the earlier closure rule. The certification run for [MATH] visited [MATH] nodes in [MATH] hours on [MATH] threads. As a consequence, a friend of [MATH] would be larger than [MATH].
tldr: A computer-assisted exhaustive search proves that any 'friend of 10' (a number n with aliquot sum equal to 10) must have at least eleven distinct prime factors.
motivation: Whether a friend of 10 exists is an open problem; Thackeray previously established a lower bound of ten distinct prime factors, and strengthening this bound constrains the search space and pushes any hypothetical solution to enormous magnitudes.
method: The author performs a recursive exhaustive search over sets of primes using a certifier written in PARI/GP, extending the caioross/solitary10 project, with new techniques including splitting of almost-tight nodes, a saturation dichotomy for nodes with three or more unknown primes, a counting rule for unfactored cofactors of cyclotomic values, and a correction of a soundness gap in the prior closure rule.
result: The certification run visited a large number of nodes over many hours across multiple threads, establishing that a friend of 10 has at least eleven distinct prime factors, which implies any such number exceeds a stated enormous bound.
conclusion: The strengthened lower bound substantially narrows the remaining search space for the open problem, and the corrected and extended certification framework provides a reusable tool for further computational number-theory searches.

title: An ADMM-Based Approach To The Large-Scale Geomagnetically Induced Current Blocker Placement Problem
authors: Minseok Ryu, Arthur Barnes, Russell Bent, Adam Mate, Jose Tabarez
