abstract: ArXiv:2611.28578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM)-based approach for addressing the challenge of determining placements for geomagnetically induced current (GIC) blocking devices on large-scale transmission networks. Traditional formulations of this placement problem lead to mixed-integer nonlinear programs (MINLPs) that are difficult for state-of-the-art MINLP solvers, which often struggle to exploit problem structure and fail to produce high-quality solutions on large systems. To overcome these challenges, the proposed method employs a three-block ADMM decomposition enhanced with (i) partial linearization of the GIC-related nonlinearities, supported by conditions guaranteeing exactness, and (ii) heterogeneous penalty parameters that significantly accelerate convergence to high-quality local solutions. Numerical experiments on newly constructed large-scale benchmark systems (up to 10,000 buses) demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods by several orders of magnitude in runtime while producing solutions whose objective values closely approach the ideal all-blocker lower bound. These results highlight the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed approach for mitigation planning efforts in large transmission networks.
tldr: The paper develops a three-block ADMM decomposition algorithm with partial linearization and heterogeneous penalty parameters to solve large-scale geomagnetically induced current (GIC) blocker placement problems on transmission networks.
motivation: GIC blocker placement is naturally formulated as a mixed-integer nonlinear program that state-of-the-art MINLP solvers cannot scale to realistic transmission networks, so a structure-exploiting decomposition is needed.
method: The authors propose a three-block ADMM scheme with partial linearization of GIC-related nonlinearities (with exactness conditions) and heterogeneous penalty parameters to accelerate convergence to high-quality local solutions.
result: On newly constructed benchmarks up to 10,000 buses, the method outperforms existing approaches by orders of magnitude in runtime while approaching the ideal all-blocker lower bound on objective value.
conclusion: The approach offers a scalable tool for mitigation planning in large transmission networks, though it addresses power-systems optimization rather than quantum information science.

title: Structure-preserving Active Flux Method For The Compressible Euler Equations With Gravity
authors: Christian Klingenberg Jiahui Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a structure-preserving active flux method for the compressible Euler equations under gravitational fields, ensuring exactness for the generalized hydrostatic equilibrium state and the preservation of positivity for both density and pressure. This approach entails the update of the cell average and the point values simultaneously. To obtain the equilibrium preservation of the scheme for the cell average, the strategy pursued is to reformulate the gravitational term using the steady state solution, followed by the application of a decomposition algorithm. For the point values, we introduce minor adjustments to the Lax-Friedrichs flux vector splitting, coupled with the same finite difference operator performed on the flux and source term to restore the well-balancedness. Furthermore, a posteriori Multi-dimensional Optimal Order Detection (MOOD) paradigm is adopted for achieving positivity preservation and oscillation control near strong discontinuities. A series of numerical experiments are performed to verify the high-order accuracy of our proposed method, along with its exact equilibrium and positivity preservation, and its ability to capture small perturbations at or close to steady flow without spurious oscillations.
tldr: The paper introduces a structure-preserving active flux method for compressible Euler equations with gravity that exactly preserves generalized hydrostatic equilibrium and positivity of density and pressure.
motivation: Numerical schemes for compressible Euler equations under gravity must handle near-equilibrium flows without spurious oscillations while maintaining physical positivity constraints.
method: The method updates cell averages and point values simultaneously, reformulates the gravitational source term using the steady-state solution for well-balancedness, adjusts Lax-Friedrichs flux splitting, and applies a posteriori MOOD for positivity and oscillation control.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order accuracy, exact equilibrium preservation, positivity preservation, and the ability to capture small perturbations near steady flow without spurious oscillations.
conclusion: The proposed active flux method provides a robust structure-preserving numerical framework for gravitational Euler flows, though it is unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Quantity-Level Fdia In SDR-Based P2p Energy Trading: Cyber-Economic Impact And Pre-Clearing Detection
authors: Razane Tajeddine Wassim Sarrieddine
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the cyber-economic impact and pre-clearing detectability of false data injection attacks (FDIAs) in peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading among interconnected microgrids. In the proposed cyber-economic framework, load and photovoltaic profiles drive a sequential 15-minute market with deterministic double-sided proportional (pro-rata) allocation and supply-to-demand-ratio (SDR) pricing, while true physical injections are separated from communicated market quantities. The framework is evaluated through a multi-microgrid case study over 69,904 market-aligned states, for which all AC power-flow solutions converged and voltages remained within 0.98999-1.04369 per unit. Healthy local exchange reached 1,159.66 MWh and generated USD 92,772.62 of community benefit. Bias, scaling, and ramp attacks modify only one microgrid's communicated quantity, altering the settlement price, P2P allocation, scheduled residual-grid exchange, participant financial outcomes, and benefit fairness, while true feeder injections remain unchanged. Role-specific random forest, statistical threshold, and score-fusion detectors are compared using only information available before clearing. Pooled sample-level detection rates range from 7.82% to 12.14%, with false-alarm rates from 4.69% to 7.70% and role dependence. In the investigated case study, measurable downstream economic distortion and low pre-clearing detectability coexist under bounded quantity manipulation.
tldr: The paper analyzes false data injection attacks on peer-to-peer energy trading among microgrids, quantifying their economic impact and showing that pre-clearing detectors achieve only low detection rates.
motivation: P2P energy trading markets rely on communicated quantities that may diverge from physical injections, creating an attack surface whose economic consequences and detectability are not well characterized.
method: A cyber-economic framework with 15-minute sequential markets, pro-rata allocation and supply-to-demand-ratio pricing is simulated over 69,904 market states in a multi-microgrid case study, with bias, scaling and ramp attacks evaluated against random-forest, threshold and score-fusion detectors.
result: Attacks altered settlement prices, allocations and benefit fairness while physical feeder injections stayed unchanged; pooled detection rates were 7.82%–12.14% with 4.69%–7.70% false alarms and strong role dependence.
conclusion: Bounded quantity manipulation can produce measurable economic distortion with low pre-clearing detectability, motivating better market-side anomaly detection.

title: Enabling Verifiable Output Lineage For Virtualized Ml Workload Execution
authors: Prach Chantasantitam, Adam Caulfield, Sujaya Maiyya, N. Asokan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning (ML) property attestation lets a model provider demonstrate properties of their models and datasets to verifiers, and trusted execution environments (TEEs) have emerged as its most practical mechanism. However, existing TEE-based systems attest only a static snapshot of the TEE's initial configuration, leaving run-time behavior unauditable. Proof of execution (PoX) architectures close this gap by requiring the prover's root of trust to also demonstrate that (1) the attested operation actually executed and (2) the claimed outputs were affected only by that operation. Existing PoX designs, though, target microcontrollers and rely on hardware features unavailable in server-grade TEEs, so they cannot be applied directly to ML workloads. We present EVOLVE, a software-based PoX framework for server-grade TEEs. EVOLVE mediates an operation's writes and control flow to track whether a requested ML operation executes without violation. It binds the execution status to measurements of the operation's inputs and outputs, enabling verifiers to assess run-time behavior through ML property attestation. We implement EVOLVE on Intel TDX as a Rust module within its virtual firmware, with policy checks built on primitives formally verified in F*. Our evaluation shows that EVOLVE is versatile across diverse ML applications on unmodified hardware, provides formal guarantees for its policy checks. EVOLVE incurs per-request run-time overhead on average ranging from 1.07[MATH] (for decision trees) to 2.13[MATH] (for multi-layer perceptrons).
tldr: EVOLVE is a software-based proof-of-execution framework for server-grade TEEs that enables verifiable run-time lineage for ML workload outputs.
motivation: Existing TEE-based ML property attestation only verifies static initial configuration, leaving run-time behavior and output lineage unauditable; existing proof-of-execution designs target microcontrollers and do not work on server-grade TEEs.
method: The authors implement EVOLVE on Intel TDX as a Rust module in virtual firmware, mediating writes and control flow to track whether requested ML operations execute without violation and binding execution status to input/output measurements, with policy checks built on F*-verified primitives.
result: EVOLVE is versatile across diverse ML applications on unmodified hardware, provides formal guarantees for policy checks, and incurs average per-request overhead ranging from 1.07x for decision trees to 2.13x for multi-layer perceptrons.
conclusion: EVOLVE closes the run-time auditability gap for TEE-based ML attestation by providing verifiable output lineage, though it is not related to quantum information science or the user's research directions.

title: Reimbursement As A Revenue Instrument In Costly Clock Auctions
authors: Miriam Nelson (independent Researcher), Jack Stanick (boston College), Edwin Lock (king's College London), Francisco Marmolejo-Coss\'{\i}o
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bidders in an ascending auction may incur a cost each time they choose to continue, for example when bidding requires a blockchain transaction. We therefore investigate whether a seller can increase net revenue by reimbursing these costs, and how reimbursements should be distributed across auction rounds. We study auctions in which bidders must actively confirm their participation as prices rise and the seller commits to reimbursements before bidding begins. We first show how a linear program can find the cheapest payments that keep bidders' strategies optimal when participation costs are introduced. Maximizing net revenue, however, can require changing those strategies. In a two-bidder example, we identify conditions under which reimbursing only the last scheduled decision earns the most net revenue among the schedules we analyze. This policy outperforms no reimbursement, full reimbursement, and the cheapest policy that maintains the original strategies. Some auctions end earlier than under full reimbursement, but the seller's savings exceed the resulting loss in sale receipts. Experiments with learning bidders reproduce these revenue comparisons. In a four-bidder example, they also identify a policy with partial reimbursements in earlier rounds that earns more than reimbursing only the final decision. These results show how the seller's preferred reimbursement timing can change across auction environments. Finally, we explain how requiring bidders to confirm continued participation limits the prices they can be charged when messages are missing, and discuss the requirements for implementing these auctions on a blockchain.
tldr: This paper studies whether and how a seller in a costly ascending (clock) auction can increase net revenue by reimbursing bidders' participation costs, and how to schedule those reimbursements across auction rounds.
motivation: In ascending auctions where continuing to bid incurs real costs (e.g., blockchain transaction fees), sellers may improve net revenue by subsidizing participation, but the optimal timing and distribution of reimbursements is unclear.
method: The authors formulate a linear program to compute the cheapest reimbursements preserving bidders' optimal strategies, then analyze revenue-maximizing policies that may deliberately alter bidder strategies, using two- and four-bidder examples plus experiments with learning bidders.
result: Reimbursing only the last scheduled decision can maximize net revenue in the two-bidder setting, outperforming no reimbursement, full reimbursement, and the cheapest strategy-preserving policy; in a four-bidder example, partial early-round reimbursement can do even better.
conclusion: The seller's preferred reimbursement timing depends on the auction environment, and requiring active confirmation of continued participation constrains chargeable prices when messages are missing, with implications for blockchain implementation.

title: SoK: Splitting The Trigger Or Adding Attackers? Disentangling Distributed Backdoor Attacks In Federated Learning
authors: Zhuotao Lian, Qingkui Zeng, Weiyu Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed backdoor attacks split a trigger among several federated learning clients, so that the backdoor appears only in the aggregated model. Since DBA, a line of work has reported that such attacks are stronger, more persistent, and stealthier than a single attacker with the full trigger. We systematize this literature and test this belief. We code nineteen primary studies and fifteen papers that evaluate against DBA. The reported advantage is rarely measured against a complete trigger delivered by the same attackers, and none of the fifteen evaluations tests whether individual pieces remain effective. We then run 875 paired federated runs that separate adding attackers from splitting the trigger. In our image experiments, adding attackers raised attack success in every seed of all 30 cells where we measured it, by 7.5 to 83.4 percentage points on average. Splitting the trigger among the same attackers had a smaller effect, and its sign depended on the piece layout, the allocation, and the attackers' local training. With DBA's compact layout, splitting lowered attack success on CIFAR-10. A larger penalty on small CNNs vanished once the attackers trained longer, and an FCBA-style allocation gained a few points. Widely separated pieces helped on CIFAR-10, its grayscale version, and GTSRB. No model required all pieces. Neural Cleanse suppressed single pieces together with the full trigger, but split backdoors with separated pieces survived it better than complete ones. We derive reporting requirements for attack and defense evaluations.
tldr: A systematization-of-knowledge study that disentangles the claimed advantages of distributed (split-trigger) backdoor attacks in federated learning by separating the effect of adding more attackers from that of splitting the trigger.
motivation: The literature since DBA has widely assumed that splitting a backdoor trigger across multiple federated clients yields stronger, stealthier, and more persistent attacks, but this belief is rarely tested against a proper baseline where the same attackers hold the complete trigger.
method: The authors code nineteen primary studies and fifteen evaluation papers, then run 875 paired federated learning experiments that independently vary the number of attackers and the trigger-splitting layout across image datasets (CIFAR-10, grayscale CIFAR-10, GTSRB) and defenses such as Neural Cleanse.
result: Adding attackers consistently raised attack success by 7.5-83.4 percentage points, whereas splitting the trigger had a smaller and layout-dependent effect that could even reduce success on CIFAR-10 with DBA's compact layout; widely separated pieces helped, no model required all pieces, and split backdoors with separated pieces survived Neural Cleanse better.
conclusion: The reported superiority of distributed backdoor attacks is largely attributable to the number of attackers rather than trigger splitting itself, motivating explicit reporting requirements for future attack and defense evaluations.

title: Mechanism Design Under Belief Disagreement: Allocation Flexibility And Rent Capacity
authors: Ce Zhang Lijian Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A seller jointly chooses allocation and payments when buyers misperceive competition. Under independent private values, statewise participation, and payment restrictions, allocation determines both required rents and their delivery capacity. We separate these effects under a common subjective law. For three values and shared-top beliefs, explicit score and capacity conditions characterize globally optimal lower-value lotteries, including top-rent overflow and welfare differences among revenue optima. A two-buyer construction establishes a strict allocation advantage over every reserve under the same fixed reporting certificate and positive margin. A transport test and exact band-boundary incentive equalities identify separate conditions restoring objective-law revenue ceilings. For three bands and a common affine belief interval, an explicitly certified reserve attains the ceiling under stated score conditions. A case scaled to public collectible-auction records yields a nominal shared-top allocation gain of 24.72 cents per auction. A one-cent report-by-report margin yields matched gains of 1.48 cents under projection and 3.32 cents under shared-top beliefs; the three-band point-belief gain of 2.50 cents disappears with common-interval protection. These comparisons bound the additional recurring costs an allocation redesign can cover at the specified reporting requirement.
tldr: The paper studies mechanism design when buyers hold subjective beliefs that differ from the seller's objective law, showing how allocation choices determine rent requirements and rent-delivery capacity.
motivation: The authors aim to understand optimal selling mechanisms when buyers misperceive competition, a setting relevant to auction design under belief disagreement rather than standard common-prior assumptions.
method: The analysis separates allocation effects on required rents from effects on rent capacity under a common subjective law, deriving score and capacity conditions for optimal lower-value lotteries and constructing two-buyer examples.
result: It characterizes globally optimal lotteries for three values, establishes a strict allocation advantage over reserves, identifies conditions restoring objective-law revenue ceilings, and quantifies small nominal gains in a collectible-auction calibration.
conclusion: Allocation flexibility can improve revenue under belief disagreement, but the gains are bounded by reporting requirements and belief specifications, with common-interval protection eliminating some point-belief advantages.

title: Who Is Prompt-Injecting Coding Agents? An Empirical Study Of Hidden AI-Directed Text On GitHub
authors: Zvika Babo Gabi Nakibly
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI coding agents now triage issues, review pull requests and pick up tasks inside GitHub repositories, and to do so they read text that anyone with a GitHub account can write. This makes GitHub a prime surface for indirect prompt injection, in which instructions embedded in untrusted content steer a model that later processes it. Prior work has demonstrated such attacks against agents on GitHub in controlled settings, but how often they occur in practice, who deploys them, and for what purpose remain unknown. We present the first large-scale empirical study of AI-directed hidden text on GitHub. We analyzed roughly 145 million issues, pull requests, comments and README files, detected text that GitHub does not render to a human reader but that an agent receives in full, and filtered it with a two-stage LLM classification, a template provenance check and an exhaustive manual review. We identify 2,281 validated findings in issues, pull requests and comments (16 per million items), and AI-directed hidden text in the READMEs of 107 repositories. We find a heterogeneous ecosystem of four uses: attacks on other parties' agents, defensive text that restricts agents, content override that steers what they write, and first-party orchestration, in which projects coordinate their own agents through hidden markers. Attacks are rare (about one in 3.3 million items) but aimed at maintainers' own triage, review and CI agents. Orchestration accounts for two thirds of the findings in issues, pull requests and comments, grew fivefold in four months, and forms a control channel that anyone who can comment can imitate. Replayed offline against five models we tested, the attacks succeed against one small, fast model in 19% of cases, and against none once HTML comments are stripped. We release our detection tool and every finding.
tldr: A large-scale empirical study of hidden AI-directed text (indirect prompt injection) embedded in GitHub issues, pull requests, comments, and READMEs that targets AI coding agents.
motivation: AI coding agents now read untrusted GitHub content, making the platform a prime surface for indirect prompt injection, yet the real-world prevalence, actors, and purposes of such hidden text were unknown.
method: The authors analyzed roughly 145 million GitHub items, detected text invisible to human readers but visible to agents (e.g., HTML comments, hidden markdown), and filtered candidates via two-stage LLM classification, template provenance checks, and exhaustive manual review; attacks were replayed offline against five models.
result: They validated 2,281 findings in issues/PRs/comments (16 per million items) and hidden AI-directed text in 107 repository READMEs, spanning four use categories: attacks, defensive text, content override, and first-party orchestration; attacks are rare (~1 in 3.3 million) but orchestration dominates and grew fivefold in four months, and attacks succeeded against one small model 19% of the time, failing entirely once HTML comments were stripped.
conclusion: Hidden AI-directed text on GitHub forms a heterogeneous, fast-growing control channel that anyone who can comment can imitate, motivating defensive stripping of invisible content and continued monitoring of agent-directed prompt injection.

title: MM-Open5x: Practical Conformal Electronics Via Multi-Material Multi-Axis Additive Manufacturing
authors: Iv\'an Revenga Riesco, Freddie Hong, Borut Lampret, Connor Myant, David Boyle
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28772v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-axis, multi-material additive manufacturing enables the production of conformal electronic systems that are difficult to realise using planar processes and can offer enhanced performance; however, accessibility and reproducibility remain challenging. This paper presents MM-Open5x, an open and low-cost multi-material, multi-axis additive manufacturing workflow for practical conformal electronics. The workflow spans design, simulation, toolpath generation, fabrication, testing, and assembly, and is released alongside complete design files, toolpaths, and representative G-code. Representative case studies demonstrate both the benefits and limitations of multi-axis deposition in practice, explicitly documenting common failure modes, calibration sensitivities, assembly bottlenecks, and material variability. Rather than prescribing an optimal solution, MM-Open5x is presented as a transparent, reproducible foundation upon which a broader community can iterate, extend, and apply conformal electronics workflows across diverse application domains.
tldr: MM-Open5x presents an open-source, low-cost multi-material multi-axis additive manufacturing workflow for fabricating conformal electronics, released with design files, toolpaths, and G-code.
motivation: Conformal electronic systems made via multi-axis multi-material printing offer performance advantages over planar processes, but accessibility and reproducibility of such workflows remain limited.
method: The authors develop an end-to-end workflow covering design, simulation, toolpath generation, fabrication, testing, and assembly, and demonstrate it through representative case studies while documenting failure modes, calibration sensitivities, and material variability.
result: The case studies illustrate both benefits and practical limitations of multi-axis deposition, highlighting assembly bottlenecks and reproducibility challenges alongside the released open resources.
conclusion: MM-Open5x is offered not as an optimal solution but as a transparent, reproducible foundation for the community to iterate on and extend conformal electronics workflows.

title: Ads For Agents: Measuring Ad-Serving Mcp Servers
authors: Shahrooz Pouryousef, Sohini Chakraborty, Ali Montazer, Muoi Tran
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents call external tools through protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Some MCP servers return paid advertisements (ads) into the model's context. The model then decides whether these ads and their disclosures reach the user. We trace these ads from their sources to the agent's tool results across public MCP servers and packages. We find the servers through their public traces in ad networks, package registries, certificate logs, hostnames, MCP directories, and GitHub configurations. We then query the ad-serving servers with read-only requests and inspect their ad links. Ads appear on only 0.57% of 101,363 open MCP endpoints and 0.04% of 122,656 local MCP packages. Although 173 ad networks target agents, operators insert the ads themselves on about half of the 226 ad-returning servers. Nearly all ad-serving packages likewise carry the operator's own affiliate identifier. While ads adapt to the topic and intent of the query, their disclosure stays fixed within each tool. Only 9.3% of the ads carry an explicit sponsored label. Most ad links also hide their destinations. Since operators insert most ads themselves and label them inconsistently, we propose a per-item ad annotation in MCP results. Clients can show this annotation to the user independently of the model's answer.
tldr: A measurement study of paid advertisements injected into AI agent contexts by public MCP servers and packages, proposing per-item ad annotation in tool results.
motivation: AI agents increasingly call external tools via the Model Context Protocol, and some servers return paid ads into the model's context, letting the model decide whether ads and disclosures reach the user—an unexamined transparency risk.
method: The authors trace ads from sources to agent tool results by discovering servers through ad-network traces, package registries, certificate logs, hostnames, MCP directories, and GitHub configurations, then querying ad-serving servers with read-only requests and inspecting ad links across 101,363 open MCP endpoints and 122,656 local packages.
result: Ads appear on only 0.57% of open MCP endpoints and 0.04% of local packages; 173 ad networks target agents but operators insert ads themselves on about half of 226 ad-returning servers, only 9.3% of ads carry an explicit sponsored label, and most ad links obscure their destinations.
conclusion: Because operators self-insert most ads and label them inconsistently, the authors propose a per-item ad annotation in MCP results that clients can display independently of the model's answer.

title: Correspondence Between Orbit Equivalences And Exact Symplectomorphisms For Anosov Flows
authors: Agustin Moreno
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that for a closed hyperbolic [MATH]-manifold, two Anosov flows are orbital equivalent if and only if the corresponding Anosov Liouville structures are exact symplectomorphic.
tldr: The paper proves that for closed hyperbolic 3-manifolds, orbital equivalence of Anosov flows is equivalent to exact symplectomorphism of the associated Anosov Liouville structures.
motivation: Anosov flows and their orbital equivalence are central in hyperbolic dynamics, while Anosov Liouville structures provide a symplectic-geometric framework; the paper aims to connect these two classifications.
method: The author uses techniques from hyperbolic dynamics and symplectic geometry to establish a correspondence between orbit equivalence classes of Anosov flows and exact symplectomorphism classes of Anosov Liouville structures.
result: For a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold, two Anosov flows are orbitally equivalent if and only if their Anosov Liouville structures are exact symplectomorphic.
conclusion: This gives a geometric characterization of orbital equivalence for Anosov flows via exact symplectomorphisms, linking dynamical and symplectic classification problems.

title: Generalized Fundamental Theorem Of Calculus On A Regular Time Scale
authors: Billur Kaymak\c{c}alan, Yeter \c{s}ahiner, \c{s}eyda Y{\i}ld{\i}z, Emre Deniz Y{\i}lmaz
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The main objectives of this paper can be summarized as, giving a fundamental theorem on a regular time scale as well as illustrating that applications are possible on a homogeneous time scale.
tldr: The paper establishes a fundamental theorem of calculus on regular time scales and shows how it can be applied on homogeneous time scales.
motivation: Time scale calculus unifies discrete and continuous analysis, and a general fundamental theorem on regular time scales would extend the available toolbox for dynamic equations.
method: Purely mathematical derivation: properties of regular and homogeneous time scales are used to formulate and prove a generalized fundamental theorem of calculus.
result: A fundamental theorem is obtained for regular time scales, with examples illustrating applications in the homogeneous case.
conclusion: The result extends classical calculus identities to a broader class of time scales, but remains a pure analysis result with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Generalized Framework For Structured Low-Rank Approximation And Completion
authors: Rishav Chakraborty, A. Sanand Amita Dilip, Swanand R. Khare
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate a generalized version of SLRA, consisting of general affine constraints, which subsumes the problems of structured low-rank matrix approximation and completion as special cases. We characterize its critical points and propose an algorithm to approximately solve the general problem. Finally, we demonstrate the performance of the proposed algorithm for stock-price forecasting, computing approximate gcd of polynomials with noisy coefficients, and time-series denoising.
tldr: The paper proposes a generalized structured low-rank approximation framework with affine constraints, characterizes critical points, and gives an approximate algorithm demonstrated on forecasting, polynomial GCD, and denoising.
motivation: Structured low-rank approximation and completion are important matrix-analysis problems, and the authors aim to unify them under a broader affine-constrained formulation.
method: They formulate a generalized SLRA problem with general affine constraints, characterize its critical points, and propose an algorithm to approximately solve it.
result: The algorithm is demonstrated on stock-price forecasting, approximate GCD computation for noisy polynomials, and time-series denoising.
conclusion: The framework generalizes structured low-rank approximation/completion and shows practical utility in several signal-processing and numerical applications.

title: Jointly Recovering Destination Attractiveness And Spatial Preference Segments From Observed Tours Via Inverse Optimization
authors: Yudai Honma Hiroyuki Hasada
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantifying destination attractiveness by counting visitors, the most direct approach, can favor accessible sites and understate destinations that travelers reach at considerable cost. Preferences may also cut across a priori socio-demographic groupings. This study develops an inverse optimization framework that recovers destination attractiveness and preference segments jointly from observed multi-stop trip tours and generalized travel costs, without prespecifying tour-level segment assignments or imposing a parametric distribution on the unexplained part of utility. Representing each destination visit as a link in an extended network turns utility-maximizing tour choice into an inverse shortest paths problem. We apply the framework to 2,931 holiday vehicle trip tours over 51 target municipalities in Hokkaido, Japan. Constraint generation and alternating optimization make estimation tractable in this multi-destination setting, and the segments recovered under a three-segment specification show contrasting spatial preferences across the established coastal centers, the corridor around Sapporo, and the inland lake districts. The recovered values are expressed on a common monetary scale across destinations and segments without segment-specific scale normalization. They are uncorrelated with visit counts in the input data (r = -0.01) yet moderately correlated with tourist arrivals from an independent prefectural survey (r = 0.40), and are positively associated with the cost of reaching a destination (r = 0.60); destinations above this cost-value relationship include niche places that visit counts alone do not distinguish. The results provide a spatially explicit account of destination value and preference heterogeneity that can inform urban and regional planning and segment-targeted marketing.
tldr: An inverse optimization framework recovers destination attractiveness and traveler preference segments jointly from observed multi-stop holiday tours in Hokkaido, Japan.
motivation: Counting visitors understates destinations that require substantial travel cost to reach, and preferences may cut across socio-demographic groupings, so a cost-aware, segmentation-free estimation is needed.
method: Each destination visit is represented as a link in an extended network, turning utility-maximizing tour choice into an inverse shortest-path problem solved via constraint generation and alternating optimization.
result: Estimated values are uncorrelated with raw visit counts (r = -0.01), moderately correlated with independent survey arrivals (r = 0.40), and positively associated with access cost (r = 0.60); three segments show contrasting spatial preferences.
conclusion: The approach yields a spatially explicit account of destination value and preference heterogeneity useful for regional planning and segment-targeted marketing.

title: Strictness Of The Containment Of Kirk's Asymptotic Contractions In A Class Defined By Two Quasi-metrics
authors: Jie Shi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kirk's asymptotic contractions are defined by moduli [MATH] which converge uniformly on [MATH] to a Boyd--Wong function and are evaluated at the distance [MATH] only. A relaxed class, in which the estimate involves a lower and an upper quasi-metric built from the four distances [MATH], [MATH], [MATH] and [MATH], was recently shown to contain Kirk's class and to admit the same fixed point conclusion. It was left open whether the containment is strict. We prove that it is. The separating maps form a family of radial damping maps [MATH] on a normed space, where [MATH] is continuous, [MATH], nonconstant and periodic: every such map is a relaxed asymptotic contraction with explicit linear moduli, whereas its one-step dispersion at a fixed distance is unbounded, so that no finite Kirk modulus exists. A slowly modulated nonperiodic damping law is treated as well. We further show that strictness can occur only when the image [MATH] is not relatively compact: in a complete space, if [MATH] is relatively compact, the two classes coincide, hence on a compact (in particular finite) space no separating example exists. Applications to semi-active vibration isolation with amplitude-dependent damping and to digital maturity gaps in the digital transformation of small and medium-sized enterprises are discussed, and numerical illustrations are provided.
tldr: The paper proves that the class of relaxed asymptotic contractions defined via lower and upper quasi-metrics strictly contains Kirk's asymptotic contractions, with separating examples built from periodic radial damping maps.
motivation: Kirk's asymptotic contractions use moduli evaluated only at a single distance, and a recently introduced relaxed class using two quasi-metrics was known to contain Kirk's class and admit the same fixed point conclusion, but strictness of the containment was left open.
method: Constructive counterexamples: continuous, nonconstant, periodic radial damping maps on a normed space whose one-step dispersion at fixed distance is unbounded, hence admit no finite Kirk modulus, but which satisfy explicit linear relaxed moduli; plus a nonperiodic slowly modulated damping law and a compactness characterization.
result: The containment is strict; moreover strictness requires the image not be relatively compact, so in complete spaces with relatively compact image the two classes coincide and no separating example exists on compact or finite spaces.
conclusion: The relaxed quasi-metric framework is genuinely more general than Kirk's, with the dichotomy governed by relative compactness; applications to semi-active vibration isolation and SME digital maturity gaps are sketched.

title: Finite-difference Neural Policy Iteration For High-dimensional Degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi Equations
authors: Yeoneung Kim Hee Jun Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a finite-difference neural policy iteration method for high-dimensional degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and Isaacs equations. Artificial viscosity yields a monotone finite-difference operator, and neural networks approximate the linear equations of semi-discrete policy iteration using local stencil values. This avoids global tensor-grid storage. For measurable feedbacks, we bound the propagation of evaluation, terminal, gradient, and control optimization errors by a geometrically weighted sum. Discrete comparison, consistency, and vanishing viscosity relate the approximation to the original degenerate equation. On coupled manufactured problems with rank-deficient diffusion, the method achieves lower mean errors than direct physics-informed neural networks at every tested dimension from five to fifty under equal training time. At fifty dimensions and [MATH] seconds, the mean relative [MATH] error over three paired seeds is about [MATH] lower. Two-dimensional refinement attains [MATH] error against the original degenerate solution, with independent grid references separating approximation error from viscosity bias. In a twenty-dimensional game with finite control sets, reusing policies reduces the measured time to a relative error of [MATH] by [MATH] compared with direct minimization of the same discrete residual with fresh samples at every update.
tldr: The paper introduces a finite-difference neural policy iteration scheme for solving high-dimensional degenerate Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman and Isaacs equations without global tensor-grid storage.
motivation: High-dimensional degenerate HJB/Isaacs equations suffer from the curse of dimensionality, and physics-informed neural networks often yield poor accuracy, so a more stable and accurate numerical scheme is needed.
method: Artificial viscosity is used to build a monotone finite-difference operator, and neural networks approximate the linear semi-discrete policy-iteration equations using local stencil values; error propagation is bounded by a geometrically weighted sum.
result: On coupled manufactured problems with rank-deficient diffusion, the method achieves lower mean errors than direct PINNs across dimensions five to fifty, with roughly an order-of-magnitude improvement at fifty dimensions, and policy reuse substantially cuts time to a given relative error.
conclusion: The approach provides a provably consistent, vanishing-viscosity-justified approximation for degenerate HJB/Isaacs equations and outperforms direct residual minimization in high dimensions.

title: Interface-aware Dynamic Mode Decomposition With Control For Partitioned Multiphysics Systems
authors: Jiarui Tian, Dunhui Xiao, Lei Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an interface-aware dynamic mode decomposition with control (DMDc) formulation for multiphysics systems, within an optimization-based partitioned coupling framework. The finite-element interface-input operator is projected onto the reduced space and kept fixed during identification, while the unknown state-dependent local dynamics are learned from trajectory data. The common interface control is recomputed online by minimizing the mismatch between the reconstructed physical interface quantities. The formulation accommodates local subproblems governed by ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and differential--algebraic equations (DAEs). For a DAE subproblem, tangent projection identifies the state dynamics, whereas a residualized normal regression identifies the pressure balance and provides an algebraic pressure reconstruction. We further propose regularized quadratic correction DMDc to enrich the tangent dynamics and, for DAEs, the normal pressure balance through jointly fitted linear and compact quadratic operators. Feature normalization and block-dependent regularization control the enlarged regression while retaining the prescribed interface operators and identified DAE geometry. The proposed framework is evaluated on problems involving both ODE--ODE and DAE--ODE couplings. The numerical results demonstrate accurate predictions and stable long-time behavior.
tldr: The paper develops an interface-aware dynamic mode decomposition with control (DMDc) for partitioned multiphysics systems coupling ODE and DAE subproblems.
motivation: Reduced-order modeling of coupled multiphysics systems requires respecting interface physics and coupling constraints, which standard DMDc does not handle well.
method: The finite-element interface-input operator is projected onto the reduced space and held fixed while state-dependent local dynamics are learned from trajectory data; interface control is recomputed online by minimizing reconstructed interface mismatch, using tangent projection for DAE state dynamics and residualized normal regression for pressure balance, plus a regularized quadratic correction DMDc.
result: Numerical experiments on ODE–ODE and DAE–ODE coupled problems show accurate predictions and stable long-time behavior.
conclusion: The interface-aware DMDc framework provides a practical reduced-order modeling approach for partitioned multiphysics systems with algebraic constraints.

title: Development Of An Effective Federated Learning-Based Defense System Against Phishing Attacks On Mobile Platforms
authors: Eren Dogan, Busra Buyuktanir, Gozde Karatas Baydogmus, Kazim Yildiz
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phishing remains one of the most pervasive and damaging cyber threats, exploiting both technical flaws and human behavior to compromise sensitive data. We present a privacy-preserving, real-time defense that analyzes full webpage source code on mobile platforms. Our system combines a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for end-to-end feature extraction with a Federated Learning (FL) framework that updates models collaboratively on user devices without transferring raw data-supporting regulatory compliance and personalization. Evaluated on a large and diverse dataset, the model attains 86.02\% accuracy, 90.35\% precision, 80.64\% recall, and 92.78\% ROC-AUC. While some centralized, classical approaches may report higher accuracy, our design emphasizes a practical balance among accuracy, user privacy, and real-time performance on resource-constrained devices. We further demonstrate an end-to-end integration within the open-source Lightning Android browser, achieving real-time detection with low computational overhead. This work shows that privacy-first, AI-driven phishing detection is both feasible and scalable across mobile and IoT settings, delivering robust protection while keeping user data on-device.
tldr: The paper presents a privacy-preserving federated learning system with a lightweight CNN for real-time phishing detection on mobile platforms, integrated into an Android browser.
motivation: Phishing is a pervasive mobile cybersecurity threat, and centralized detection approaches raise privacy concerns and may be impractical for resource-constrained devices.
method: The authors combine a lightweight CNN for webpage source-code feature extraction with federated learning to train collaboratively across user devices without transferring raw data, and integrate the detector into the Lightning Android browser.
result: The system achieves 86.02% accuracy, 90.35% precision, 80.64% recall, and 92.78% ROC-AUC while maintaining low computational overhead for real-time mobile detection.
conclusion: Privacy-first AI-driven phishing detection is feasible and scalable for mobile and IoT settings, though the work is outside quantum information science and related research directions.

title: Analytical Modeling And Optimal Gpu Provisioning For Disaggregated Llm Inference
authors: Akshat Pandey, Dominic Cheng, Sidharth Sharma, Ashwin Gumaste
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28760v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present OSplit, an exact analytical method that enables efficient partitioning of a GPU L1 domain into prefill and decode workers, including sharding for classical and advanced GPUs. OSplit takes into consideration model parameters, enabling any inference model to be partitioned into prefill and decode workers with a goal of producing the maximum throughput possible. OSplit is based on a capacity model that takes as inputs the model, the loading scheme (batch size, max sequence length), and models an inference serving framework (vLLM) and computes the efficiency of each GPU. For this, we model H100 and GB300 GPUs, and model a scale-up domain, along with FlashAttention-based kernels. OSplit first computes an optimal collective generation policy, which gives inputs to the capacity model that enables optimal split of prefill and decode GPUs. We evaluate our scheme over H100 (NVL8) and GB300 (NVL72) using vLLM inference serving and show throughput, predicted and measured latency, showing near-perfect theoretical-to-measured values over leading LLMs (Llama and Qwen).
tldr: OSplit is an analytical capacity model that optimally partitions a GPU domain into prefill and decode workers for LLM inference to maximize throughput.
motivation: Disaggregated LLM inference on modern GPU clusters requires deciding how many GPUs to allocate to prefill versus decode, a choice usually made heuristically; an exact analytical method would remove guesswork.
method: The authors build a capacity model parameterized by model architecture, batching scheme, sequence length, vLLM serving behavior, and FlashAttention kernels, and use it to derive an optimal collective generation policy and the corresponding optimal prefill/decode GPU split.
result: Evaluated on H100 NVL8 and GB300 NVL72 with Llama and Qwen models, the model's predicted throughput and latency closely match measurements, indicating near-perfect theoretical-to-measured agreement.
conclusion: Analytical modeling can guide GPU provisioning for disaggregated LLM serving with high accuracy, though the work is an ML systems/infrastructure contribution with no quantum information, thermodynamics, network, or hybrid-system component.

title: ActWithin: Bounding Wrong-Payment Risk In Delegated Payment Batches
authors: Shuhao Zheng, Zhipeng Wang, Zi Xuan Zhang, Yang Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A delegated payment agent can hold valid rights for incompatible revisions of a batch. We study the window in which the selected revision cannot be verified by the execution deadline. For batches that permit every subset of up to q revisions, ActWithin compiles the limit into a shared quota of q successful replacement payments. If approved plans are mutually replayable with the same observable inputs, deadlines, and resources, this quota preserves normal completion without additional approvals and minimizes worst-case wrong-payment principal for arbitrary positive amounts. A dynamic program computes its exact risk and witness. For amount-preserving recipient changes, we derive the exact risk of the tightest single amount cap on the same replacement group, provided mixed payment subsets can settle within the window. A two-phase result isolates the risk to payments due before trusted verification. Against the amount cap, an exploratory setting with 16-64 payments and one quarter of positions revisable yields aggregate reductions of 16.23-16.88% on adapted IBM AMLSim amounts and 10.12-12.52% on an adapted controlled catalog. The 760 funded original controlled paths with constructed single-position revisions yield 2.69%. In one local MetaMask fixture, both policies complete all 37 normal plans and the worst wrong debit falls from 93,962 to 81,056 test wei.
tldr: This paper studies wrong-payment risk in delegated payment batches and proposes ActWithin, a quota-based mechanism to bound worst-case principal when batch revisions cannot be verified before execution.
motivation: Delegated payment agents may hold valid rights for incompatible batch revisions, creating a window where a selected revision cannot be trusted before the execution deadline.
method: The authors formalize worst-case wrong-payment risk for batches allowing up to q revisions, compile the limit into a shared quota of q replacement payments, and use dynamic programming to compute exact risk and witnesses; they also analyze a tight single amount cap for amount-preserving recipient changes.
result: The quota minimizes worst-case wrong-payment principal for arbitrary positive amounts, and exploratory evaluations show aggregate risk reductions against an amount cap across adapted AMLSim and controlled catalog settings, with a MetaMask fixture preserving all normal plans.
conclusion: ActWithin provides a risk-bounding mechanism for delegated payment batches, though the work is entirely about payment-system security and has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Stackelberg Games With Convex Risk Measures
authors: Arunesh Sinha
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stackelberg games have important real-world applications in which reliable commitments require accounting for multiple sources of uncertainty. We study finite Stackelberg games in which environmental uncertainty makes each mixed strategy profile induce a random reward, and each player evaluates that reward with a convex monetary risk criterion. In reward form, it is a concave, monotone, translation-equivariant utility and also represented as penalized expected reward over distributions of environmental outcomes. We provide two conditions under which the follower has a unique continuous mixed response, which leads to inducible optimistic equilibrium. We show that even approximate equilibrium computation is NP Hard. We then derive an exact mathematical program with equilibrium constraints for the problem. We also develop an action entropy smoothed implicit-gradient method and prove an end-to-end additive approximation guarantee under the assumption that the gradient method reaches global optimality. We validate our scalability and other results with experiments on synthetic and real data.
tldr: The paper studies finite Stackelberg games where players evaluate random rewards using convex monetary risk measures and provides equilibrium existence, hardness, and approximation results.
motivation: Stackelberg games with environmental uncertainty require reliable commitments, motivating risk-sensitive models rather than expected-reward optimization.
method: The authors characterize follower responses under convex risk criteria, derive an exact mathematical program with equilibrium constraints, and propose an action-entropy smoothed implicit-gradient method.
result: They identify conditions for a unique continuous follower response and inducible optimistic equilibrium, show approximate equilibrium computation is NP-hard, and prove an additive approximation guarantee under a global-optimality assumption.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical and algorithmic framework for risk-sensitive Stackelberg games, supported by synthetic and real-data experiments.

title: Consumer-Time Validity In Stateful Ai Runtimes: Verifying Recovered State And Deferred Authority
authors: Guijia Zhang, Huihao Jing, Bing Li, Shing-Chi Cheung, Harry Yang, Ziqi Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.29004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stateful LLM serving engines and agent runtimes reuse execution state and deferred permissions across components and sessions. A cancellation, rollback, or approval is recorded by one component and relied on by another, and recording it does not make the later use valid: a downstream consumer may read state or dispatch an action whose identity, production status, allocation, or target revision has since changed. We call the missing check consumer-time validity and separate two forms. State validity governs what a consumer reads. On vLLM with LMCache, an interrupted KV load leaves unwritten blocks indexed, and a host-only counter rewind desynchronizes the GPU position, so a second tenant generates a schema-valid tool call naming the wrong tenant in 10/10 native-fault runs; the call is recorded and not executed. Authority freshness governs what a consumer executes: on a multi-session approval runtime, an unrevoked deferred grant overwrote a newer revision in one admitted live execution. Output equality cannot test state validity: a fault-free run diverges at token 30 through BF16 batching alone while attended-KV digests match. We therefore specify consumer-bound recovery contracts that, for state recovery, jointly require exclusion, retention, and task completion, and an admissible-witness standard realized as a GPU-free offline trace verifier over scheduler metadata and persisted tool artifacts. On recorded traces the verifier agrees with the reference verdicts in 42/42 frozen GPU-matrix scenarios. An allocation-aware repair satisfies 7/7 triggered vLLM fault predicates on a pinned scheduler-case matrix, where upstream PR 61769 satisfies 2/7, and revision-bound dispatch blocks all 160 deterministic conflicting overwrites in a separate dispatcher cohort. Recovery must be checked where state and authority are consumed, with evidence bound to the consuming request.
tldr: The paper introduces 'consumer-time validity' for stateful LLM serving and agent runtimes, distinguishing state validity (what a consumer reads, e.g., interrupted KV cache loads in vLLM/LMCache) from authority freshness (what a consumer executes, e.g., stale deferred approvals), and proposes consumer-bound recovery contracts plus a GPU-free offline trace verifier.
motivation: Stateful LLM serving engines and agent runtimes reuse execution state and deferred permissions across components and sessions, so a cancellation, rollback, or approval recorded by one component can be relied on by another after its identity, status, allocation, or target revision has changed.
method: The authors demonstrate concrete fault scenarios in vLLM with LMCache (indexed-unwritten KV blocks, host-only counter rewinds) and multi-session approval runtimes, then specify recovery contracts requiring exclusion, retention, and task completion, realized as an admissible-witness standard implemented as an offline trace verifier over scheduler metadata and persisted tool artifacts.
result: The verifier matches reference verdicts on 42/42 frozen GPU-matrix scenarios, an allocation-aware repair satisfies 7/7 triggered vLLM fault predicates versus 2/7 for upstream PR 61769, and revision-bound dispatch blocks all 160 deterministic conflicting overwrites; output equality alone fails as a test since BF16 batching diverges at token 30 even with matching attended-KV digests.
conclusion: Recovery correctness must be checked at the point where state and authority are consumed, with evidence bound to the consuming request rather than to the recording component.

title: HiPerfCC-StateReuse: Ciphertext Reuse For Fast Confidential Gpu Data Movement
authors: Haoxuan Xu, Shaoyu Wang, Minghao Lin, Beijie Liu, Potung Yu, Yongqin Wang, Vincent Quentin Ulitzsch, Seo Jin Park, Murali Annavaram, Mengyuan Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.29067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Confidential GPUs offer near-native on-device compute performance, but transfers between CPU and GPU TEEs through untrusted host memory require bulk CPU encryption and decryption, even for unchanged data. Existing software techniques overlap or parallelize these operations but retain their per-byte CPU cost. Reusing exported ciphertext could avoid this work, but GPU TEE firmware enforces direction-specific encryption keys and fresh per-transfer initialization vectors (IVs), preventing direct reuse. We introduce ciphertext rebinding, a purely software primitive enabling repeated and cross-GPU ciphertext reuse on existing GPU TEEs without hardware changes, while preserving confidentiality, integrity, and freshness. Specifically, ciphertext rebinding exploits the separation between ciphertext-dependent and IV-dependent components in GPU TEE's AES-GCM authentication: a GPU-precomputed summary under the destination key can enable the CPU to update authentication tags without processing the payload. With this modification, GPU's subsequent read on the retained ciphertext can still proceed through the GPU's hardware-fixed copy-engine interfaces, which cannot be modified by software. An additional GPU correction step can then compensate for differences in the keys and IVs to recover the original plaintext. By retaining GPU-exported ciphertext in untrusted host memory, ciphertext rebinding avoids bulk CPU decryption and re-encryption, improving effective bandwidth for GPU-state restoration and sharing. We implement this primitive in HiPerfCC-StateReuse through only driver and library changes, combining batched submissions with pipelined GPU processing and copy-engine transfers. We evaluate transfer efficiency and CPU overhead through microbenchmarks, and application performance through three case studies: model switching, key-value cache offloading, and cross-instance cache sharing.
tldr: The paper introduces ciphertext rebinding, a software-only primitive that enables reuse of GPU-exported ciphertext for confidential CPU-GPU data movement, avoiding bulk CPU decryption and re-encryption.
motivation: Confidential GPUs require CPU-mediated encryption/decryption for transfers through untrusted host memory, imposing per-byte CPU overhead even for unchanged data; existing methods only overlap this cost rather than eliminate it.
method: The authors exploit AES-GCM's separation of ciphertext-dependent and IV-dependent authentication components so the CPU can update tags under a destination key without processing payloads, combined with GPU correction steps and pipelined copy-engine transfers.
result: Implemented in HiPerfCC-StateReuse via driver and library changes, the approach improves effective bandwidth for GPU-state restoration and sharing, evaluated with microbenchmarks and case studies on model switching, KV-cache offloading, and cross-instance cache sharing.
conclusion: Ciphertext rebinding enables repeated and cross-GPU ciphertext reuse on existing GPU TEEs without hardware changes while preserving confidentiality, integrity, and freshness.

title: Measure-class Classification Of Achievable Cantorvals
authors: Hanyu Dong
abstract: ArXiv:2611.28162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An achievable Cantorval is a Cantorval that is the set of subsums of a convergent series of positive terms. We construct an explicit achievable Cantorval whose boundary has Lebesgue measure at least [MATH]. This answers a question of G{\l}{}b and Prus-Wi{\'s}niowski and gives a counterexample to the conjecture of Nowakowski and Prus-Wi{\'s}niowski that every achievable Cantorval is standard. The example is generated by a hybrid series of Pratsiovytyi, Vynnyshyn and Vynnyshyn. The lower bound comes from an isolated-digit criterion, which produces a Cantor subset of the boundary whose measure is an explicit infinite product; after rescaling, the boundary measure can be made arbitrarily close to [MATH]. We also prove that the boundary of every achievement set is either Lebesgue null or has positive measure near each of its points. Consequently, up to homeomorphisms that preserve Lebesgue null sets in both directions, there are exactly two achievable Cantorvals, distinguished by whether the boundary is null. For boundaries of positive measure, the homeomorphism can be chosen so that it changes the normalized boundary measure of every Borel set by a factor arbitrarily close to [MATH]. For general Cantorvals we classify the case of a relatively clopen boundary support and show that further invariants appear beyond this case. Finally, the null-set preserving self-homeomorphisms of a Cantorval always form a meager subgroup of its homeomorphism group. This subgroup is dense exactly when the support of Lebesgue measure on the boundary is empty or the whole boundary; in particular, it is dense for every achievable Cantorval.
tldr: The paper classifies achievable Cantorvals—sets of subsums of convergent positive series—up to Lebesgue-null-preserving homeomorphisms and constructs an explicit nonstandard achievable Cantorval with large boundary measure.
motivation: The work addresses a question of Głąb and Prus-Wiśniewski and disproves a conjecture of Nowakowski and Prus-Wiśniewski that every achievable Cantorval is standard.
method: It constructs a hybrid series due to Pratsiovytyi, Vynnyshyn and Vynnyshyn, uses an isolated-digit criterion to lower-bound boundary measure via an explicit infinite product, and analyzes boundary supports and measure-class invariants under homeomorphisms.
result: The constructed Cantorval has boundary Lebesgue measure arbitrarily close to the whole interval after rescaling, and every achievement-set boundary is either null or has positive measure near each point; up to null-set-preserving homeomorphisms there are exactly two achievable Cantorvals.
conclusion: The classification shows that positive-measure boundaries occur and that null-set-preserving homeomorphisms can adjust normalized boundary measure by factors arbitrarily close to one; the subgroup of null-set-preserving self-homeomorphisms is meager but often dense.
